+## 2026-10-22 「拆分确定性」被路径写法击穿（同一张卡拆出 8 与 12 个单元）
+
+现象：`claim-pack.ts` 按 claim 的 `定位` / `判据` token 聚簇。同一张 review 卡、同一批 23 条 claim，
+直接调组合器得 `units=8`，经门禁（`acIndex` 值拼成 `.agenticdoc/<key>/spec.md:42`）得 `units=12`。
+聚簇输入里只要混进一种路径拼法，拆法就不可复现 —— 而 manifest 的 sha 链正是用来防"事后被改"的，
+拆法本身不稳定会让 sha 链变成摆设。
+
+规避：**任何进入聚簇/去重/关联的路径，先规范成 `basename:line[-end]`**（`canonicalizeLocator`），
+并写一条断言：同一输入用两种路径拼法 → `units` / `ids` / 序列化产物逐字节相同。
+同类风险点：manifest sha（口径必须 EOL 归一化才能与 `card_sha256` 对照）、`acIndex`、
+`read_scope` 锚点（`isSameOrUnder` 同样按字符串比较）。
+
+## 2026-10-22 自动化提取会把「人判清单」原样搬成 claim，制造 0% 机检的假拆分
+
+现象：把真实 QG 卡（`T-QG-evidence-closure`）的 AC 引用提成 claim 后，34 条 claim 全是 `manual`，
+装箱阶段 12/12 单元被判 `split:unit-infeasible:manual-only`，读预算通胀 6.2 倍。
+根因不是实现 bug：`CLAIM_MANUAL_CAP = min(4, ceil(n/3))` 决定"逐条判 N 条 AC"根本无法用 claims 忠实编码。
+
+规避：**claim 驱动只适用于"断言可机检"的评审**（有 `cmd:`/`grep:`/`shape:` 判据）。
+遇到"逐条人判"的审计卡，不要为了凑数把 manual 包装成 `grep:`（结算期被 `tautology`/`judgement` 判掉），
+直接判"不适用"。派生反证条件同理：机器类可派生具体反证，人判类必须上游提供，缺就计数。

 ## 2. 验收标准
 
 **G1 · 确定性拦截**
 - **AC-001** 对含 reparse point 的 worktree 执行 `git worktree remove`（含 `--force`）时，**执行前被 block**，命令未真正运行（以副作用为零证明）。
-- **AC-002** block 的报错文本**包含可直接照抄的正规命令**（G2 形式），且含被检出的链接路径与目标。
+- **AC-002** block 的报错文本**包含可直接照抄的正规命令**（G2 形式），且含被检出的链接路径与目标。扩展（决策 **D-11**，2026-10-13）：对**非 worktree 目标**的穿透形态（`rm -rf <dir>/`、`rm -rf <dir>/*`、`Remove-Item -Recurse <dir>\*`）被拦时，文本给出的是可照抄的 `cmd /c rmdir "<link>"`（无 `/S`）而不是 `mw worktree rm`——后者只适用于已注册 worktree。
 - **AC-003** 对**不含** reparse point 的 worktree，`git worktree remove` **不被误拦**（零副作用放行），并有反向对照。
 
 **G2 · 唯一正规命令 `mw worktree rm <path>`**
 - **AC-004** 六步顺序固定且不可跳步：枚举 → 校验目标在仓库内 → 只摘链 → 复核主树 `node_modules/@earendil-works/*` 链接目标逐条未变 → `git worktree remove --force` → 打印前后对照。
 - **AC-005** 含链 worktree：**只摘链、主树零损伤**（以主树 `node_modules` 与 8 个包的文件清单/哈希前后一致证明）。
-- **AC-006** 链接目标**在仓库外**时**拒绝执行**（fail-closed），且拒绝时不摘任何链。
+- **AC-006**（决策 D-1，2026-10-13 用户确认）链接目标按**三分类**处置：① 目标在 `repo_root` 内 ⇒ 摘链 → 复核 → `remove`；② 目标在**待删 worktree 子树内**（自指链，如 worktree 内 `npm ci` 生成的仓内自举）⇒ 摘链；③ 其它（真正的仓库外）⇒ **fail-closed 拒绝执行**，不摘任何链。
 - **AC-007** 任一步失败 ⇒ **中止并保留现场**，明确输出"未降级继续"；不得部分摘链后继续 remove。
 
 **G3 · 对称命令与巡检**
 - **AC-008** `mw worktree add <path>` 默认**不创建 junction**；显式 `--link-deps` 时才建链，并**登记注册表**（含目标、创建时刻、创建者）。
-- **AC-009** `mw doctor` 报出「遗留的、指向仓库内的 junction」并给出路径；对无遗留的仓库不误报（反向对照，语料锚点 = `%TEMP%\mwvg-t5-probe\node_modules` 曾存在的形态）。
+- **AC-009**（决策 D-2，2026-10-13 用户确认）`mw doctor` 报出「遗留的、指向仓库内的 junction」并给出路径；判定域**默认 = 注册表域 + 仓库内 `node_modules/*` 顶层**（实测 ~2 ms），`%TEMP%` 等全域猎捕走**显式开关**（不做默认）。「遗留」的判据（决策 **D-10**）：① 注册表登记项 —— `link` 仍在而 `worktree` 已不在 ⇒ `leftover`，`link` 已不在 ⇒ `stale-entry`；② 仓内顶层链 —— 目标规范化（**剥 `\\?\` 前缀**）后落在 `repo_root` 内**且不在 `package-lock.json` 的 `"link": true` 期望集内** ⇒ `leftover`（`node_modules/*` 的 workspace 链是**正常态，必须静默**）。对无遗留的仓库不误报：反向对照 = 本仓实测期望集 14 条 = 磁盘 14 条 ⇒ `count==0`、零行输出、rc 不变；语料锚点 = `%TEMP%\mwvg-t5\node_modules` 现存活雷形态，仅在开关开启时可见。域 (c) 额外遵循决策 **D-12**：不报「worktree 仍存活的已登记链」（那是正常态），只报 worktree 已消失或未登记的链。
 
 **G4 · 可观测**
 - **AC-010** 「已跟踪文件数骤降」判据：构造 file-count 骤降（临时仓库）⇒ 触发；正常波动（如单文件编辑）⇒ 不触发。
 - **AC-011** 「junction 目标丢失」判据：构造断链 ⇒ 触发并给出路径；完好链 ⇒ 不触发。
 - **AC-012** 端到端复现：在 `%TEMP%` 内建 worktree + 链 → 走新流程清理 → **主树 mtime 与内容零变化**（机器对照），且全程无 block 误放行。

+## 6. 需规避坑点（前馈）
+
+> 每条都由本阶段实测坐实（证据：`evidence/research/design-*-20261013.md`），实现时**不得**再踩。行号同 §5 的漂移警示。
+
+| # | 坑点 | 规避 |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1 | **行号漂移**：卡/spec 期行号是 2026-10-09 旧修订（`_parse_args` 5324→5603、`doctor_report` 2957→3624、`_doctor_issues` 2780→3401…） | 一律 grep 函数名，不照抄数字；本 key 的证据与 `design.md` 用实测行号 |
+| 2 | **`mw doctor` 注入段永不产生 issue**：`mw.py:522-526` 的注入发生在 `_doctor_issues`（`mw_common.py:3662`）之后 ⇒ 只能 informational、不翻转退出码 | AC-009 挂 `doctor_report` 内部；若确要“只可见”，必须在 design 里显式写明降级 |
+| 3 | **`readdirSync(..., {recursive:true})` 会跟进 junction**（实测返回链接内部条目） | 自建显式栈 + 命中 reparse point 不下钻 |
+| 4 | **`os.walk` 也会下钻 junction**（`followlinks=False` 亦然） | 全仓扫描必须显式剪枝，否则重复遍历 `packages/**`、病态时成环 |
+| 5 | **Node 判不出 junction vs symlink**：`lstatSync` 对 junction 报 `isSymbolicLink()=true`，`Stats` 无 `fileAttributes`/`reparseTag`（实测 `undefined`） | junction 判定与 AC-011 的权威实现放 Python |
+| 6 | **不能用 `git ls-files` 当骤降判据**：它只读索引，磁盘文件被删后计数不变（实测 6→6、5001→5001） | 用 `git ls-files -d`（或 `git status --porcelain` 的 ` D` 行）；切分支会让 tracked 总数变（180↔200）却 `-d` 不变，任何用总数的方案都会误报 |
+| 7 | **不排除 dist 必误报**：本仓 2,239 个 tracked 在 `*/dist/`（占 `packages/` 58.5%），`npm run clean --workspaces` 会让“总 D”飙到 ~2,170 | 判据按路径面排除 dist（照 `mw.py:4504` 惯例） |
+| 8 | **`existsSync`/`stat` 看不见断裂 junction**（断链 `exists=False`，但 `lstat.isSymbolicLink()=true`）；`Test-Path <link>` 对链接本身恒 True | 用 `lstat`/`os.path.lexists`/`isjunction`；判目标完好要判 `<target>` 而非 `<link>` |
+| 9 | **`os.readlink` 带 `\\?\` 前缀**（junction）；Windows 短名（`WENBOZ~1`）与长名混用 | 前缀剥掉 + `normcase`+`normpath` 后再做前缀比较 |
+| 10 | **PowerShell `FileSystemInfo.Target` 惰性解析**：先删链再读 `.Target` 得空串（`Test-Path ""` 抛错） | 删除前把 `Path/LinkType/Target` 落到普通对象 |
+| 11 | **`open("w")` 写注册表会先截断**（序列化异常 ⇒ 文件写空） | tmp + `os.replace` + 读回验证（照 `_write_workers_file:2063-2075`） |
+| 12 | **两套锁协议 = 事故温床** | 复用 `mw_common.acquire_lock`/`release_lock` 与既有命名锁规则，不新写 |
+| 13 | **G1 的 block 文案必须可执行**：G2 命令此刻还不存在（`mw.py` 的 `worktree` 命中只有 `:5335`/`:5360` 两处只读 docstring，无子命令） | G1/G2 同版本落地；文案与 `design.md` §4.3 契约逐字一致 |
+| 14 | **AC-006 字面与“仓库外 worktree + `npm ci` 自指链”死锁**（G2 拒 + G1 拦） | 按 `design.md` §4.4 的三分类判定（决策 D-1，2026-10-13 已确认） |
+| 15 | **采样命令可能刷新 `.git/index`**（未观测到变化，但 git 文档允许） | 采样统一 `git --no-optional-locks` / `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`；不并跑其它 git 写操作 |
+| 16 | **夹具绝对不能指回真树**，清理也不能用穿透形态 | 链接目标全部在夹具目录内；清理 = 先逐条 `cmd /c rmdir <link>`（无 `/S`、无尾分隔符）再 `rmdir /S /Q <root>` |

+The claim locators are part of the scope because a review unit has to be able to read the files its claims are about; anything wider would let the review price itself by repo size again. `read`, `grep`, `find` and `ls` all draw on the same `l2_read_file_cap` call budget (only `read` charges bytes against `l2_read_byte_cap`), so a locator bounds both what is read and what can be searched.

 ### Gate modes
 
-`advisory` is the default: the dispatch receipt carries one `[claims] ... warnings=[...]` line and the dispatch proceeds. `MW_CLAIM_GATE=enforce` is the explicit opt-in that turns every finding into a refusal (code `dispatch-claims`, zero side effects). An unknown or blank value falls back to `advisory` with one diagnostic, so a typo can neither enforce silently nor stall the loop.

* pm/decision-tool.ts — the `ask_decision` tool: the ONLY LLM-facing channel\n * for asking an external decision point (mw-decision-substitution T-05, spec\n * DS-7/DS-10, design D-017, D4 research Q1..Q6).\n *\n * Contract\n * - Input: `dp` (enum of the registry ids this module holds as constants),\n *   `trigger` (audit label: `<task_key>` | `<task_key>#ckpt<N>` | `ts`; the\n *   decision id  7-value vocabulary) and/or `missing_fields` when they apply, followed by a\n *   fixed second line that forbids guessing. The model sees this text verbatim\n *   as the tool result, so both shapes are deterministic (no prose rewriting,\n *   design Q2 §2.4).\n * - `execute` runs `python -X utf8 mw.py decide run --project=<dir> --dp <id>\n *   --request-file <tmp> --json` with an ASYNC spawn and a hard 20 s wall\n *   (design D-017: a synchronous child inside a tool call would freeze the\n *   event loop, the heartbeat and trace writes). The request JSON travels in a\n *   temp file, never on argv (spec D-003).\n * - Failure shape: a SERVICE failure is DATA (`available:false` + directive) —\n *   it must not throw, or the model would lose the \"do not guess\" instruction.\n *   Only argument misuse (the TypeBox enum) is rejected by the loop's\n *   `validateToolArguments`, because `AgentToolResult`\n *   (`packages/agent/src/types.ts:355-368`) has no `isError` field; `execute`\n *   throwing is the only other way to surface a hard error.\n *\n * Authorization, `mode` and `acted` (D-036 / D-041)\n * - A structured request (`--dp <registry id>`, no `questions`) makes\n *   `mw decide run` call `decision_points.decide_for(..., intent=\"answer\")`,\n *   which is the single authority: it reads `.mw/decide-points.json` itself\n *   (step 2), resolves the mode (step 3) and archives one row per decision\n *   (`packages/multi-workers/mw.py:_decide_run`). Every other dp is not gated on required fields by the registry, so\n * it is never pre-refused here (over-gating would be its own authority drift).\n */\nexport function missingDecisionStateFields(dp: string, state: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {\n\tif (!(ASK_DECISION_ENFORCED_STATE_DP_IDS as readonly string[]).includes(dp)) return [];\n\treturn validateStructuredState(dp, state).filter((field) => !PYTHON_AUTO_FILLED_FIELDS.has(field));\n}\n\n/** Serialise the request envelope (single line; questions come from the\n * registry because `--dp` is always given, design D-027). */\nexport function buildDecisionRequestJson(state: Record<string, unknown>): string {\n\treturn JSON.stringify({ state });\n}\n\n// ── Async spawn with a hard wall ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nexport interface RawDecideResult {\n\tstatus: number | null;\n\tstdout: string;\n\tstderr: string;\n\t/** Spawn-level failure text (missing mw.py, ENOENT, aborted, ...). */\n\terror?: string;\n\ttimedOut: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface SpawnWithTimeoutOptions {\n\ttimeoutMs?: number;\n\tsignal?: AbortSignal;\n}\n\n/** Cap on captured child output so a runaway child cannot exhaust memory. */\nconst MAX_CHILD_OUTPUT_BYTES = 1_048_576;\n\n/**\n * Spawn `argv` (no shell) and race it against a hard wall-clock timeout.\n *\n * `timedOut:true` means the child was killed after `timeoutMs`. The promise\n * settles on `close` (stdio drained); a killed child that never emits `close`\n * is force-resolved after a short grace so a tool call can never hang.\n */\nexport function spawnWithTimeout(argv: string[], options: SpawnWithTimeoutOptions = {}): Promise<RawDecideResult> {\n\tconst timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? ASK_DECISION_TIMEOUT_MS;\n\treturn new Promise<RawDecideResult>((resolve) => {\n\t\tlet settled = false;\n\t\tlet stdout = \"\";\n\t\tlet stderr = \"\";\n\t\tlet timedOut = false;\n\t\tlet spawnError: string | undefined;\n\t\tlet wallTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;\n\t\tlet graceTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;\n\n\t\tconst finish = (status: number | null): void => {\n\t\t\tif (settled) return;\n\t\t\tsettled = true;\n\t\t\tif (wallTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(wallTimer);\n\t\t\tif (graceTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(graceTimer);\n\t\t\toptions.signal?.removeEventListener(\"abort\", onAbort);\n\t\t\tconst result: RawDecideResult = { status, stdout, stderr, timedOut };\n\t\t\tif (spawnError !== undefined) result.error = spawnError;\n\t\t\tresolve(result);\n\t\t};\n\n\t\tconst append = (current: string, chunk: string): string => {\n\t\t\tif (Buffer.byteLength(current, \"utf8\") >= MAX_CHILD_OUTPUT_BYTES) return current;\n\t\t\treturn current + chunk;\n\t\t};\n\n\t\tconst child = spawn(argv[0], argv.slice(1), {\n\t\t\twindowsHide: true,\n\t\t\tstdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"pipe\"],\n\t\t});\n\n\t\tconst kill = (): void => {\n\t\t\ttry {\n\t\t\t\t// SIGKILL maps to TerminateProcess on Windows; no grandchildren are\n\t\t\t\t// left behind by `mw decide run` (it is a single Python process).\n\t\t\t\tchild.kill(\"SIGKILL\");\n\t\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t\t// Already gone — `close` will settle the promise.\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t// A process killed mid-write may hold stdio open; never hang the tool.\n\t\t\tgraceTimer = setTimeout(() => finish(child.exitCode), 2_000);\n\t\t};\n\t\tconst onAbort = (): void => {\n\t\t\tif (settled) return;\n\t\t\tspawnError = \"aborted\";\n\t\t\tkill();\n\t\t};\n\n\t\tchild.stdout?.setEncoding(\"utf8\");\n\t\tchild.stderr?.setEncoding(\"utf8\");\n\t\tchild.stdout?.on(\"data\", (chunk: string) => {\n\t\t\tstdout = append(stdout, chunk);\n\t\t});\n\t\tchild.stderr?.on(\"data\", (chunk: string) => {\n\t\t\tstderr = append(stderr, chunk);\n\t\t});\n\t\tchild.on(\"error\", (err: Error) => {\n\t\t\tspawnError = err.message;\n\t\t\tfinish(null);\n\t\t});\n\t\tchild.on(\"close\", (code: number | null) => finish(code));\n\n\t\tif (options.signal !== undefined) {\n\t\t\tif (options.signal.aborted) onAbort();\n\t\t\telse options.signal.addEventListener(\"abort\", onAbort, { once: true });\n\t\t}\n\t\twallTimer = setTimeout(() => {\n\t\t\tif (settled) return;\n\t\t\ttimedOut = true;\n\t\t\tkill();\n\t\t}, timeoutMs);\n\t});\n}\n\nexport interface DecideRunRequest {\n\tprojectDir: string;\n\tdp: string;\n\t/** Request JSON (state envelope) — written to a temp file, never argv. */\n\tinput: string;\n\ttimeoutMs: number;\n}\n\n/** Injectable runner (tests replace this; production uses {@link runDecideMw}). */\nexport type DecideRunner = (request: DecideRunRequest, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<RawDecideResult>;\n\n/** Build the `python -X utf8 mw.py decide run ...` argv (design D-003: the\n * state rides `--request-file`, argv carries only routing). The caller prepends\n * {@link PYTHON_EXE}; this list is platform-independent on purpose. */\nexport function buildDecideArgv(mwPy: string, request: DecideRunRequest, requestFile: string): string[] {\n\treturn [\n\t\t\"-X\",\n\t\t\"utf8\",\n\t\tmwPy,\n\t\t\"decide\",\n\t\t\"run\",\n\t\t`--project=${request.projectDir}`,\n\t\t\"--dp\",\n\t\trequest.dp,\n\t\t\"--request-file\",\n\t\trequestFile,\n\t\t\"--json\",\n\t];\n}\n\n/** Write the request JSON to a private temp dir and return `{dir, file}`. */\nfunction writeRequestFile(input: string): { dir: string; file: string } {\n\tconst dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), \"mw-decide-\"));\n\tconst file = path.join(dir, \"request.json\");\n\tfs.writeFileSync(file, input, { encoding: \"utf8\", mode: 0o600 });\n\treturn { dir, file };\n}\n\n/**\n * The real child: reuse mw-runner's interpreter/path resolution, write the\n * request to a temp file, await the async spawn, always clean the temp file up.\n */\nexport const runDecideMw: DecideRunner = async (request, signal) => {\n\tconst mwPy = findMwPy();\n\tif (!mwPy) return { status: null, stdout: \"\", stderr: \"\", error: \"mw.py not found\", timedOut: false };\n\tlet files: { dir: string; never throws). */\nexport function parseDecisionJson(stdout: string): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {\n\tconst candidates = [stdout.trim()];\n\tconst lastLine = stdout.trim().split(\"\\n\").at(-1)?.trim();\n\tif (lastLine !== undefined && lastLine !== candidates[0]) candidates.push(lastLine);\n\tfor (const text of candidates) {\n\t\tif (!text) continue;\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tconst parsed = JSON.parse(text) as unknown;\n\t\t\tif (isRecord(parsed)) return parsed;\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t// Try the next candidate.\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn undefined;\n}\n\n/** The fixed no-guessing line appended to every unavailable payload. */\nexport function unavailableDirective(reason: string, dp: string): string {\n\tconst base =\n\t\t`UNAVAILABLE(${reason}) — ${ASK_DECISION_GUESS_DIRECTIVE}，不要执行被门控的动作，` +\n\t\t`不要用别的工具绕过，也不要重复问同一个问题。上报 \"blocked on decision ${dp}\" 并等待人工裁决。`;\n\tif (reason === \"disabled\") {\n\t\treturn `${base} disabled ≠ approval：决策点未开启不等于放行，被门控的动作仍受其常规工具权限约束。`;\n\t}\n\treturn base;\n}\n\n/** Terminal directive emitted once a dp hits the per-turn block cap. */\nexport function terminalDirective(dp: string, blocks: number): string {\n\treturn (\n\t\t`TERMINAL: \"${dp}\" has been blocked ${blocks} time(s) in this turn. ${ASK_DECISION_GUESS_DIRECTIVE}。` +\n\t\t`停止重试，上报 \"blocked on decision ${dp}\" 并结束本轮（不要再次调用 ask_decision）。`\n\t);\n}\n\n// ── The one decision call ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nexport interface AskDecisionInput {\n\tprojectDir: string;\n\tdp: string;\n\t/** Audit label for the trace line only; The enum in the\n\t// tool schema already rejects it; `runAskDecision` is also called directly.\n\tif (!isRegisteredDp(dp)) return unavailable(\"disabled\", dp, false);\n\n\tconst state = buildDecisionState({ dp, note: input.note, taskKey: input.taskKey });\n\t// `decide_for` step 5 refuses a state that misses a registry-required field,\n\t// so report the field names (L0) instead of spending a round trip that can\n\t// only come back `input-incomplete`/`bad-response` (MAJOR-2).\n\tconst missing = missingDecisionStateFields(dp, state);\n\tif (missing.length > 0) {\n\t\treturn unavailable(ASK_DECISION_REASON_INPUT_INCOMPLETE, dp, false, { missing_fields: missing });\n\t}\n\tif (canonicalStateBytes(state) > ASK_DECISION_MAX_STATE_BYTES) {\n\t\treturn unavailable(ASK_DECISION_REASON_INPUT_OVERSIZE, dp, false);\n\t}\n\tconst requestJson = buildDecisionRequestJson(state);\n\n\tconst runner = input.runner ?? runDecideMw;\n\tconst request: DecideRunRequest = {\n\t\tprojectDir: input.projectDir,\n\t\tdp,\n\t\tinput: requestJson,\n\t\ttimeoutMs: input.timeoutMs ?? Repeating the same call in one turn is cut off by the retry breaker.\",\n\t\t\t\"unavailable=input-incomplete lists missing_fields: the registry needs them and this tool cannot \" +\n\t\t\t\t\"produce them, so do not retry — report the block.\",\n\t\t\t\"note is an L0/L1 summary (<=600 bytes): no credentials, no user quotes, no absolute paths, no code.\",\n\t\t\t\"mode=suggest only archives an advisory row; acted is the service's verdict and never your own \" +\n\t\t\t\t\"inference from the mode.\",\n\t\t],\n\t\tparameters: ASK_DECISION_PARAMETERS,\n\t\t// Sequential: an ask changes gate state, so it must not race the tools\n\t\t// it authorizes (design Q1 §1.1).\n\t\texecutionMode: \"sequential\",\n\t\texecute: async (_toolCallId, params, signal) => {\n\t\t\tconst outcome = await runAskDecision({\n\t\t\t\tprojectDir,\n\t\t\t\tdp: params.dp,\n\t\t\t\ttrigger: params.trigger,\n\t\t\t\tquestion: params.question,\n\t\t\t\tnote: params.note,\n\t\t\t\ttaskKey,\n\t\t\t\trunner: options.runner,\n\t\t\t\ttimeoutMs: options.timeoutMs,\n\t\t\t\tsignal,\n\t\t\t});\n\t\t\tconst iso = new Date().toISOString();\n\t\t\tif (outcome.payload.available) {\n\t\t\t\tcounter.clear(params.dp);\n\t\t\t\tappendDecisionTrace(\n\t\t\t\t\ttracePath,\n\t\t\t\t\t`[DECISION] ${iso} dp=${params.dp} trigger=${params.trigger} ` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t`decision_id=${outcome.payload.decision_id} mode=${outcome.payload.mode} ` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t`acted=${String(outcome.payload.acted)} source=${outcome.payload.confidence_source} ` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t`latency_ms=${outcome.payload.latency_ms}`,\n\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t\treturn { content: [{ type: \"text\", text: outcome.text }], details: outcome.payload };\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tconst reason = outcome.payload.unavailable;\n\t\t\tconst escalated =\n\t\t\t\toutcome.payload.escalated_reason !== undefined\n\t\t\t\t\t? ` escalated_reason=${outcome.payload.escalated_reason}`\n\t\t\t\t\t: \"\";\n\t\t\tconst blocks = counter.recordBlock(params.dp);\n\t\t\tappendDecisionTrace(\n\t\t\t\ttracePath,\n\t\t\t\t`[DECISION_UNAVAILABLE] ${iso} dp=${params.dp} trigger=${params.trigger} reason=${reason}` +\n\t\t\t\t\t`${escalated} count=${blocks} max=${ASK_DECISION_MAX_BLOCKED_PER_TURN}`,\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t\tif (blocks < ASK_DECISION_MAX_BLOCKED_PER_TURN) {\n\t\t\t\treturn { content: [{ type: \"text\", text: outcome.text }], details: outcome.payload };\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tappendDecisionTrace(\n\t\t\t\ttracePath,\n\t\t\t\t`[DECISION_RETRY_STOP] ${iso} dp=${params.dp} trigger=${params.trigger} reason=${reason} ` +\n\t\t\t\t\t`count=${blocks} max=${ASK_DECISION_MAX_BLOCKED_PER_TURN}`,\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t// `terminate` stops the tool loop when every finalized result in the\n\t\t\t// batch asks for it (agent-loop.ts:582-584); ask_decision is\n\t\t\t// sequential, so a batch that contains it stops here.\n\t\t\treturn {\n\t\t\t\tcontent: [{ type: \"text\", text: `${outcome.text}\\n${terminalDirective(params.dp, blocks)}` }],\n\t\t\t\tdetails: outcome.payload,\n\t\t\t\tterminate: true,\n\t\t\t};\n\t\t},\n\t});\n\n\t// Active-set append (spec §5.3 / design Q5 §5.2): runs after the worker's\n\t// own before_agent_start recomputation, so every role sees the tool without\n\t// touching TOOL_ALLOWLISTS. Idempotent — a repeated append is a no-op.\n\tpi.on(\"before_agent_start\", () => {\n\t\tconst active = pi.getActiveTools();\n\t\tif (active.includes(ASK_DECISION_TOOL)) return;\n\t\tpi.setActiveTools([...active, ASK_DECISION_TOOL]);\n\t});\n\n\treturn { projectDir, tracePath, counter };\n}\n"]}

+/** Look one registry path (dotted) up in a material/state object. */
+function readMaterialPath(source, dotted) {

+export function missingMaterialPaths(dp, material) {

+function pushFieldIssue(issues, field, value) {
+    switch (field.type) {
+        case "string":
+            if (typeof value !== "string" || value.trim() === "") {
+                issues.push({ field: field.name, rule: "must be a non-empty string" });
+            }
+            return;
+        case "array":
+            if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
+                issues.push({ field: field.name, rule: "must be an array" });
+                return;
+            }
+            if (field.itemType === "string" && value.some((item) => typeof item !== "string" || item.trim() === "")) {
+                issues.push({ field: field.name, rule: "every item must be a non-empty string" });
+            }
+            return;
+        case "object":
+            if (!isRecord(value))
+                issues.push({ field: field.name, rule: "must be an object" });
+            return;
+        default:
+            if (value === undefined || value === null) {
+                issues.push({ field: field.name, rule: "must be present" });
+            }
+            return;
+    }

+/** dp3 native dynamic candidates: 2..5 problem-specific options, contiguous
+ * `c1..cN`, single-line labels <= 80 chars, non-empty descriptions, distinct
+ * labels (mirror of `decision_points.dynamic_choices_value_error`). */
+function checkHandlingOptions(value, issues) {
+    if (!Array.isArray(value))
+        return;
+    if (value.length < DP3_HANDLING_MIN_OPTIONS) {
+        issues.push({
+            field: "handling_options",
+            rule: `needs at least ${DP3_HANDLING_MIN_OPTIONS} distinguishable candidates`,
+        });
+    }
+    if (value.length > DP3_HANDLING_MAX_OPTIONS) {
+        issues.push({
+            field: "handling_options",
+            rule: `expected at most ${DP3_HANDLING_MAX_OPTIONS} candidates`,
+        });
+    }
+    const labels = new Set();
+    value.forEach((raw, index) => {
+        const item = isRecord(raw) ? raw : undefined;
+        if (item === undefined) {
+            issues.push({ field: `handling_options[${index}]`, rule: "must be an {id,label,description} object" });
+            return;
+        }
+        for (const unknownKey of Object.keys(item)) {
+            if (unknownKey !== "id" && unknownKey !== "label" && unknownKey !== "description") {
+                issues.push({ field: `handling_options[${index}].${unknownKey}`, rule: "not a candidate field" });
+            }
+        }
+        const expectedId = `c${index + 1}`;
+        if (item.id !== expectedId) {
+            issues.push({
+                field: `handling_options[${index}].id`,
+                rule: `must be the contiguous candidate id ${expectedId}`,
+            });
+        }
+        const label = item.label;
+        if (typeof label !== "string" || label.trim() === "") {
+            issues.push({ field: `handling_options[${index}].label`, rule: "must be a non-empty string" });
+        }
+        else {
+            if (/[\r\n]/.test(label)) {
+                issues.push({ field: `handling_options[${index}].label`, rule: "must be a single line" });
+            }
+            if (label.length > DP3_HANDLING_LABEL_MAX) {
+                issues.push({
+                    field: `handling_options[${index}].label`,
+                    rule: `must be at most ${DP3_HANDLING_LABEL_MAX} characters`,
+                });
+            }
+            if (labels.has(label)) {
+                issues.push({
+                    field: `handling_options[${index}].label`,
+                    rule: "must differ from every other candidate label",
+                });
+            }
+            labels.add(label);
+        }
+        const description = item.description;
+        if (typeof description !== "string" || description.trim() === "") {
+            issues.push({ field: `handling_options[${index}].description`, rule: "must be a non-empty string" });
+        }
+    });

+/**
+ * Validate one dp's business material against the generated registry.
+ *
+ * Every field, and the closed key set, comes from `DECIDE_REGISTRY`
+ * (`modelStateFields` + `requiredStateFields`/`optionalStateFields`) — the one
+ * authority T01 publishes — so a renamed field shows up here as a refusal, not
+ * as a second contract drifting from Python. The material is returned VERBATIM
+ * (no truncation, no default, no invention): necessary material that cannot be
+ * sent is refused as `input-oversize` by the caller instead. Unknown facts stay
+ * `unknown` in the text the agent wrote; this function never derives one.
+ */
+export function validateDecisionMaterial(dp, material) {
+    const entry = DECIDE_REGISTRY[dp];
+    const paths = entry?.modelStateFields;
+    if (entry === undefined || paths === undefined) {
+        return { ok: false, issues: [{ field: "dp", rule: "no material contract for this dp" }] };
+    }
+    if (!isRecord(material)) {
+        return { ok: false, issues: [{ field: "material", rule: "must be an object" }] };
+    }
+    const issues = [];
+    const allowedTop = new Set(paths.map((item) => item.split(".")[0]));
+    for (const key of Object.keys(material)) {
+        if (!allowedTop.has(key)) {
+            issues.push({ field: key, rule: "not in required_state_fields (closed key set)" });
+        }
+    }
+    // Nested containers may only carry declared children (background.*,
+    // verification_evidence.*).
+    const containers = new Map();
+    for (const item of paths) {
+        const [head, child] = item.split(".");
+        if (head === undefined || child === undefined)
+            continue;
+        const children = containers.get(head) ?? new Set();
+        children.add(child);
+        containers.set(head, children);
+    }
+    for (const [container, children] of containers) {
+        const value = material[container];
+        if (!isRecord(value))
+            continue;
+        for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {
+            if (!children.has(key)) {
+                issues.push({ field: `${container}.${key}`, rule: "not in required_state_fields (closed key set)" });
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    for (const field of entry.requiredStateFields) {
+        pushFieldIssue(issues, field, readMaterialPath(material, field.name));
+    }
+    for (const field of entry.optionalStateFields) {
+        const value = readMaterialPath(material, field.name);
+        if (value !== undefined && value !== null)
+            pushFieldIssue(issues, field, value);
+    }
+    if (paths.includes("handling_options"))
+        checkHandlingOptions(material.handling_options, issues);
+    if (issues.length > 0)
+        return { ok: false, issues };
+    return { ok: true, material };
+}

+/** Resolve dp3's native `handling` answer to the candidate the asker supplied. */
+export function resolveHandlingSelection(answers, options) {
+    if (!isRecord(answers) || !Array.isArray(options))
+        return undefined;
+    const entry = answers.handling;
+    const value = isRecord(entry) ? entry.value : undefined;
+    if (typeof value !== "string" || value === "")
+        return undefined;
+    for (const raw of options) {
+        if (!isRecord(raw) || raw.id !== value)
+            continue;
+        const label = typeof raw.label === "string" ? raw.label : undefined;
+        const description = typeof raw.description === "string" ? raw.description : undefined;
+        return { question: "handling", id: value, label, description };
+    }
+    return undefined;

+/** The real feedback child: the payload rides stdin, never argv. */

+/** Write one feedback fact through the single Python lifecycle writer.
+ *
+ * Never throws and never claims success: a timeout, a non-zero exit, a missing
+ * CLI, an unparsable receipt or `recorded:false` all become `status:"failed"`
+ * with the child's own class, so the caller can report "反馈缺失" instead of
+ * fabricating the row. A `duplicate` receipt is reported as `duplicate` (the
+ * same event replayed), never silently rewritten to `written`.
+ *
+ * Exported because the dp1 dispatch consumer is a second real writer face: one
+ * CLI writer implementation serves dp1, dp3 and dp25.
+ */
+export async function writeDecisionLifecycle(projectDir, envelope, runner = runLifecycleMw) {
+    const stage = envelope.stage;
+    try {
+        const raw = await runner({
+            projectDir,
+            input: JSON.stringify(envelope),
+            timeoutMs: DECISION_LIFECYCLE_TIMEOUT_MS,
+        });
+        if (raw.timedOut)
+            return { stage, status: "failed", recorded: false, reason: "timeout" };
+        if (raw.error !== undefined)
+            return { stage, status: "failed", recorded: false, reason: "unavailable" };
+        const receipt = parseDecisionJson(raw.stdout);
+        if (receipt === undefined) {
+            return { stage, status: "failed", recorded: false, reason: raw.status === 0 ? "bad-response" : "cli-error" };
+        }
+        if (receipt.recorded !== true) {
+            const errorClass = typeof receipt.error_class === "string" ? receipt.error_class : "rejected";
+            return { stage, status: "failed", recorded: false, reason: errorClass };
+        }
+        const status = receipt.status === "duplicate" ? "duplicate" : "written";
+        return { stage, status, recorded: true };
+    }
+    catch {
+        return { stage, status: "failed", recorded: false, reason: "runner-threw" };
+    }

The model sees this text verbatim\n *   as the tool result, so both shapes are deterministic (no prose rewriting,\n *   design Q2 §2.4).\n * - `execute` runs `python -X utf8 mw.py decide run --project=<dir> --dp <id>\n *   --request-file <tmp> --json` with an ASYNC spawn and a hard 20 s wall\n *   (design D-017: a synchronous child inside a tool call would freeze the\n *   event loop, the heartbeat and trace writes). The request JSON travels in a\n *   temp file, never on argv (spec D-003).\n * - Failure shape: a SERVICE failure is DATA (`available:false` + directive) —\n *   it must not throw, or the model would lose the \"do not guess\" instruction.\n *   Only argument misuse (the TypeBox enum) is rejected by the loop's\n *   `validateToolArguments`, because `AgentToolResult`\n *   (`packages/agent/src/types.ts:355-368`) has no `isError` field; `execute`\n *   throwing is the only other way to surface a hard error.\n *\n * Authorization, `mode` and `acted` (D-036 / D-041)\n * - A structured request (`--dp <registry id>`, no `questions`) makes\n *   `mw decide run` call `decision_points.decide_for(..., intent=\"answer\")`,\n *   which is the single authority: it reads `.mw/decide-points.json` itself\n *   (step 2), resolves the mode (step 3) and archives one row per decision\n *   (`packages/multi-workers/mw.py:_decide_run`). Its JSON therefore carries\n *   `decision_id` / `mode` / `acted` / `escalated_reason`\n *   (`_decide_run_payload`, T-02b).\n * - This module consumes those four keys verbatim. It never reads the\n *   authorization table, never derives `mode` from a tier default and never\n *   turns `mode` into `acted`: D-041 makes `acted` a consuming-side fact, and\n *   an `intent=\"answer\"` decision is archived with `acted=false` (D-035) no\n *   matter what the mode is.\n * - `trigger` is an audit label for the trace line and the directives only. The\n *   authoritative `decision_id` is `<dp>:<trigger_id>` resolved by Python from\n *   the state's `key`/`task_key` (`decision_points.py:Trigger.resolved_id`), so\n *   a locally concatenated id would drift from the archive row.\n * - Nothing here writes config or the archive: Python stays the single writer\n *   (D-005).\n *\n * Structured state (spec §5.4 L0/L1, D6 Q5.1)\n * - {@link buildDecisionState} fills only what this call site knows\n *   (`v`/`dp`/`key`/`task_key`/`task_summary`). `decide_for` step 5 refuses a\n *   state that misses one of the registry's `REQUIRED_STATE_FIELDS`\n *   (`packages/multi-workers/decision_points.py:626`), so for the dps that map\n *   covers (dp1/dp2/dp3) the tool refuses **before** the spawn and reports the\n *   field names (names only: L0) instead of spending a round trip on a state\n *   Python can only answer with `input-incomplete`/`bad-response` (MAJOR-2).\n * - The field table itself is not copied: the check reuses\n *   `pm/triage-client.ts`'s structured-state validator and\n *   `REQUIRED_FIELDS_BY_DP` (single source). Only the id set of the dps the\n *   registry gates is held here, pinned to the Python source by the suite.\n *\n * Anti-retry (spec §5.3 / design Q3 §3.3)\n * - A per-dp block counter is scoped to one agent turn (`turn_start` resets it).\n *   Reaching {@link ASK_DECISION_MAX_BLOCKED_PER_TURN} marks the tool result\n *   `terminate: true` and appends a terminal directive, so the tool loop stops\n *   instead of the model re-asking forever. Every block/answer leaves one\n *   machine line in the worker's trace.log.\n */\n\nimport { spawn } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport * as fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport * as os from \"node:os\";\nimport * as path from \"node:path\";\nimport { type TLiteral, Type } from \"typebox\";\nimport type { ExtensionAPI } from \"../../../core/extensions/types.ts\";\nimport { findMwPy, PYTHON_EXE } from \"../shared/mw-runner.ts\";\nimport { controlRootFromTaskPath } from \"../shared/paths.ts\";\nimport { canonicalStateBytes, MAX_STRUCTURED_STATE_BYTES, validateStructuredState } from \"./triage-client.ts\";\n\n/** Registered tool name (referenced by `activeToolsForType` wiring in index.ts). */\nexport const ASK_DECISION_TOOL = \"ask_decision\";\n\n/** Hard client-side wall for one `mw decide run` child (design D-017/D-006). */\nexport const ASK_DECISION_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000;\n\n/** Same-dp blocks inside one turn before the tool loop is terminated. */\nexport const ASK_DECISION_MAX_BLOCKED_PER_TURN = 2;\n\n/** The only failure action the model is ever told about (spec §5.1 fail-closed). */\nexport const ASK_DECISION_BLOCKED_ACTION = \"blocked-ask-human\";\n\n/** Client-side canonical state budget (spec AC-013 / §5.4). The promise\n * settles on `close` (stdio drained); a killed child that never emits `close`\n * is force-resolved after a short grace so a tool call can never hang.\n */\nexport function spawnWithTimeout(argv: string[], options: SpawnWithTimeoutOptions = {}): Promise<RawDecideResult> {\n\tconst timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? Writing design.md / plan.md also\n * runs the next-phase evidence gate (mirrors advance_phase.py): the previous\n * phase's research notes must exist, or the user is warned immediately. */\nexport async function autoTakeOverFromDoc(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\tindexStore: IndexStore,\n\twatch: PmWatchState,\n\trefreshWatch: (ctx: ExtensionContext) => void,\n\tkey: string,\n\tdoc: PhaseDocName,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n): Promise<void> {\n\t// Next-phase evidence gate: writing design.md means the spec phase should be\n\t// complete (its research notes exist); writing plan.md means design should be.\n\t// Fires regardless of takeover idempotency — the missing evidence is the\n\t// message, and it stays true until the notes are written.\n\tconst docs = readPhaseDocs(agenticdocRoot, key);\n\tif (doc === \"spec.md\" && docs.specEvidence < 1) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/spec-*.md found — write the research notes (or a zero-research declaration) alongside the spec; the advance-to-design gate checks them.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tif (doc === \"design.md\" && docs.specEvidence < 1) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/spec-*.md found — the advance-to-design gate requires >= 1 research note (a zero-research declaration counts). Write it before advancing.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tif (doc === \"plan.md\") {\n\t\tif (!docs.design) {\n\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: design.md missing or under 500 bytes — required before plan (run the system-design workflow).`,\n\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t} else if (docs.designEvidence < 1) {\n\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/design-*.md found — the advance-to-plan gate requires >= 1 research note (a zero-research declaration counts). Write it before advancing.`,\n\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tconst row = indexStore.findByKey(key);\n\tconst wasWatching = watch.key === key;\n\tconst wasClaimed = row?.claimId === windowClaimId();\n\tif (wasWatching && wasClaimed) return; // already ours — nothing to do\n\n\tconst result = await takeOverKey(indexStore, key, false, agenticdocRoot);\n\twatch.key = key;\n\tpi.appendEntry(WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE, { key, claimed: result.ok });\n\trefreshWatch(ctx);\n\tif (result.ok) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] claimed key '${key}' (doc write detected) — watching it${result.created ? \" (new key registered)\" : \"\"}.`,\n\t\t\t\"info\",\n\t\t);\n\t\tif (result.audit.length > 0) ctx.ui.notify(result.audit.join(\"\\n\"), \"warning\");\n\t} else {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' is claimed by another live window (${result.blockedBy}) — watching only.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Restore this window's watched key from the session file (survives restart\n * and resume) and re-render the bottom widget. A watch that came with a key\n * takeover re-claims the key with this process's identity — quietly, unless\n * another live window took it over in the meantime. */\nexport async function restoreWatch(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\twatch: PmWatchState,\n\tindexStore: IndexStore,\n\tworkerStore: WorkerStore,\n\tackStore: AckStore,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n): Promise<void> {\n\tlet data: { key?: string; claimed?: boolean } | undefined;\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst entries = ctx.sessionManager.getEntries();\n\t\tfor (let i = entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n\t\t\tconst e = entries[i];\n\t\t\tif (e.type === \"custom\" && e.customType === WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE) {\n\t\t\t\tdata = e.data as { key?: string; claimed?: boolean } | undefined;\n\t\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn; // session entries unavailable — nothing to restore\n\t}\n\tif (!data?.key) return;\n\tconst key = data.key;\n\twatch.key = key;\n\n\t// T-16c: the restart restore path may take a key back from THIS host's\n\t// conductor (a `held-conductor` synthetic claim is yieldable — T-16b). That\n\t// handover is correct (human priority) but must not be silent: the goal is\n\t// that \"who took the key from the conductor, and when\" stays explainable.\n\t// Recorded on existing surfaces only — no new event name, no new entry type:\n\t//   * the `_index.parallel` Claim cell (and the pm-state.md mirror) flips to\n\t//     this window — the state surface;\n\t//   * `tookOverFromConductor` rides the EXISTING `agent-team-loop:watch`\n\t//     session entry shape, giving the durable machine-readable act record;\n\t//   * a transcript notice via the existing `displaySummary` channel states\n\t//     the holder change out loud (passive — it never spends an agent turn).\n\t// The timeline is deliberately NOT written here: it has a single writer (the\n\t// conductor, `timeline.py` D-109) and a second seq counter would corrupt it.\n\t// Set only in the `held-conductor` branch, so a second restart (row now this\n\t// window's, or stale) leaves exactly the same record count — idempotent by\n\t// construction.\n\tlet tookOverFromConductor: string | undefined;\n\tif (data.claimed) {\n\t\tconst row = indexStore.findByKey(key);\n\t\tif (row) {\n\t\t\tconst self = windowClaimId();\n\t\t\tconst previousClaim = row.claimId.trim();\n\t\t\tconst holder = claimState(previousClaim, self);\n\t\t\tif (holder === \"held-live\") {\n\t\t\t\t// Another window took over while this one was closed — keep the\n\t\t\t\t// watch (display-only) and say so; do not touch the shared row.\n\t\t\t\t// Unchanged by T-16c (requirement 3): a truly live foreign claim\n\t\t\t\t// is still never taken silently.\n\t\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' is claimed by another window (${row.claimId}) — watching only.`,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t// Our previous process is gone; re-bind ownership through the\n\t\t\t\t// atomic claim — a window that raced us to this key wins and we\n\t\t\t\t// degrade to watch-only (review M2). Quiet re-claim: no demote of\n\t\t\t\t// other active rows, no status flip; only claimId/updated move.\n\t\t\t\tconst outcome = await indexStore.claim(key, self, (id) => claimState(id, self) === \"held-live\", {\n\t\t\t\t\tdemoteOthers: false,\n\t\t\t\t\tactivate: false,\n\t\t\t\t});\n\t\t\t\tif (!outcome.ok) {\n\t\t\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' is claimed by another window (${outcome.blockedBy}) — watching only.`,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t// This path flips the index row's Claim column too, so the\n\t\t\t\t\t// pm-state.md mirror must be synced as well (D-108). A failed\n\t\t\t\t\t// mirror never reverts the claim — the index row is\n\t\t\t\t\t// authoritative — but the divergence must be visible.\n\t\t\t\t\tconst sync = syncPmStateClaimId(agenticdocRoot, key, self);\n\t\t\t\t\tconst syncWarning = claimSyncWarningText(key, sync);\n\t\t\t\t\tif (syncWarning !== \"\") ctx.ui.notify(syncWarning, \"warning\");\n\t\t\t\t\tif (holder === \"held-conductor\") {\n\t\t\t\t\t\ttookOverFromConductor = previousClaim;\n\t\t\t\t\t\tdisplaySummary(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tpi,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t`[mw] 窗口重启恢复：key '${key}' 原由本机 autopilot conductor 接管（合成 claim ${previousClaim}），` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t`已改由本窗口接管（${self}）。人工优先，conductor 下次 tick 让位且不再抢回；` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\"记录面：_index.parallel 的 Claim 单元 + 本 session 的 agent-team-loop:watch entry（tookOverFromConductor）。\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tsetWatchWidget(\n\t\tctx,\n\t\trenderWatchLines(indexStore, workerStore, ackStore, agenticdocRoot, key, watch.dispatchedTaskKeys),\n\t);\n\t// Re-stamp the entry so it lands in the (possibly new) session file.\n\t// T-16c: `tookOverFromConductor` (the pre-takeover synthetic claim id) is\n\t// added ONLY on the handover restore, so the act record is exactly one entry\n\t// regardless of how often the window restarts afterwards.\n\tpi.appendEntry(WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE, {\n\t\tkey,\n\t\tclaimed: data.claimed ?? false,\n\t\t...(tookOverFromConductor === undefined ? {} : { tookOverFromConductor }),\n\t});\n\n\t// Saved working context (pm-save): point the user at it — a notice, never\n\t// an injected instruction (same principle as evidenceReviewNotice: the\n\t// framework flags, the user decides whether the agent reads it).\n\tconst pmStatePath = path.join(agenticdocRoot, key, \"pm-state.md\");\n\tif (fs.existsSync(pmStatePath)) {\n\t\tconst updated = fs.statSync(pmStatePath).mtime.toISOString();\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' 有已保存的 pm-state.md（更新于 ${updated}）。如需接续上次的工作上下文，让 agent 读取 ${key}/pm-state.md 的 Notes 区。`,\n\t\t\t\"info\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction pickWorkerRoute(taskContent: string): { cli: string; provider: string } {\n\t// Global default is pi/timi: review/research are routing HINTS for the\n\t// agent, not claude redirects (design D-005) — a claude worker requires an\n\t// explicit `cli` param on dispatch_worker / /worker, where missing\n\t// credentials fail per-task instead of silently degrading the route.\n\t// The reading comes from the single-source header parser (AC-005/F-6): the\n\t// old `/^type:\\s*codex/im` full-text regex let one body line flip the\n\t// dispatch CLI, outside the shared `type:` matrix.\n\tif (readTaskType(taskContent).type === \"codex\") return { cli: \"codex\", provider: \"\" };\n\treturn { cli: \"pi\", provider: \"timi\" };\n}\n\n// Optional `model:` line in task.md → passed through to the launcher as --model/-m.\nfunction readModel(taskContent: string): string {\n\tconst m = taskContent.match(/^model:\\s*(.+)$/im);\n\treturn m ? m[1].trim() : \"\";\n}\n\n// Conductor-origin marker line (D-104): `origin: conductor`. Conductor task.md\n// files are rendered by autopilot/dispatch.py render_task_md; the value is the\n// literal token \"conductor\" (line-exact, CRLF-tolerant).\nconst ORIGIN_LINE_RE = /^origin:[ \\t]*(\\S+)[ \\t\\r]*$/m;\n\n/** Dispatch origin of a task.md, when it carries an `origin:` line. */\nfunction readTaskOrigin(taskContent: string): string | undefined {\n\treturn ORIGIN_LINE_RE.exec(taskContent)?.[1];\n}\n\n/** Is this a conductor-owned task (D-104)? Such tasks are queued by the\n * conductor alone — the TS scan must never upsert them, closing both the\n * scan/upsert race and the re-insert-as-pending path that a launcher restart\n * (or an archived row) would otherwise open. Manual/legacy tasks carry no\n * marker and behave exactly as before (AC-012 zero regression). Unreadable\n * task.md returns false so the dispatch loop hits the same read error it\n * always did. */\nfunction isConductorTask(taskMdPath: string): boolean {\n\ttry {\n\t\treturn readTaskOrigin(fs.readFileSync(taskMdPath, \"utf8\")) === \"conductor\";\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Why a dispatch scan refused to queue anything (AC-020/AC-021). */\nexport type DispatchAlarmKind =\n\t| \"queue-rows-unparsable\"\n\t| \"queue-unreadable\"\n\t| \"dispatch-quota\"\n\t// A candidate outside this window's scope (AC-019/T-19): the PM must be able\n\t// to see what it did NOT touch, aggregated per scan — visibility, not\n\t// prohibition (the read side stays global, AC-024). NOTICE, not a refusal:\n\t// nothing was refused, these keys simply belong to somebody else. Since T-22\n\t// the kind carries ONLY keys with no owner record at all (no index row AND no\n\t// `pm-state.md` machine line / worker `trace.log`): the text names the exact\n\t// human action (`switch_key` / `dispatch_worker(key=…)`) because a guessed\n\t// index row would invent Phase/ClaimId/Deps facts.\n\t| \"out-of-scope\"\n\t// A registered key with undispatched work, no live claim and no live run\n\t// (AC-011/T-19): its owner is gone and nothing will ever re-dispatch it —\n\t// the conductor only skips CLAIM_LIVE keys and claiming one is forbidden\n\t// (AUTOPILOT-HANDOFF §5 #13), so the scan repairs it claim-free. Actionable\n\t// NOTICE, one per key per session, never a refusal.\n\t| \"orphaned-keys\"\n\t// A candidate whose product already ends the run while the ledger says\n\t// nothing (AC-022/T-20): refused, never re-run.\n\t| \"run-ledger-conflict\"\n\t// A read-only run that settled without any deliverable (AC-006): the worker\n\t// recorded `needs-clarification` and emitted this alarm itself, with the\n\t// ledger root pinned to the true `.agenticdoc` (never `<key>/workers`).\n\t| \"no-product\"\n\t// Residual write-guard risk (AC-007/T-03): a writeless+shell worker was\n\t// allowed through by contract on a target that is not statically\n\t// determinable (`allow-unknown`) while its basename still names a deny-list\n\t// artifact (`pm-state.md`, `_workers*`). The guard itself cannot block;\n\t// observability is the only remaining defence (design DD-08).\n\t| \"write-scope-risk\"\n\t// A registered key whose repair evidence is STALE (T-24/C-30): the index row\n\t// is `idle`/`done` (or its claim is an old legacy Claim-Id) and the key's own\n\t// state documents have not moved in the freshness window. C-30 measured the\n\t// framework treating an`idle` key's months-old worker dirs as undispatched\n\t// work and queuing them claim-free. Such a key is NEVER repaired — repairing\n\t// a foreign idle key is exactly the cross-key pollution C-30 exposed — and\n\t// only one neutral notice is emitted (key, judged work, why not repaired).\n\t| \"orphan-repair-skipped\"\n\t// A write-face gate refusal consumed on the PM dispatch path (AC-003/D-008,\n\t// card T-W-I13): the caller saw a `DispatchOutcome` with `ok: false`, did NOT\n\t// count the task as queued, and turned it into a durable ledger row. It is\n\t// PER TASK, so unlike the scan-level refusal kinds it must never be deduped\n\t// per session — every refused task has to leave its own trace.\n\t| \"write-face-refusal\"\n\t// Consecutive model-error terminals under one owned project key (AC-006,\n\t// design §3.4/D7): K=2 or more worker runs of the same key ended with\n\t// model-unavailable evidence. PERCEPTION ONLY — this key deliberately does\n\t// NOT block or alter any re-dispatch decision (blocking the automatic\n\t// conductor loop is the separate stalled-gate idea, design D7 option B). NOT\n\t// a refusal: nothing was refused, the PM is being told the model layer keeps\n\t// failing underneath it.\n\t| \"model-error\"\n\t// DP-1 pre-dispatch triage produced an advisory suggestion (mw-jev-provider-\n\t// integration T-03, design D-005 item 3): recorded for every produced advice,\n\t// never a decision input. The summary rides `detail`; the PM is woken by a\n\t// separate `deliverPmAlert` ONLY when the suggestion disagrees with the\n\t// dispatched type (and `points.dp1.alert_on_disagreement !== false`).\n\t| \"triage-suggestion\"\n\t// DP-1 could not produce a suggestion (disabled is NOT this kind — disabled is\n\t// a complete bypass). Recorded only when `triage_notify_on_unavailable=true`;\n\t// the dispatch proceeds unchanged and the PM is never woken by it.\n\t| \"triage-unavailable\";\n\nexport interface DispatchAlarm {\n\tkind: DispatchAlarmKind;\n\tcount: number;\n\tdetail?: string;\n}\n\n/** Alarm kinds that are NOT refusals — the scan made a scope/ownership\n * observation. Their text must stay neutral (`[mw] dispatch 提示：…`); only\n * real refusal kinds may say `[mw] dispatch 已拒绝：…` (AC-011/T-19). */\nexport const NOTICE_DISPATCH_ALARM_KINDS: ReadonlySet<DispatchAlarmKind> = new Set([\n\t\"out-of-scope\",\n\t\"orphaned-keys\",\n\t\"orphan-repair-skipped\",\n\t// AC-006: a run of model-error terminals refuses nothing — it is an\n\t// observation about the model layer, so its text must read as `提示`.\n\t\"model-error\",\n\t// T-03: DP-1 triage rows refuse nothing — the advice is advisory and the\n\t// unavailable notice is informational, so both read as `提示`.\n\t\"triage-suggestion\",\n\t\"triage-unavailable\",\n]);\n\n/** Is this alarm a notice (neutral wording) rather than a refusal? */\nexport function isNoticeDispatchAlarm(kind: DispatchAlarmKind): boolean {\n\treturn NOTICE_DISPATCH_ALARM_KINDS.has(kind);\n}\n\n/** Autopilot ledger path (shared with the Python conductor). */\nconst AUTO_DECISIONS_FILE = \"auto-decisions.jsonl\";\n\n/** One-line human text for a refused dispatch scan (AC-020/AC-021). Notice\n * kinds carry neutral wording; the verdict prefix is added by\n * {@link formatDispatchAlarm} (AC-011/T-19). */\nexport function describeDispatchAlarm(alarm: DispatchAlarm): string {\n\tswitch (alarm.kind) {\n\t\tcase \"queue-rows-unparsable\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} unreadable row(s) in _workers.parallel — dispatch refused (fix the row; nothing was queued)${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"queue-unreadable\":\n\t\t\treturn `the queue looks empty while the work has already run (key ${alarm.detail ?? \"?\"}) — dispatch refused instead of re-running ${\n\t\t\t\talarm.count\n\t\t\t} task(s)`;\n\t\tcase \"dispatch-quota\":\n\t\t\treturn `scan quota reached after ${alarm.count} task(s) — the rest of this scan was refused`;\n\t\tcase \"out-of-scope\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} key(s) with undispatched work but no owner record, outside this window's write scope (${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ?? \"?\"\n\t\t\t}) — scanned read-only, nothing written. Action required: register the key first (switch_key <key> or dispatch_worker(key=<key>)), then dispatch; its work sits in {key}/workers/<task-key>/task.md`;\n\t\tcase \"orphaned-keys\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} orphaned key(s) with undispatched work, no live claim and no live run (${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ?? \"?\"\n\t\t\t}) — claim-free repair dispatch applied (the conductor stays eligible); no _index.parallel claim was written`;\n\t\tcase \"orphan-repair-skipped\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} key(s) with work but stale owner evidence — claim-free repair skipped, nothing written (${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ?? \"?\"\n\t\t\t})`;\n\t\tcase \"run-ledger-conflict\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} task(s) already have a terminal run.json while the queue has no row for them — not re-queued${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"no-product\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} read-only run(s) settled without a product — needs-clarification, awaiting human judgement${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"write-scope-risk\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} write-scope residual-risk row(s) (blocked=false, risk=deny-basename)${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? ` on ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t} — the guard allowed them by contract; review the audited target`;\n\t\tcase \"write-face-refusal\":\n\t\t\treturn `write_face gate refused ${alarm.count} task(s)${alarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"} — not queued`;\n\t\tcase \"model-error\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} consecutive worker run(s) ended with model-unavailable evidence${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? ` (latest: ${alarm.detail})` : \"\"\n\t\t\t} — the same key keeps settling against a failing model; check the provider route/credential or the fallback model list before the next dispatch`;\n\t\tcase \"triage-suggestion\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} pre-dispatch triage suggestion(s), advisory only — the dispatch type/role/model were NOT changed${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"triage-unavailable\":\n\t\t\treturn `pre-dispatch triage produced no suggestion — dispatch proceeds unchanged${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? ` (${alarm.detail})` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t}\n}\n\n/** The full PM alert line for one alarm (AC-011/T-19): only real refusal kinds\n * carry the `已拒绝` verdict — a notice (`out-of-scope` / `orphaned-keys`) says\n * `提示` and never reads as a refusal. */\nexport function formatDispatchAlarm(alarm: DispatchAlarm): string {\n\tconst verdict = isNoticeDispatchAlarm(alarm.kind) ? \"提示\" : \"已拒绝\";\n\treturn `[mw] dispatch ${verdict}：${describeDispatchAlarm(alarm)}`;\n}\n\n/** Append one machine-readable alarm row to the autopilot ledger\n * (`.agenticdoc/_autopilot/auto-decisions.jsonl`, AC-020/AC-021). The shape\n * mirrors the Python single writer (`conductor._append_auto_decision_row`):\n * one JSON object per line, 1-based `seq`. Decision consumers filter on\n * `phase == \"decide\"`, so `phase: \"dispatch-alarm\"` is invisible to them while\n * staying visible to humans, `mw doctor` and later consumers. Best-effort by\n * design: losing the alarm must never break dispatch. */\nexport function recordDispatchAlarm(agenticdocRoot: string, alarm: DispatchAlarm): void {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst ledger = path.join(agenticdocRoot, \"_autopilot\", AUTO_DECISIONS_FILE);\n\t\tlet seq = 1;\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tseq =\n\t\t\t\tfs\n\t\t\t\t\t.readFileSync(ledger, \"utf8\")\n\t\t\t\t\t.split(\"\\n\")\n\t\t\t\t\t.filter((l) => l.trim() !== \"\").length + 1;\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\tseq = 1;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst row = { seq, phase: \"dispatch-alarm\", kind: alarm.kind, count: alarm.count, detail: alarm.detail ?? \"\" };\n\t\tfs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(ledger), { recursive: true });\n\t\tfs.appendFileSync(ledger, `${JSON.stringify(row)}\\n`, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch (err) {\n\t\tconsole.error(`[mw] dispatch alarm not recorded: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Count the write-guard residual-risk audit rows in one worker trace\n * (AC-007/T-03): `[WRITE_SCOPE]` lines carrying BOTH `blocked=false` and\n * `risk=deny-basename`. The filter is deliberately the two-field pair and never\n * `rule=allow-unknown` alone (design-write-guard-landing §5.5): the unknown tier\n * is the contract, the deny-list basename is the residual risk. Best-effort — a\n * missing/unreadable trace is zero, never an error. */\nexport function countWriteScopeResidualRisks(taskDir: string): number {\n\tlet raw: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\traw = fs.readFileSync(path.join(taskDir, \"trace.log\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tlet count = 0;\n\tfor (const line of raw.split(\"\\n\")) {\n\t\tif (!line.startsWith(\"[WRITE_SCOPE] \")) continue;\n\t\tif (!line.includes(\"blocked=false\")) continue;\n\t\tif (!line.includes(\"risk=deny-basename\")) continue;\n\t\tcount += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn count;\n}\n\n/** PM-side exit for the write-guard residual risk (AC-007/DD-08): the worker\n * was allowed through by contract, so the ledger row is the remaining defence.\n * Reuses the single dispatch-alarm channel and its unchanged row shape; returns\n * the number of residual-risk rows found (0 ⇒ nothing written). */\nexport function recordWriteScopeResidualRisks(agenticdocRoot: string, taskKey: string, taskDir: string): number {\n\tconst count = countWriteScopeResidualRisks(taskDir);\n\tif (count === 0) return 0;\n\trecordDispatchAlarm(agenticdocRoot, { kind: \"write-scope-risk\", count, detail: taskKey });\n\treturn count;\n}\n\n/** Exit-Reason prefix every model-exhausted worker writes (design §4; the\n * worker-side T-01 half of this key). */\nexport const MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_PREFIX = \"model unavailable:\";\n\n/** Consecutive model-error terminals before the PM records one `model-error`\n * alarm (AC-006; K=2 per design §3.4/D7). */\nexport const MODEL_ERROR_STREAK_K = 2;\n\n/** `run.json.model_exhausted === true` (design §4: the worker sets it on the\n * model-exhausted terminal, exit 3). Read raw rather than through the shared\n * `RunState` type because that field is added by the worker protocol (T-01) and\n * `shared/run-store.ts` is not this file's write face; a missing, unreadable or\n * malformed record is simply `false` (never throws — the poll loop calls this\n * on every terminal row). */\nexport function runModelExhausted(taskDir: string): boolean {\n\tlet raw: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\traw = fs.readFileSync(path.join(taskDir, RUN_FILE_NAME), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(raw);\n\t\tif (typeof parsed !== \"object\" || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) return false;\n\t\treturn (parsed as { model_exhausted?: unknown }).model_exhausted === true;\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Does this terminal run carry model-unavailable evidence (AC-006/design\n * §3.4)? Two independent sources, OR'd: the worker's own\n * `run.json.model_exhausted` flag and the `## Exit Reason` body starting with\n * `model unavailable:`. Reading failures degrade to `false`, never throw. */\nexport function isModelErrorTerminal(taskDir: string): boolean {\n\tif (runModelExhausted(taskDir)) return true;\n\tconst reason = readLastProductSectionBody(taskDir, [\"Exit Reason\"]);\n\treturn (reason ?? \"\").trimStart().startsWith(MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_PREFIX);\n}\n\n/** Bump (model-error) or clear (every other terminal) one key's consecutive\n * model-error streak. The pure half of AC-006, exported so tests can drive the\n * sequence without standing up the poll loop. */\nexport function bumpModelErrorStreak(streaks: Map<string, number>, key: string, modelError: boolean): number {\n\tif (!modelError) {\n\t\tstreaks.delete(key);\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tconst next = (streaks.get(key) ?? 0) + 1;\n\tstreaks.set(key, next);\n\treturn next;\n}\n\n/** PM-side model-error perception for one terminal worker row (AC-006, design\n * §3.4/D7). Called once per terminal transition on the poll loop's ownership\n * branch: bumps the owning key's streak, clears it on any non-model-error\n * terminal, and records ONE `model-error` alarm row through the single\n * dispatch-alarm channel once the streak reaches {@link MODEL_ERROR_STREAK_K}.\n * `detail` is the task key of the terminal that triggered the alarm. PERCEPTION\n * ONLY: the return value is never used to block or alter a re-dispatch. */\nexport function recordModelErrorTerminal(\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tstreakKey: string,\n\ttaskKey: string,\n\ttaskDir: string,\n\tstreaks: Map<string, number>,\n): number {\n\tconst count = bumpModelErrorStreak(streaks, streakKey, isModelErrorTerminal(taskDir));\n\tif (count < MODEL_ERROR_STREAK_K) return count;\n\trecordDispatchAlarm(agenticdocRoot, { kind: \"model-error\", count, detail: taskKey });\n\treturn count;\n}\n\n// ── Decision correlation: settle rows (T-08 / spec §6.2, design D-013) ─────\n\n/** `settle.outcome` vocabulary of the archive (`decide_archive._OUTCOMES`). */\nexport type DecisionSettleOutcome = \"pending\" | \"ok\" | \"rework\" | \"rollback\" | \"inconclusive\";\n\n/** One `kind=settle` row to append — the exact argument set of\n * `decide_archive.append_settle` (dp is derived from the decision id).\n *\n * `evidenceRef` carries the run id `<task_key>@<iso>` (`run.json.run_id`): it is\n * the per-run half of the `(decision_id, outcome, run_id)` idempotency key and\n * the only place the frozen row contract can carry it (there is no `run_id`\n * field). */\nexport interface DecisionSettleRow {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\tdp: string;\n\tkey: string;\n\ttaskKey: string | null;\n\toutcome: DecisionSettleOutcome;\n\tsettledBy: \"pm-auto\" | \"human\";\n\tevidenceRef: string | null;\n\tnote: string | null;\n}\n\n/** Why a terminal row produced no settle row. `no-decision-header` is the\n * explicit non-association bucket demanded by spec §6.2 — PM-local decisions,\n * long-latency (dp10), composite attribution, worker-internal `tool_call`s and\n * cross-key spillover all land there and are NEVER guessed at. */\nexport type DecisionSettleSkipReason =\n\t| \"no-decision-header\"\n\t| \"needs-clarification\"\n\t| \"not-terminal\"\n\t| \"inconsistent-run\"\n\t| \"duplicate-settle\"\n\t| \"rollback-without-ok\"\n\t| \"unreadable-task-md\"\n\t| \"append-failed\";\n\nexport interface DecisionSettleSkip {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\treason: DecisionSettleSkipReason;\n}\n\n/** Mapping verdict for one terminal transition (6-state table of card T-08). */\nexport type DecisionSettleMapping =\n\t| { ok: true; outcome: DecisionSettleOutcome; note?: string }\n\t| { ok: false; reason: DecisionSettleSkipReason };\n\n/** The 6 terminal-state mapping (design D-013):\n *\n * | terminal | outcome |\n * | --- | --- |\n * | `done` (exit 0) | `ok` |\n * | `failed` | `rework` |\n * | `failed` + exit 3 / `model_exhausted` | `inconclusive` |\n * | `needs-clarification` | NO row (the human is the next settle subject) |\n * | `lost` | `pending` + `note=lost` |\n * | superseded (replacement landed) | `rollback` |\n *\n * `done` is `ok` without re-reading the contract sections: the worker folds the\n * contract verdict into the exit code (`evidence.delivered && gaps.ok ? 0 : 2`),\n * so a second PM-side oracle could only disagree with the run record. */\nexport function mapTerminalToSettle(input: {\n\tstatus: WorkerStatus;\n\t/** `run.json.exit`; undefined while unknown (`lost`, pre-terminal record). */\n\trunExit?: number;\n\t/** `isModelErrorTerminal(taskDir)`: exit 3 / `model unavailable:` evidence. */\n\tmodelError: boolean;\n}): DecisionSettleMapping {\n\tswitch (input.status) {\n\t\tcase \"done\":\n\t\t\tif (input.runExit !== undefined && input.runExit !== 0) {\n\t\t\t\t// Contradictory record (status says delivered, exit says otherwise): do not\n\t\t\t\t// invent an outcome; leave the decision pending and report the anomaly.\n\t\t\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"inconsistent-run\" };\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn { ok: true, outcome: \"ok\" };\n\t\tcase \"failed\":\n\t\t\t// exit 3 / model_exhausted never says anything about the work: it stays out\n\t\t\t// of the denominator instead of counting as rework.\n\t\t\treturn input.modelError || input.runExit === 3\n\t\t\t\t? { ok: true, outcome: \"inconclusive\" }\n\t\t\t\t: { ok: true, outcome: \"rework\" };\n\t\tcase \"lost\":\n\t\t\t// Process gone, result unknown: the explicit registration row is what closes\n\t\t\t// the correlation loop (without it the archive reads \"still running\" forever).\n\t\t\treturn { ok: true, outcome: \"pending\", note: \"lost\" };\n\t\tcase \"needs-clarification\":\n\t\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"needs-clarification\" };\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"not-terminal\" };\n\t}\n}\n\n/** `<dp>:<trigger_id>` split on the FIRST `:` (design D-023: trigger ids may\n * contain `:`, dp ids are kebab-case registry ids). Rejects empty halves and\n * any whitespace so a free-text value can never become a decision id. */\nexport function splitDecisionId(decisionId: string): { dp: string; triggerId: string } | undefined {\n\tconst at = decisionId.indexOf(\":\");\n\tif (at <= 0 || at === decisionId.length - 1) return undefined;\n\tif (/\\s/.test(decisionId)) return undefined;\n\treturn { dp: decisionId.slice(0, at), triggerId: decisionId.slice(at + 1) };\n}\n\n/** One settle row already in the archive (the fields the fold needs). */\nexport interface DecisionSettleRecord {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\toutcome: string;\n\trunId: string | null;\n}\n\n/** Read the settle rows of the decision archive, tolerating foreign/broken\n * lines (a half-written tail row is not this reader's error). Returns `[]` when\n * the archive does not exist yet. */\nexport function readDecisionSettles(archivePath: string): DecisionSettleRecord[] {\n\tlet content: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tcontent = fs.readFileSync(archivePath, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn [];\n\t}\n\tconst rows: DecisionSettleRecord[] = [];\n\tfor (const line of content.split(\"\\n\")) {\n\t\tif (line.trim() === \"\") continue;\n\t\tlet parsed: unknown;\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tparsed = JSON.parse(line);\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (typeof parsed !== \"object\" || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) continue;\n\t\tconst row = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;\n\t\tif (row.kind !== \"settle\") continue;\n\t\tif (typeof row.decision_id !== \"string\" || typeof row.outcome !== \"string\") continue;\n\t\trows.push({\n\t\t\tdecisionId: row.decision_id,\n\t\t\toutcome: row.outcome,\n\t\t\trunId: typeof row.evidence_ref === \"string\" && row.evidence_ref !== \"\" ? row.evidence_ref : null,\n\t\t});\n\t}\n\treturn rows;\n}\n\n/** Decide whether one settle row may be appended (pure): idempotency on\n * `(decision_id, outcome, run_id)` (a PM restart replay writes nothing) and the\n * `rollback` ordering rule (a rollback only exists for a decision that already\n * settled `ok` — otherwise it would fabricate a reversal that never happened).\n * Multiple settles per decision ARE legal: the fold takes the LAST one, which is\n * the only way `ok → rollback` can ever be recorded (design D-013). */\nexport function planDecisionSettle(input: {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\townerKey: string;\n\ttaskKey: string | null;\n\trunId: string | null;\n\toutcome: DecisionSettleOutcome;\n\tnote?: string;\n\tprior: readonly DecisionSettleRecord[];\n}): { ok: true; row: DecisionSettleRow } | { ok: false; reason: DecisionSettleSkipReason } {\n\tconst split = splitDecisionId(input.decisionId);\n\tif (!split) return { ok: false, reason: \"no-decision-header\" };\n\t// Both rules are per DECISION: another decision settling `ok` on the same run\n\t// says nothing about this one (and must not license a rollback for it).\n\tconst prior = input.prior.filter((row) => row.decisionId === input.decisionId);\n\tif (input.outcome === \"rollback\" && !prior.some((row) => row.outcome === \"ok\")) {\n\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"rollback-without-ok\" };\n\t}\n\tif (prior.some((row) => row.outcome === input.outcome && row.runId === input.runId)) {\n\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"duplicate-settle\" };\n\t}\n\treturn {\n\t\tok: true,\n\t\trow: {\n\t\t\tdecisionId: input.decisionId,\n\t\t\tdp: split.dp,\n\t\t\tkey: input.ownerKey,\n\t\t\ttaskKey: input.taskKey,\n\t\t\toutcome: input.outcome,\n\t\t\tsettledBy: \"pm-auto\",\n\t\t\tevidenceRef: input.runId,\n\t\t\tnote: input.note ?? null,\n\t\t},\n\t};\n}\n\n/** Append implementation for one settle row (injected in tests). */\nexport type DecisionSettleAppender = (row: DecisionSettleRow) => { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string };\n\n/** In-process delegate to the archive's SINGLE writer (`decide_archive.py`):\n * no `mw decide settle` subcommand exists yet, so the interpreter imports the\n * module and `append_settle` receives the row as JSON on stdin (state is never\n * argv — the same rule `mw decide run` follows). Delegating, instead of\n * re-implementing the `prev_sha` chain, the lock and the row validation here,\n * keeps exactly one writer for `decisions.jsonl` (design §2.7 / D2-S0). */\nconst APPEND_SETTLE_PROGRAM = [\n\t\"import sys, json, pathlib\",\n\t\"sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])\",\n\t\"import decide_archive\",\n\t\"payload = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())\",\n\t\"decide_archive.append_settle(\",\n\t\"    pathlib.Path(payload['archive_path']),\",\n\t\"    decision_id=payload['decision_id'],\",\n\t\"    dp=payload['dp'],\",\n\t\"    key=payload['key'],\",\n\t\"    task_key=payload['task_key'],\",\n\t\"    outcome=payload['outcome'],\",\n\t\"    settled_by=payload['settled_by'],\",\n\t\"    evidence_ref=payload['evidence_ref'],\",\n\t\"    note=payload['note'],\",\n\t\")\",\n].join(\"\\n\");\n\nfunction archiveSettleAppender(archivePath: string): DecisionSettleAppender {\n\treturn (row) => {\n\t\tconst mwPy = findMwPy();\n\t\tif (!mwPy) return { ok: false, error: \"mw.py not found\" };\n\t\tconst payload = JSON.stringify({\n\t\t\tarchive_path: archivePath,\n\t\t\tdecision_id: row.decisionId,\n\t\t\tdp: row.dp,\n\t\t\tkey: row.key,\n\t\t\ttask_key: row.taskKey,\n\t\t\toutcome: row.outcome,\n\t\t\tsettled_by: row.settledBy,\n\t\t\tevidence_ref: row.evidenceRef,\n\t\t\tnote: row.note,\n\t\t});\n\t\tconst result = spawnSync(PYTHON_EXE, [\"-X\", \"utf8\", \"-c\", APPEND_SETTLE_PROGRAM, path.dirname(mwPy)], {\n\t\t\tinput: payload,\n\t\t\tencoding: \"utf8\",\n\t\t\ttimeout: 20_000,\n\t\t\twindowsHide: true,\n\t\t});\n\t\tif (result.error) return { ok: false, error: result.error.message };\n\t\tif (result.status !== 0) {\n\t\t\treturn { ok: false, error: (result.stderr ?? \"\").trim() || `exit ${result.status ?? \"?\"}` };\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn { ok: true };\n\t};\n}\n\n/** Test seams for the settle path (production passes none). */\nexport interface DecisionSettleHooks {\n\t/** Archive path; defaults to `<agenticdocRoot>/_autopilot/decisions.jsonl`. */\n\tarchivePath?: string;\n\t/** Append implementation; defaults to {@link archiveSettleAppender}. */\n\tappend?: DecisionSettleAppender;\n\t/** Run-state reader; defaults to `readRunState`. */\n\treadRun?: (taskDir: string) => ReturnType<typeof readRunState>;\n\t/** Model-terminal probe; defaults to `isModelErrorTerminal`. */\n\tmodelError?: (taskDir: string) => boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface DecisionSettleResult {\n\twritten: DecisionSettleRow[];\n\tskipped: DecisionSettleSkip[];\n}\n\n/** Settle the decision one terminal worker row executes (spec §6.2 / D-013).\n *\n * Called once per terminal transition from the poll loop (the `notified` set is\n * the per-task-per-session bound, exactly like `recordWriteScopeResidualRisks` /\n * `recordModelErrorTerminal` next to it). The decision id is reverse-looked up\n * from the task's own `decision:` head line; a task without one stays\n * un-associated (never guessed). A `supersedes:` task that settled `ok` also\n * records the `rollback` of the decision it replaced. Fail-soft: an unwritable\n * archive is reported in the result, never thrown into the poll loop. */\nexport function recordDecisionSettle(\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\townerKey: string,\n\tentry: Pick<WorkerEntry, \"taskKey\" | \"status\">,\n\ttaskDir: string,\n\thooks: DecisionSettleHooks = {},\n): DecisionSettleResult {\n\tconst result: DecisionSettleResult = { written: [], skipped: [] };\n\tlet taskContent: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\ttaskContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(taskDir, \"task.md\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"unreadable-task-md\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\tconst decisionId = (readTaskHeaderScalar(taskContent, \"decision\") ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (decisionId === \"\") {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"no-decision-header\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\tconst readRun = hooks.readRun ?? readRunState;\n\tconst run = readRun(taskDir);\n\tconst mapping = mapTerminalToSettle({\n\t\tstatus: entry.status,\n\t\trunExit: run?.exit,\n\t\tmodelError: (hooks.modelError ?? isModelErrorTerminal)(taskDir),\n\t});\n\tif (!mapping.ok) {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId, reason: mapping.reason });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\n\tconst archivePath = hooks.archivePath ?? path.join(agenticdocRoot, \"_autopilot\", \"decisions.jsonl\");\n\tconst append = hooks.append ?? archiveSettleAppender(archivePath);\n\tconst appendOne = (\n\t\ttargetDecisionId: string,\n\t\ttargetTaskKey: string | null,\n\t\trunId: string | null,\n\t\toutcome: DecisionSettleOutcome,\n\t\tnote?: string,\n\t): void => {\n\t\tconst plan = planDecisionSettle({\n\t\t\tdecisionId: targetDecisionId,\n\t\t\townerKey,\n\t\t\ttaskKey: targetTaskKey,\n\t\t\trunId,\n\t\t\toutcome,\n\t\t\tnote,\n\t\t\t// Re-read per append: the rollback leg must see the `ok` settle this same\n\t\t\t// call may have just written, and a restarted PM must see the whole file.\n\t\t\tprior: readDecisionSettles(archivePath),\n\t\t});\n\t\tif (!plan.ok) {\n\t\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: targetDecisionId, reason: plan.reason });\n\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst written = append(plan.row);\n\t\tif (!written.ok) {\n\t\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: targetDecisionId, reason: \"append-failed\" });\n\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t}\n\t\tresult.written.push(plan.row);\n\t};\n\n\tappendOne(decisionId, entry.taskKey, run?.run_id ?? null, mapping.outcome, mapping.note);\n\n\t// Rollback leg (design D-013): `supersedes:` is the only way to replace a\n\t// finished run. Recorded only when the replacement actually landed (`ok`) — a\n\t// half-failed re-dispatch must not rewrite a decision that is still in force.\n\tconst superseded = (parseSupersedes(taskContent) ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (superseded === \"\" || mapping.outcome !== \"ok\") return result;\n\tconst supersededDir = path.join(path.dirname(taskDir), superseded);\n\tlet supersededContent: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tsupersededContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(supersededDir, \"task.md\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"unreadable-task-md\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\tconst supersededDecisionId = (readTaskHeaderScalar(supersededContent, \"decision\") ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (supersededDecisionId === \"\") {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"no-decision-header\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\t// The rollback belongs to the REPLACED run: its task key and its run id (the\n\t// idempotency discriminator), so a re-dispatch can never dedupe against the\n\t// replacement's settle.\n\tappendOne(supersededDecisionId, superseded, readRun(supersededDir)?.run_id ?? null, \"rollback\");\n\treturn result;\n}\n\n/** The one-line ledger detail for a PM-side write-face refusal (AC-003/D-008).\n * `DispatchRefusal.reason` is byte-identical to the conductor's\n * `DispatchResult.reason`, so it already carries the stable refusal `code`, the\n * `overlap-with:<task_key>` pair and the conflict `sample` when the gate could\n * prove one. The refused task key prefixes it because the alarm row has no key\n * column of its own. */\nexport function writeFaceRefusalDetail(taskKey: string, refusal: DispatchRefusal): string {\n\treturn `${taskKey}: ${refusal.reason}`;\n}\n\n/** Consume one non-ok `DispatchOutcome` on the PM dispatch path (AC-003/D-008,\n * card T-W-I13): the refusal is a zero-side-effect return value, so the caller\n * must NOT count the task as queued. It is turned into a durable ledger row\n * through the single {@link recordDispatchAlarm} channel (best-effort by\n * design: a lossy audit must never break dispatch) plus a short human-visible\n * PM alert. The two are deliberately separate — the alert is not the audit. */\nfunction reportWriteFaceRefusal(\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\ttaskKey: string,\n\trefusal: DispatchRefusal,\n\tonRefusal?: (text: string) => void,\n): void {\n\tconst alarm: DispatchAlarm = {\n\t\tkind: \"write-face-refusal\",\n\t\tcount: 1,\n\t\tdetail: writeFaceRefusalDetail(taskKey, refusal),\n\t};\n\trecordDispatchAlarm(agenticdocRoot, alarm);\n\tonRefusal?.(formatDispatchAlarm(alarm));\n}\n\n/** Single-scan dispatch quota (AC-021). A scan that wants to queue more rows\n * than this is looking at something it does not understand (IN-3 queued 252 in\n * one scan and the launcher spawned 66 workers at once). */\nexport const DEFAULT_DISPATCH_MAX_PER_SCAN = 3;\n\n/** `dispatch_max_per_scan` from the project's autopilot config (D-026/AC-021).\n *\n * An explicit `DispatchScanOptions.maxPerScan` wins (tests and refreshers);\n * otherwise the project config decides. \",…\" : \"\"}`,\n\t\t\t});\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (runRefused.length > 0) {\n\t\t\t// Aggregate, bounded: the PM needs to see WHICH tasks and WHY (the\n\t\t\t// distinct reasons are what tells a stale ledger from a live run),\n\t\t\t// without one ledger row per candidate.\n\t\t\tconst reasons = [...new Set(runRefused.map((r) => r.reason))].sort().join(\",\");\n\t\t\tconst shown = runRefused\n\t\t\t\t.slice(0, 3)\n\t\t\t\t.map((r) => `${r.taskKey}:${r.reason}${r.detail ? Exceeding the\n\t\t\t// quota means the scan is looking at something it does not understand,\n\t\t\t// not that hundreds of tasks need running.\n\t\t\tif (queued >= maxPerScan) {\n\t\t\t\tflushScanAlarms();\n\t\t\t\topts.onAlarm?.({ kind: \"dispatch-quota\", count: queued });\n\t\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst taskContent = fs.readFileSync(taskMdPath, \"utf8\");\n\t\t\tconst { cli, provider } = pickWorkerRoute(taskContent);\n\t\t\tconst model = readModel(taskContent);\n\t\t\ttry {\n\t\t\t\tconst outcome = await dispatchTask(\n\t\t\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\t\t\ttaskKey,\n\t\t\t\t\t\tstatus: \"pending\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcli,\n\t\t\t\t\t\tprovider,\n\t\t\t\t\t\tmodel,\n\t\t\t\t\t\ttaskPath: taskMdPath,\n\t\t\t\t\t},\n\t\t\t\t\tworkerStore,\n\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t\tif (outcome.ok) {\n\t\t\t\t\tqueued += 1;\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t// AC-003/D-008: a write-face refusal is a return value, not a\n\t\t\t\t\t// throw — counting it as queued would both falsify the quota and\n\t\t\t\t\t// leave the refusal without any durable trace.\n\t\t\t\t\treportWriteFaceRefusal(agenticdocRoot, taskKey, outcome, opts.onRefusal);\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} catch (err) {\n\t\t\t\t// Fail-closed (mw-dual-workspace AC-007): an unusable target.yml\n\t\t\t\t// must never silently degrade to an un-injected task.md — the task\n\t\t\t\t// stays undispatched and is retried on the next scan once the\n\t\t\t\t// config is fixed.
