Preference order: exact [START]→[END]\n * interval from trace.log (present on every new-bundle terminal task), ≥2\n * [HEARTBEAT] lines (older format), then the queue row's dispatchedAt→updatedAt\n * (coarse but always present). Empty when nothing is derivable. */\nfunction heartbeatStatsSuffix(taskDir: string, entry: WorkerEntry): string {\n\tconst prog = readTaskProgress(taskDir);\n\tif (prog?.startTs && prog.endTs) {\n\t\tconst durMs = Math.max(0, Date.parse(prog.endTs) - Date.parse(prog.startTs));\n\t\tconst ph = prog.endPhases && prog.endPhases !== \"-\" ? `, ph ${prog.endPhases}` : \"\";\n\t\treturn ` (${formatHeartbeatAge(durMs)}${ph})`;\n\t}\n\tconst hb = prog?.heartbeat;\n\tif (hb && hb.count >= 2) {\n\t\tconst durMs = Math.max(0, Date.parse(hb.lastTs) - Date.parse(hb.firstTs));\n\t\tconst ph = hb.phase === \"-\" ? \"\" : `, ph ${hb.phase}/${hb.phaseTotal}`;\n\t\treturn ` (${formatHeartbeatAge(durMs)}${ph})`;\n\t}\n\tconst durMs = Date.parse(entry.updatedAt) - Date.parse(entry.dispatchedAt);\n\tif (!Number.isNaN(durMs) && durMs > 0) return ` (${formatHeartbeatAge(durMs)})`;\n\treturn \"\";\n}\n\n/** Session entry type recording a delivered gate reminder. Read back on\n * restart/resume so the same ledger row is never pushed twice (design D-010).\n * Same mechanism as WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE / AUTOPILOT_SEEN_ENTRY_TYPE. */\nexport const GATE_REMINDER_ENTRY_TYPE = \"agent-team-loop:gate-reminder-seen\";\n\n/** Session entry type recording a DROPPED gate reminder (mw-autopilot-gate-\n * alarm-liveness AC-010): \"no watch\", \"other key\" and \"read error\" drops must\n * leave a visible record, never vanish silently. Deduplicated per `${gateId}:${n}:${reason}` for this process:\n * the poll loop runs every 4 s, so an undeduped drop would append an entry per\n * tick forever. `reason` is one of the three literal drop causes. */\nexport function recordDroppedGateReminder(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\tseen: Set<string>,\n\treminder: { gateId: string; reminderN: number; gateKey: string },\n\treason: \"no-watch\" | \"other-key\" | \"read-error\",\n\terror?: string,\n): void {\n\tconst dedup = `${reminder.gateId}:${reminder.reminderN}:${reason}`;\n\tif (seen.has(dedup)) return;\n\tseen.add(dedup);\n\tpi.appendEntry(GATE_REMINDER_DROPPED_ENTRY_TYPE, {\n\t\tgateId: reminder.gateId,\n\t\tn: reminder.reminderN,\n\t\tgateKey: reminder.gateKey,\n\t\treason,\n\t\t...(error === undefined ? {} : { error }),\n\t});\n}\n\n// ── dp2 checkpoint narrowing (mw-decision-substitution T-07; design D-011) ──\n//\n// The divergence escalation below wakes the PM (triggerTurn) at the first\n// mid/high convergence checkpoint of a running worker. dp2 lets a service\n// answer substitute for that wake — but ONLY with the one action that is\n// reversible, machine-decidable, local and free: narrowing the remaining scope\n// (D-011). `split` (kill + re-dispatch, a new task-ledger entry) and\n// `direct-exec` (PM takes over, bypassing the worker's process/write-face\n// isolation) change the goal or widen the authorization surface, so they stay\n// human decisions and take the UNCHANGED escalation path.\n//\n// Three closed states must stay behaviourally identical to pre-dp2 (design\n// D-007 / AC-015):\n//   - `.mw/decide.json` missing or `enabled != true` → complete bypass: no\n//     spawn, no write (the only I/O is that one config probe);\n//   - `.mw/decide-points.json` row `enabled=false` / unusable row → same bypass\n//     for dp2 only (the table is the single authority, machines never write it);\n//   - `mode=suggest` → Python still records the answer, but this hook NEVER acts\n//     on it; the alert still wakes the PM (AC-015).\n//\n// Every degraded answer (unavailable / missing `checkpoint_action` / an unknown\n// value) is fail-closed onto the original alert. The worker\n * consumes it at its next checkpoint tick (design §5.3: file transport keeps\n * coordination file-driven and the PM the single writer). */\nexport const DP2_STEER_FILE = \"steer-dp2.md\";\n\n/** Attribution marker of the narrowed-scope steer (the worker injects it as a\n * followUp; kept here so the request file and its consumer cannot drift). */\nexport const DP2_NARROW_MARKER = \"[mw dp2-narrow]\";\n\n/** Machine header line of the request file (first line of `steer-dp2.md`).\n * Exported so the worker-side consumer strips exactly what this side wrote. */\nexport const DP2_STEER_REQUEST_HEADER = \"[dp2-narrow-request]\";\n\n/** Appended to the PM alert when dp2 answered `narrow` but the worker can no\n * longer act on a steer (T-07b fallback, DS-4: never fail open). */\nexport const DP2_NARROW_FALLBACK_LINE = \"[dp2-narrow-fallback] task not running; escalated instead\";\n\n/** dp2 question set in the canonical form Python hashes: `json.dumps(list(\n * questions), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"))`\n * (decision_points.py::_questions_version). */\nconst DP2_QUESTIONS_CANONICAL =\n\t'[{\"choices\":[\"narrow\",\"split\",\"direct-exec\",\"escalate\"],\"id\":\"checkpoint_action\",\"type\":\"choice\"}]';\n\n/** `questions_version` for dp2 = `q-<sha256(canonical questions)[:8]>`, i.e. the\n * exact short code the Python registry derives (D-026). This read exists ONLY so the PM does\n * not pay for a `mw decide run` child that Python would reject — zero-spawn\n * short-circuit, nothing else. `mode`, `acted` and `decision_id` come from the\n * child payload, never from here, and when this pre-read and Python disagree\n * PYTHON WINS. Read-only (AC-010: machines never write the table).\n *\n * `source`: `default` = no table / no row (registry default for a P2 point),\n * `config` = a usable row, `invalid` = the row is present but its L2/L3/L5\n * parse degrades it (Python `force_off`). */\nexport interface Dp2Authorization {\n\tenabled: boolean;\n\tsource: \"default\" | \"config\" | \"invalid\";\n}\n\n/** Mirror of the `force_off` half of `decision_points.py::_parse_row`\n * (decision_points.py:884-968): a row that is not an object (L2) — handled by\n * the caller — or whose `mode`/`note`/`tier` is not a string of the accepted\n * shape, or whose `enabled` is not a boolean (L3/L5), is `enabled=false` for\n * that dp only.\n *\n * Deliberately NOT force-off: L4 (tier value outside P0|P1|P2) and L7 (tier\n * differs from the registry) are advisory — the registry tier wins and the row\n * stays enabled, exactly like `_parse_row`. If Python's rules change, THIS is\n * the one function to fix: Python is authoritative. */\nfunction dp2RowForceOff(row: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {\n\tif (\"mode\" in row && row.mode !== \"auto\" && row.mode !== \"suggest\") return true;\n\tif (\"note\" in row && typeof row.note !== \"string\") return true;\n\tif (\"tier\" in row && typeof row.tier !== \"string\") return true;\n\treturn \"enabled\" in row && typeof row.enabled !== \"boolean\";\n}\n\nexport function readDp2Authorization(projectDir: string): Dp2Authorization {\n\tconst fallback: Dp2Authorization = { enabled: true, source: \"default\" };\n\tlet raw: unknown;\n\ttry {\n\t\traw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(projectDir, \".mw\", \"decide-points.json\"), \"utf8\"));\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn fallback;\n\t}\n\t// L1 (unparsable file, or no `points` object): every dp keeps the registry\n\t// default, so dp2 (P2) stays enabled.\n\tconst points = recordOf(recordOf(raw)?.points);\n\tif (points === undefined || !Object.hasOwn(points, DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID)) return fallback;\n\t// L2: a present-but-non-object row forces dp2 OFF — Python never falls back\n\t// to the registry default for a row it could not parse as an object.\n\tconst row = recordOf(points[DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID]);\n\tif (row === undefined) return { enabled: false, source: \"invalid\" };\n\tif (dp2RowForceOff(row)) return { enabled: false, source: \"invalid\" };\n\t// A usable row: `enabled` defaults to the registry default (P2 → true).\n\treturn { enabled: row.enabled !== false, source: \"config\" };\n}\n\nfunction recordOf(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {\n\treturn value !== null && typeof value === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(value)\n\t\t? (value as Record<string, unknown>)\n\t\t: undefined;\n}\n\n/** Code-point-safe UTF-8 clamp, mirroring the Python field budgets. */\nfunction clampUtf8(text: string, maxBytes: number): string {\n\tif (Buffer.byteLength(text, \"utf8\") <= maxBytes) return text;\n\tlet out = \"\";\n\tlet used = 0;\n\tfor (const char of text) {\n\t\tconst size = Buffer.byteLength(char, \"utf8\");\n\t\tif (used + size > maxBytes) break;\n\t\tout += char;\n\t\tused += size;\n\t}\n\treturn out;\n}\n\n/** One `context.artifact_status` entry (W6 / D-052..D-054). */\nexport interface Dp2ArtifactStatus {\n\tpath: string;\n\texists: boolean;\n\tbytes: number;\n}\n\n/** Machine fields of the checkpoint, 8 + 4 (design Q5): elapsed/reads/writes/\n * phases/uniq_targets/repeat_top/risk from the line plus the writeless landing\n * suffix (land/last_land/artifact/done). Reads ride in the trend only — the\n * frozen state table has no `progress.reads`. */\nexport interface Dp2CheckpointStateInput {\n\townerKey: string;\n\ttaskKey: string;\n\tphase: string;\n\ttaskType: string;\n\tbudgetMin: number;\n\tcheckpoint: CheckpointInfo;\n\ttrend: Dp2CheckpointPoint[];\n\t/** `context.artifact_status` rows (already fs-stated, ≤24 enforced here). */\n\tartifacts?: readonly Dp2ArtifactStatus[];\n}\n\n/** Build the dp2 structured state (spec §5.4 / D-019: L0/L1 only, ≤2000B).\n * Required fields come from `decision_points.REQUIRED_STATE_FIELDS[\"dp2-…\"]`:\n * universal 9 + `progress.elapsed_minutes/budget_minutes/phases_done/\n * phases_total/artifact_present`; the remaining counters and the trend are\n * optional L1. */\nexport function buildDp2CheckpointState(input: Dp2CheckpointStateInput): Record<string, unknown> {\n\tconst phases = splitPhaseProgress(input.checkpoint.phases);\n\tconst progress: Record<string, unknown> = {\n\t\telapsed_minutes: Math.max(0, Math.round(input.checkpoint.elapsedS / 60)),\n\t\tbudget_minutes: Math.max(1, Math.round(input.budgetMin)),\n\t\tphases_done: phases.done,\n\t\tphases_total: phases.total,\n\t\t// Writeless roles carry the landing suffix; a write role proves its artifact\n\t\t// by having written at all (old lines have no `artifact=` field).\n\t\tartifact_present: input.checkpoint.artifactPresent ?? input.checkpoint.writes > 0,\n\t\twrites: input.checkpoint.writes,\n\t\tuniq_targets: input.checkpoint.uniqTargets,\n\t\trepeat_top: input.checkpoint.repeatTop,\n\t\ttrend: input.trend.map((point) => ({\n\t\t\telapsed_minutes: point.elapsedMin,\n\t\t\treads: point.reads,\n\t\t\twrites: point.writes,\n\t\t})),\n\t};\n\tif (input.checkpoint.lastLandingS !== undefined) {\n\t\tprogress.last_land_age_min = Math.round(input.checkpoint.lastLandingS / 60);\n\t}\n\tconst contextSlots = DECIDE_REGISTRY[DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID]?.contextSlots ?? [];\n\tconst context: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n\tif (contextSlots.includes(\"change_summary\")) {\n\t\t// The summary is prose the model reads, not a decision field: one line,\n\t\t// capped at the slot's 600 chars, derived only from machine fields.\n\t\tconst lastLand =\n\t\t\ttypeof progress.last_land_age_min === \"number\" ? ` last_land_age=${progress.last_land_age_min}m` : \"\";\n\t\tcontext.change_summary = clampUtf8(\n\t\t\t`checkpoint elapsed=${progress.elapsed_minutes}m/${progress.budget_minutes}m ` +\n\t\t\t\t`phases=${progress.phases_done}/${progress.phases_total} writes=${progress.writes} ` +\n\t\t\t\t`artifact_present=${progress.artifact_present}${lastLand}`,\n\t\t\t600,\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tif (contextSlots.includes(\"artifact_status\") && (input.artifacts?.length ?? 0) > 0) {\n\t\tcontext.artifact_status = (input.artifacts ?? []).slice(0, 24).map((entry) => ({\n\t\t\tpath: clampUtf8(entry.path, 200),\n\t\t\texists: entry.exists === true,\n\t\t\tbytes: Math.max(0, Math.round(entry.bytes)),\n\t\t}));\n\t}\n\tconst state: Record<string, unknown> = {\n\t\t// T-08 (requirement 0 / T-04b residual 1): the registry state builder and\n\t\t// `triage-client.ts::validateStructuredState` are pinned to\n\t\t// `schema_version: 2`; the dp2 checkpoint state must carry the same version\n\t\t// or the future structured-input validator would reject dp2's own input.\n\t\tschema_version: 2,\n\t\tdecision_point: DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID,\n\t\tkey: clampUtf8(input.ownerKey, 48),\n\t\tphase: clampUtf8(input.phase, 16),\n\t\ttask_type: input.taskType,\n\t\trisk: input.checkpoint.risk,\n\t\trisk_source: \"machine\",\n\t\tauthority_tier: \"P2\",\n\t\tquestions_version: DECIDE_REGISTRY[DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID]?.questionsVersion ?? DP2_QUESTIONS_VERSION,\n\t\tprogress,\n\t};\n\tif (Object.keys(context).length > 0) state.context = context;\n\t// W6: fail loud at the producer when the registry and this builder drift\n\t// (`task_key` used to ride here; it is not a dp2 field, so it is gone).\n\tassertStateMatchesRegistry(DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID, state);\n\treturn state;\n}\n\n/** `context.artifact_status` (W6): expected task outputs first, then whatever\n * else sits in the task dir, each fs-stated. Missing expected files are rows too\n * (`exists: false`) — that absence is exactly what the model should see.\n * Never throws (an unreadable dir yields no rows) and never exceeds 24 rows. */\nfunction readDp2ArtifactStatus(taskDir: string): Dp2ArtifactStatus[] {\n\tconst expected = [\"task.md\", \"output.md\", \"report.md\", \"trace.log\", \"worker.log\"];\n\tconst seen = new Set<string>();\n\tconst rows: Dp2ArtifactStatus[] = [];\n\tconst add = (rel: string): void => {\n\t\tif (rel === \"\" || seen.has(rel) || rows.length >= 24) return;\n\t\tseen.add(rel);\n\t\tconst absolute = path.join(taskDir, rel);\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tconst stat = fs.statSync(absolute);\n\t\t\tif (!stat.isFile()) return;\n\t\t\trows.push({ path: rel, exists: true, bytes: stat.size });\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\trows.push({ path: rel, exists: false, bytes: 0 });\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\tfor (const rel of expected) add(rel);\n\tlet entries: string[] = [];\n\ttry {\n\t\tentries = fs.readdirSync(taskDir).sort();\n\t} catch {\n\t\tentries = [];\n\t}\n\tfor (const rel of entries) add(rel);\n\treturn rows;\n}\n\nfunction splitPhaseProgress(phases: string): { done: number; total: number } {\n\tconst match = /^(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)$/.exec(phases.trim());\n\tif (!match) return { done: 0, total: 0 };\n\treturn { done: Number(match[1]), total: Number(match[2]) };\n}\n\n/** The dp2 state's `task_type` is the dp1 3-value taxonomy; a role outside it\n * (vision / rag_chat / default) is reported as `coding` — the field is required\n * and dp2's question is about progress, not role. */\nfunction dp2TaskType(headerType: string | undefined): string {\n\treturn headerType === \"research\" || headerType === \"review\" ? headerType : \"coding\";\n}\n\n/** Wall budget mirror of `worker-mode.resolveBudgetMs` (that module imports this\n * one, so it cannot be imported back here): task.md `timeout:` minutes >\n * PI_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS > 60m default. */\nfunction dp2BudgetMin(timeoutHeader: string | undefined, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): number {\n\tconst header = Number(timeoutHeader);\n\tif (timeoutHeader !== undefined && Number.isFinite(header) && header > 0) return header;\n\tconst envMs = Number(env.PI_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS);\n\tif (Number.isFinite(envMs) && envMs > 0) return Math.round(envMs / 60_000);\n\treturn 60;\n}\n\n/** task.md header view dp2 needs: `phase:`, `type:` and `timeout:`. Undefined\n * when task.md is unreadable (the caller then keeps its original alert). */\nexport function readDp2TaskHeader(\n\ttaskDir: string,\n\tenv: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,\n): { phase: string; taskType: string; budgetMin: number } | undefined {\n\tlet content: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tcontent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(taskDir, \"task.md\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn undefined;\n\t}\n\tconst phase = readTaskHeaderScalar(content, \"phase\") ?? \"\";\n\treturn {\n\t\tphase: phase === \"\" ? \"unknown\" : phase,\n\t\ttaskType: dp2TaskType(readTaskType(content).type),\n\t\tbudgetMin: dp2BudgetMin(readTaskHeaderScalar(content, \"timeout\"), env),\n\t};\n}\n\n/** Normalised dp2 outcome. `action` is the closed vocabulary the caller branches\n * on: only `narrow` can ever be `acted` (D-011); `split`, `direct` and\n * `escalate` all fall through to the human alert. */\nexport interface Dp2CheckpointDecision {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\ttriggerId: string;\n\t/** Raw `checkpoint_action` value when the service produced one. */\n\tanswer?: string;\n\taction: \"narrow\" | \"split\" | \"direct\" | \"escalate\" | \"none\";\n\tavailable: boolean;\n\tacted: boolean;\n\t/** Effective mode as reported by the child (`payload.mode`, D-036: mode is an\n\t * authorization OUTPUT). Absent when Python never answered; never read from\n\t * the local `.mw/decide-points.json` mirror. */\n\tmode?: \"auto\" | \"suggest\";\n\treason?: string;\n\tconfidence?: number | null;\n\tconfidenceSource?: string;\n\tbudgetMin: number;\n\telapsedMin: number;\n}\n\nexport interface Dp2CheckpointInput {\n\t/** Project root that owns `.mw/` (the control workspace in dual-root runs). */\n\tprojectDir: string;\n\townerKey: string;\n\ttaskKey: string;\n\ttaskDir: string;\n\tcheckpoint: CheckpointInfo;\n\t/** Test seam: replaces the `mw decide run` child (production: runDecideMw). */\n\trun?: DecideRunner;\n\t/** Budget env override (tests); defaults to `process.env`. */\n\tenv?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n}\n\nfunction parseDecisionPayload(stdout: string): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {\n\tconst trimmed = stdout.trim();\n\tconst attempts = [trimmed];\n\tconst lastLine = trimmed.split(\"\\n\").at(-1);\n\tif (lastLine !== undefined && lastLine !== trimmed) attempts.push(lastLine.trim());\n\tfor (const text of attempts) {\n\t\tif (!text) continue;\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tconst parsed = recordOf(JSON.parse(text) as unknown);\n\t\t\tif (parsed) return parsed;\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t// try the next candidate\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn undefined;\n}\n\n/** Ask dp2 for one checkpoint. NEVER throws and NEVER acts — it only decides\n * whether a `narrow` answer may replace the PM alert. `undefined` means the\n * feature is off for this project (design D-007 complete bypass: no spawn, no\n * write). */\nexport function decideDp2Checkpoint(input: Dp2CheckpointInput): Dp2CheckpointDecision | undefined {\n\tconst policy = readDecidePolicy(input.projectDir);\n\tif (!policy.enabled) return undefined;\n\t// AC-016: the effective per-dp policy (row > decide.json > built-in) drives\n\t// the child budget and the confidence gate below. Resolution never throws.\n\tconst effective = resolveDecidePolicy(DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID, input.projectDir);\n\t// Zero-spawn short-circuit ONLY (D-036): `readDp2Authorization` is a mirror of\n\t// the Python row parser, so its verdict is a cost saving, never an\n\t// authorization. `decision_points.decide_for` decides; a divergence resolves\n\t// to Python. That is also why the decision's `mode`/`acted` below are taken\n\t// from the child payload and not from this read.\n\tconst authorization = readDp2Authorization(input.projectDir);\n\tif (!authorization.enabled) return undefined;\n\n\tconst trend = readCheckpointTrend(input.taskDir);\n\tconst triggerId = `${input.taskKey}#ckpt${trend.total}`;\n\tconst base: Dp2CheckpointDecision = {\n\t\tdecisionId: `${DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID}:${triggerId}`,\n\t\ttriggerId,\n\t\taction: \"none\",\n\t\tavailable: false,\n\t\tacted: false,\n\t\tbudgetMin: 0,\n\t\telapsedMin: Math.max(0, Math.round(input.checkpoint.elapsedS / 60)),\n\t};\n\n\tconst header = readDp2TaskHeader(input.taskDir, input.env ?? process.env);\n\tif (!header) return { ...base, reason: \"input-incomplete\" };\n\tbase.budgetMin = header.budgetMin;\n\tconst state = buildDp2CheckpointState({\n\t\townerKey: input.ownerKey,\n\t\ttaskKey: input.taskKey,\n\t\tphase: header.phase,\n\t\ttaskType: header.taskType,\n\t\tbudgetMin: header.budgetMin,\n\t\tcheckpoint: input.checkpoint,\n\t\ttrend: trend.points,\n\t\tartifacts: readDp2ArtifactStatus(input.taskDir),\n\t});\n\n\tconst run = input.run ?? runDecideMw;\n\tlet raw: RawDecideRun;\n\ttry {\n\t\traw = run({\n\t\t\tprojectDir: input.projectDir,\n\t\t\tdp: DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID,\n\t\t\ttimeoutMs: Math.round(effective.timeoutS * 1000),\n\t\t\t// Structured envelope only: the registry is the question authority\n\t\t\t// (D-027), so no `questions` map rides along.\n\t\t\tinput: JSON.stringify({ state }),\n\t\t});\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn { ...base, reason: \"upstream-error\" };\n\t}\n\tif (raw.timedOut) return { ...base, reason: \"timeout\" };\n\tif (raw.error !== undefined || raw.status !== 0) return { ...base, reason: \"upstream-error\" };\n\tconst payload = parseDecisionPayload(raw.stdout);\n\tif (!payload) return { ...base, reason: \"bad-response\" };\n\tif (payload.available !== true) {\n\t\tconst reason = typeof payload.reason === \"string\" && payload.reason !== \"\" ? payload.reason : \"unavailable\";\n\t\treturn { ...base, reason };\n\t}\n\n\tconst answer = recordOf(recordOf(payload.answers)?.[DP2_CHECKPOINT_QUESTION]);\n\tconst value = typeof answer?.value === \"string\" ? answer.value.trim() : \"\";\n\tconst confidence =\n\t\ttypeof answer?.confidence === \"number\" && Number.isFinite(answer.confidence) ? answer.confidence : null;\n\t// D-036: the effective mode is the child's verdict. An absent/unknown value\n\t// stays undefined, which fails closed (`acted=false`) instead of guessing.\n\tconst mode = payload.mode === \"auto\" || payload.mode === \"suggest\" ? payload.mode : undefined;\n\tconst decision: Dp2CheckpointDecision = { ...base, available: true, confidence };\n\tif (mode !== undefined) decision.mode = mode;\n\tif (typeof payload.confidence_source === \"string\" && payload.confidence_source !== \"\") {\n\t\tdecision.confidenceSource = payload.confidence_source;\n\t}\n\tif (value !== \"\") decision.answer = value;\n\t// Closed mapping: an unknown / missing value stays `none` (fail-closed onto\n\t// the human alert) — there is deliberately no default action branch.\n\tif (value === \"narrow\") decision.action = \"narrow\";\n\telse if (value === \"split\") decision.action = \"split\";\n\telse if (value === \"direct-exec\" || value === \"direct\") decision.action = \"direct\";\n\telse if (value === \"escalate\") decision.action = \"escalate\";\n\t// D-011/D-041: `narrow` is the ONLY action the machine may execute, and only\n\t// in the mode Python reports (`payload.mode`, not the local mirror). `suggest`\n\t// records the answer (Python already appended its evidence row) and still\n\t// wakes the PM (AC-015). AC-016: the confidence gate is the effective\n\t// per-dp `min_confidence` (Python applies the same threshold before it can\n\t// report `auto`); a payload without a usable confidence keeps the pre-AC-016\n\t// verdict and is never invented into one.\n\tconst confident = confidence === null || confidence >= effective.minConfidence;\n\tdecision.acted = mode === \"auto\" && decision.action === \"narrow\" && confident;\n\treturn decision;\n}\n\n/** Write `<taskDir>/steer-dp2.md` (design §5.3). The PM process is the single\n * writer; the worker consumes the file at its next checkpoint tick and renames\n * it away. Returns false when the request could not be written — the caller\n * must then fall back to the human alert: a narrow that never reaches the\n * worker is not an acted decision. */\nexport function writeDp2SteerRequest(input: {\n\ttaskDir: string;\n\tdecision: Dp2CheckpointDecision;\n\trisk: string;\n}): boolean {\n\tconst target = path.join(input.taskDir, DP2_STEER_FILE);\n\tconst remainingMin = Math.max(0, input.decision.budgetMin - input.decision.elapsedMin);\n\tconst content = [\n\t\t`${DP2_STEER_REQUEST_HEADER} decision_id=${input.decision.decisionId} dp=${DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID}` +\n\t\t\t` risk=${input.risk} elapsed_minutes=${input.decision.elapsedMin}` +\n\t\t\t` budget_minutes=${input.decision.budgetMin} remaining_min=${remainingMin}`,\n\t\t`${DP2_NARROW_MARKER} dp2 已自动判定收窄本任务（decision_id=${input.decision.decisionId}）：` +\n\t\t\t`停止展开新工作，只保留能直接收敛的路径，优先保证已完成部分可交付；不新增文件、不改验收目标。` +\n\t\t\t`预算剩余约 ${remainingMin}m。`,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t].join(\"\\n\");\n\t// Atomic request: a half-written steer must never be consumed by the worker.\n\tconst tmp = `${target}.tmp`;\n\ttry {\n\t\tfs.writeFileSync(tmp, content, \"utf8\");\n\t\tfs.renameSync(tmp, target);\n\t\treturn true;\n\t} catch {\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tfs.rmSync(tmp, { force: true });\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t// Best-effort cleanup only — the false return already selects the alert path.\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/** One `[DECISION] dp2 acted=1 decision_id=… trigger=…` correlation line in the\n * task's own trace (T-04d, design D-041 row 5).\n *\n * Written ONLY after the narrow actually executed — i.e. after\n * {@link writeDp2SteerRequest} returned true and the human alert was skipped. A\n * fallback to the alert (task not running / unwritable steer), `suggest` mode\n * and a disabled dp2 never write it: an un-executed decision may not claim\n * `acted=1`. Best-effort — a trace failure must never undo a written steer.\n */\nexport function appendDp2ActedTrace(taskDir: string, decision: Dp2CheckpointDecision): void {\n\ttry {\n\t\tfs.appendFileSync(\n\t\t\tpath.join(taskDir, \"trace.log\"),\n\t\t\t`[DECISION] dp2 acted=1 decision_id=${decision.decisionId} trigger=${decision.triggerId}\\n`,\n\t\t\t\"utf8\",\n\t\t);\n\t} catch {\n\t\t// Diagnostic only: the steer file is the decision's contract.\n\t}\n}\n\n/** `running` / `settled` / `unknown` — the narrow branch may only replace the\n * human alert when the worker can still act on the steer (T-07b, DS-4). */\nexport type Dp2TaskLiveness = \"running\" | \"settled\" | \"unknown\";\n\nfunction pidAlive(pid: number): boolean {\n\ttry {\n\t\tprocess.kill(pid, 0);\n\t\treturn true;\n\t} catch (err) {\n\t\t// EPERM: the process exists but is not ours — still alive. ESRCH: gone.\n\t\treturn (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === \"EPERM\";\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Is the worker this alert is about still able to consume a `steer-dp2.md`?\n *\n * The queue row is this loop's own view and is not evidence enough — it can lag\n * a run that already finished (the row is written by the launcher, the terminal\n * state by the worker itself, AC-022). So the worker's own product is consulted\n * first: `run.json` status, plus pid liveness for an `active` record (a worker\n * killed without a terminal write would otherwise look alive forever). Only\n * when the product gives no information does the ledger row decide.\n *\n * `unknown` (unreadable/unparsable record, no ledger evidence) is passed to the\n * caller as \"not verified live\" — the caller falls back to the human alert,\n * i.e. the fail-closed direction DS-4 requires. */\nexport function probeDp2TaskLiveness(taskDir: string, ledgerStatus?: string): Dp2TaskLiveness {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst state = readRunState(taskDir);\n\t\tif (state !== undefined) {\n\t\t\tconst kind = runStateKind(state);\n\t\t\tif (kind === \"terminal\") return \"settled\";\n\t\t\tif (kind === \"active\") {\n\t\t\t\tconst pid = state.pid;\n\t\t\t\tif (typeof pid === \"number\" && Number.isInteger(pid) && pid > 0)\n\t\t\t\t\treturn pidAlive(pid) ? \"running\" : \"settled\";\n\t\t\t\treturn \"running\";\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t} catch {\n\t\t// A probe that throws is not evidence of a live run: fail closed below.\n\t\treturn \"unknown\";\n\t}\n\tif (ledgerStatus === \"running\" || ledgerStatus === \"pending\") return \"running\";\n\tif (\n\t\tledgerStatus === \"done\" ||\n\t\tledgerStatus === \"failed\" ||\n\t\tledgerStatus === \"needs-clarification\" ||\n\t\tledgerStatus === \"lost\"\n\t) {\n\t\treturn \"settled\";\n\t}\n\treturn \"unknown\";\n}\n\n/** Test seams + the explicit project root for the dp2 checkpoint hook.\n * Production passes only `projectDir`; `run` lets the suite replace the\n * `mw decide run` child (the triage-client DecideRunner seam). */\nexport interface Dp2CheckpointHooks {\n\tprojectDir?: string;\n\trun?: DecideRunner;\n}\n\nexport function startWorkerPollLoop(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\tworkerStore: WorkerStore,\n\tackStore: AckStore,\n\tindexStore: IndexStore,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\twatch: PmWatchState,\n\tui: PmUiHolder,\n\tpollIntervalMs = POLL_INTERVAL_MS,\n\tdp2Hooks?: Dp2CheckpointHooks,\n): NodeJS.Timeout {\n\t// Baseline snapshot: rows already terminal when this window opens are\n\t// history — never replay their summaries. No branch ever replays a readback\n *   because of ack state.\n */\nconst POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 4000; // < 5s per AC-001\n\nfunction isTerminal(status: WorkerStatus): boolean {\n\treturn status === \"done\" || status === \"failed\" || status === \"needs-clarification\" || status === \"lost\";\n}\n\n/** AC-012/AC-013 unread count: terminal queue rows whose readback this window\n * never delivered and which the PM never acked. Pure; the caller supplies the\n * already-read `acked` set so one tick reads `_workers.acked` at most once. */\nfunction countUnreadTerminal(\n\tentries: readonly WorkerEntry[],\n\tacked: ReadonlySet<string>,\n\treadbackDelivered: ReadonlySet<string>,\n): number {\n\tlet n = 0;\n\tfor (const e of entries) {\n\t\tif (!isTerminal(e.status)) continue;\n\t\tif (acked.has(e.taskKey) || readbackDelivered.has(e.taskKey)) continue;\n\t\tn += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn n;\n}\n\nexport type PhaseDocName = \"spec.md\" | \"design.md\" | \"plan.md\";\n\ninterface DocWriteTarget {\n\tkey: string;\n\tdoc: PhaseDocName;\n}\n\n/** The phase-doc write/edit target, when the tool path resolves to\n * {agenticdocRoot}/{key}/spec.md | design.md | plan.md — the PM phase docs that\n * mean \"this window is now executing this key\". Any other path (or file) is\n * not a claim signal. */\nfunction docWriteTarget(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): DocWriteTarget | undefined {\n\tif (toolName !== \"write\" && toolName !== \"edit\") return undefined;\n\tconst filePath = (args as { path?: unknown } | undefined)?.path;\n\tif (typeof filePath !== \"string\" || filePath === \"\") return undefined;\n\tconst rel = path.relative(path.resolve(agenticdocRoot), path.resolve(projectDir, filePath));\n\tif (rel.startsWith(\"..\") || path.isAbsolute(rel)) return undefined; // outside .agenticdoc\n\tconst parts = rel.split(path.sep);\n\tconst doc = parts.length === 2 ? parts[1] : undefined;\n\tif (doc !== \"spec.md\" && doc !== \"design.md\" && doc !== \"plan.md\") return undefined;\n\tconst key = parts[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (!key || key.startsWith(\"_\") || key.startsWith(\".\")) return undefined;\n\treturn { key, doc };\n}\n\n/** The key a phase-doc write/edit belongs to (see docWriteTarget). */\nexport function keyFromDocWrite(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): string | undefined {\n\treturn docWriteTarget(toolName, args, projectDir, agenticdocRoot)?.key;\n}\n\n/** Which phase doc was written/edited (see docWriteTarget). */\nexport function docFromWrite(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): PhaseDocName | undefined {\n\treturn docWriteTarget(toolName, args, projectDir, agenticdocRoot)?.doc;\n}\n\nexport type EvidencePhase = \"spec\" | \"design\";\n\n/** The evidence-note write target, when the tool path resolves to\n * {agenticdocRoot}/{key}/evidence/research/spec-*.md | design-*.md. Not a\n * claim signal (only phase docs are) — but the moment evidence lands is the\n * moment an already-written phase doc's claims can be re-reviewed against\n * it. */\nexport function evidencePhaseFromWrite(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): { key: string; phase: EvidencePhase } | undefined {\n\tif (toolName !== \"write\" && toolName !== \"edit\") return undefined;\n\tconst filePath = (args as { path?: unknown } | undefined)?.path;\n\tif (typeof filePath !== \"string\" || filePath === \"\") return undefined;\n\tconst rel = path.relative(path.resolve(agenticdocRoot), path.resolve(projectDir, filePath));\n\tif (rel.startsWith(\"..\") || path.isAbsolute(rel)) return undefined; // outside .agenticdoc\n\tconst parts = rel.split(path.sep);\n\tif (parts.length !== 4 || parts[1] !== \"evidence\" || parts[2] !== \"research\") return undefined;\n\tconst note = parts[3] ?? \"\";\n\tif (!note.endsWith(\".md\")) return undefined;\n\tconst phase: EvidencePhase | undefined = note.startsWith(\"spec-\")\n\t\t? \"spec\"\n\t\t: note.startsWith(\"design-\")\n\t\t\t? \"design\"\n\t\t\t: undefined;\n\tif (!phase) return undefined;\n\tconst key = parts[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (!key || key.startsWith(\"_\") || key.startsWith(\".\")) return undefined;\n\treturn { key, phase };\n}\n\n/** UI notice when a phase doc and its research evidence coexist — the\n * \"re-review when evidence is generated\" protocol, as a *notice*, not an\n * injected instruction (mw-evidence-nudge-notify): the old sendUserMessage\n * form made the model treat the automatic nudge as the user ordering an\n * immediate review pass, so the window agent started rewriting the doc with\n * no consent and no chance to veto, hijacking the turn. The framework's role\n * is to flag the moment; the user decides when (and whether) to run the\n * review. Fires once per (key, phase) per session, only when both the phase\n * doc (>= 500 bytes) and >= 1 evidence note exist: the review needs both\n * sides of the comparison. */\nexport function evidenceReviewNotice(\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n\tkey: string,\n\tphase: EvidencePhase,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tnotified: Set<string>,\n): void {\n\tconst dedup = `${key}:${phase}`;\n\tif (notified.has(dedup)) return;\n\tconst docs = readPhaseDocs(agenticdocRoot, key);\n\tconst docOk = phase === \"spec\" ? docs.spec : docs.design;\n\tconst evidence = phase === \"spec\" ? docs.specEvidence : docs.designEvidence;\n\tif (!docOk || evidence < 1) return;\n\tnotified.add(dedup);\n\tconst doc = phase === \"spec\" ? \"spec.md\" : \"design.md\";\n\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t`[mw] ${key}: ${phase} 阶段证据已就位（${evidence} 份 research note）——建议对照 evidence/research/ 复查 ${doc}（断言-证据对照 / 数字口径 / 内部一致性 / 可证伪性）。何时执行复查由你决定。`,\n\t\t\"info\",\n\t);\n}\n\n/** Nudge the user toward the /goal brainstorm when the project goal is not\n * yet established. Headless sessions (print/-p) skip the nudge entirely:\n * sendUserMessage starts a generation immediately, and the queued -p prompt\n * would collide with it (\"Agent is already processing\") before ever reaching\n * the model — `pi -p` in any project without an established goal.md would\n * hard-fail at startup. */\nexport function nudgeGoalUnestablished(pi: ExtensionAPI, agenticdocRoot: string, hasUI: boolean): void {\n\tconst goal = readGoal(agenticdocRoot);\n\tif (hasUI && !isGoalEstablished(goal)) {\n\t\tpi.sendUserMessage(\n\t\t\t\"[agent-team-loop] 项目总目标（.agenticdoc/goal.md）尚未确立。\\n\" +\n\t\t\t\t\"建议先运行 /goal，与我对话共创项目总目标——它是后续每个 spec 对齐的锚点。\\n\" +\n\t\t\t\t\"（也可直接编辑 .agenticdoc/goal.md 填好三段内容并把 status 改为 active。）\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Auto-takeover on phase-doc write: writing/editing {key}/spec.md, design.md,\n * or plan.md is this window saying \"I am now executing key X\" — claim it and\n * watch it, exactly like /pm-key switch. Writing design.md / plan.md also\n * runs the next-phase evidence gate (mirrors advance_phase.py): the previous\n * phase's research notes must exist, or the user is warned immediately. */\nexport async function autoTakeOverFromDoc(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\tindexStore: IndexStore,\n\twatch: PmWatchState,\n\trefreshWatch: (ctx: ExtensionContext) => void,\n\tkey: string,\n\tdoc: PhaseDocName,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n): Promise<void> {\n\t// Next-phase evidence gate: writing design.md means the spec phase should be\n\t// complete (its research notes exist); writing plan.md means design should be.\n\t// Fires regardless of takeover idempotency — the missing evidence is the\n\t// message, and it stays true until the notes are written.\n\tconst docs = readPhaseDocs(agenticdocRoot, key);\n\tif (doc === \"spec.md\" && docs.specEvidence < 1) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/spec-*.md found — write the research notes (or a zero-research declaration) alongside the spec; the advance-to-design gate checks them.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tif (doc === \"design.md\" && docs.specEvidence < 1) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/spec-*.md found — the advance-to-design gate requires >= 1 research note (a zero-research declaration counts). Write it before advancing.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tif (doc === \"plan.md\") {\n\t\tif (!docs.design) {\n\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: design.md missing or under 500 bytes — required before plan (run the system-design workflow).`,\n\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t} else if (docs.designEvidence < 1) {\n\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/design-*.md found — the advance-to-plan gate requires >= 1 research note (a zero-research declaration counts). Write it before advancing.`,\n\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tconst row = indexStore.findByKey(key);\n\tconst wasWatching = watch.key === key;\n\tconst wasClaimed = row?.claimId === windowClaimId();\n\tif (wasWatching && wasClaimed) return; // already ours — nothing to do\n\n\tconst result = await takeOverKey(indexStore, key, false, agenticdocRoot);\n\twatch.key = key;\n\tpi.appendEntry(WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE, { key, claimed: result.ok });\n\trefreshWatch(ctx);\n\tif (result.ok) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] claimed key '${key}' (doc write detected) — watching it${result.created ? \" (new key registered)\" : \"\"}.`,\n\t\t\t\"info\",\n\t\t);\n\t\tif (result.audit.length > 0) ctx.ui.notify(result.audit.join(\"\\n\"), \"warning\");\n\t} else {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' is claimed by another live window (${result.blockedBy}) — watching only.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Restore this window's watched key from the session file (survives restart\n * and resume) and re-render the bottom widget. A watch that came with a key\n * takeover re-claims the key with this process's identity — quietly, unless\n * another live window took it over in the meantime. */\nexport async function restoreWatch(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\twatch: PmWatchState,\n\tindexStore: IndexStore,\n\tworkerStore: WorkerStore,\n\tackStore: AckStore,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n): Promise<void> {\n\tlet data: { key?: string; claimed?: boolean } | undefined;\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst entries = ctx.sessionManager.getEntries();\n\t\tfor (let i = entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n\t\t\tconst e = entries[i];\n\t\t\tif (e.type === \"custom\" && e.customType === WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE) {\n\t\t\t\tdata = e.data as { key?: string; claimed?: boolean } | undefined;\n\t\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn; // session entries unavailable — nothing to restore\n\t}\n\tif (!data?.key) return;\n\tconst key = data.key;\n\twatch.key = key;\n\n\t// T-16c: the restart restore path may take a key back from THIS host's\n\t// conductor (a `held-conductor` synthetic claim is yieldable — T-16b). That\n\t// handover is correct (human priority) but must not be silent: the goal is\n\t// that \"who took the key from the conductor, and when\" stays explainable.\n\t// Recorded on existing surfaces only — no new event name, no new entry type:\n\t//   * the `_index.parallel` Claim cell (and the pm-state.md mirror) flips to\n\t//     this window — the state surface;\n\t//   * `tookOverFromConductor` rides the EXISTING `agent-team-loop:watch`\n\t//     session entry shape, giving the durable machine-readable act record;\n\t//   * a transcript notice via the existing `displaySummary` channel states\n\t//     the holder change out loud (passive — it never spends an agent turn).\n\t// The timeline is deliberately NOT written here: it has a single writer (the\n\t// conductor, `timeline.py` D-109) and a second seq counter would corrupt it.\n\t// Set only in the `held-conductor` branch, so a second restart (row now this\n\t// window's, or stale) leaves exactly the same record count — idempotent by\n\t// construction.\n\tlet tookOverFromConductor: string | undefined;\n\tif (data.claimed) {\n\t\tconst row = indexStore.findByKey(key);\n\t\tif (row) {\n\t\t\tconst self = windowClaimId();\n\t\t\tconst previousClaim = row.claimId.trim();\n\t\t\tconst holder = claimState(previousClaim, self);\n\t\t\tif (holder === \"held-live\") {\n\t\t\t\t// Another window took over while this one was closed — keep the\n\t\t\t\t// watch (display-only) and say so; do not touch the shared row.\n\t\t\t\t// Unchanged by T-16c (requirement 3): a truly live foreign claim\n\t\t\t\t// is still never taken silently.\n\t\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' is claimed by another window (${row.claimId}) — watching only.`,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t// Our previous process is gone; re-bind ownership through the\n\t\t\t\t// atomic claim — a window that raced us to this key wins and we\n\t\t\t\t// degrade to watch-only (review M2). Quiet re-claim: no demote of\n\t\t\t\t// other active rows, no status flip; only claimId/updated move.\n\t\t\t\tconst outcome = await indexStore.claim(key, self, (id) => claimState(id, self) === \"held-live\", {\n\t\t\t\t\tdemoteOthers: false,\n\t\t\t\t\tactivate: false,\n\t\t\t\t});\n\t\t\t\tif (!outcome.ok) {\n\t\t\t\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' is claimed by another window (${outcome.blockedBy}) — watching only.`,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t// This path flips the index row's Claim column too, so the\n\t\t\t\t\t// pm-state.md mirror must be synced as well (D-108). A failed\n\t\t\t\t\t// mirror never reverts the claim — the index row is\n\t\t\t\t\t// authoritative — but the divergence must be visible.\n\t\t\t\t\tconst sync = syncPmStateClaimId(agenticdocRoot, key, self);\n\t\t\t\t\tconst syncWarning = claimSyncWarningText(key, sync);\n\t\t\t\t\tif (syncWarning !== \"\") ctx.ui.notify(syncWarning, \"warning\");\n\t\t\t\t\tif (holder === \"held-conductor\") {\n\t\t\t\t\t\ttookOverFromConductor = previousClaim;\n\t\t\t\t\t\tdisplaySummary(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tpi,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t`[mw] 窗口重启恢复：key '${key}' 原由本机 autopilot conductor 接管（合成 claim ${previousClaim}），` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t`已改由本窗口接管（${self}）。人工优先，conductor 下次 tick 让位且不再抢回；` +\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\"记录面：_index.parallel 的 Claim 单元 + 本 session 的 agent-team-loop:watch entry（tookOverFromConductor）。\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tsetWatchWidget(\n\t\tctx,\n\t\trenderWatchLines(indexStore, workerStore, ackStore, agenticdocRoot, key, watch.dispatchedTaskKeys),\n\t);\n\t// Re-stamp the entry so it lands in the (possibly new) session file.\n\t// T-16c: `tookOverFromConductor` (the pre-takeover synthetic claim id) is\n\t// added ONLY on the handover restore, so the act record is exactly one entry\n\t// regardless of how often the window restarts afterwards.\n\tpi.appendEntry(WATCH_ENTRY_TYPE, {\n\t\tkey,\n\t\tclaimed: data.claimed ?? false,\n\t\t...(tookOverFromConductor === undefined ? {} : { tookOverFromConductor }),\n\t});\n\n\t// Saved working context (pm-save): point the user at it — a notice, never\n\t// an injected instruction (same principle as evidenceReviewNotice: the\n\t// framework flags, the user decides whether the agent reads it).\n\tconst pmStatePath = path.join(agenticdocRoot, key, \"pm-state.md\");\n\tif (fs.existsSync(pmStatePath)) {\n\t\tconst updated = fs.statSync(pmStatePath).mtime.toISOString();\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] key '${key}' 有已保存的 pm-state.md（更新于 ${updated}）。如需接续上次的工作上下文，让 agent 读取 ${key}/pm-state.md 的 Notes 区。`,\n\t\t\t\"info\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction pickWorkerRoute(taskContent: string): { cli: string; provider: string } {\n\t// Global default is pi/timi: review/research are routing HINTS for the\n\t// agent, not claude redirects (design D-005) — a claude worker requires an\n\t// explicit `cli` param on dispatch_worker / /worker, where missing\n\t// credentials fail per-task instead of silently degrading the route.\n\t// The reading comes from the single-source header parser (AC-005/F-6): the\n\t// old `/^type:\\s*codex/im` full-text regex let one body line flip the\n\t// dispatch CLI, outside the shared `type:` matrix.\n\tif (readTaskType(taskContent).type === \"codex\") return { cli: \"codex\", provider: \"\" };\n\treturn { cli: \"pi\", provider: \"timi\" };\n}\n\n// Optional `model:` line in task.md → passed through to the launcher as --model/-m.\nfunction readModel(taskContent: string): string {\n\tconst m = taskContent.match(/^model:\\s*(.+)$/im);\n\treturn m ? m[1].trim() : \"\";\n}\n\n// Conductor-origin marker line (D-104): `origin: conductor`. Manual/legacy tasks carry no\n * marker and behave exactly as before (AC-012 zero regression). Unreadable\n * task.md returns false so the dispatch loop hits the same read error it\n * always did. */\nfunction isConductorTask(taskMdPath: string): boolean {\n\ttry {\n\t\treturn readTaskOrigin(fs.readFileSync(taskMdPath, \"utf8\")) === \"conductor\";\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Why a dispatch scan refused to queue anything (AC-020/AC-021). */\nexport type DispatchAlarmKind =\n\t| \"queue-rows-unparsable\"\n\t| \"queue-unreadable\"\n\t| \"dispatch-quota\"\n\t// A candidate outside this window's scope (AC-019/T-19): the PM must be able\n\t// to see what it did NOT touch, aggregated per scan — visibility, not\n\t// prohibition (the read side stays global, AC-024). NOTICE, not a refusal:\n\t// nothing was refused, these keys simply belong to somebody else. Since T-22\n\t// the kind carries ONLY keys with no owner record at all (no index row AND no\n\t// `pm-state.md` machine line / worker `trace.log`): the text names the exact\n\t// human action (`switch_key` / `dispatch_worker(key=…)`) because a guessed\n\t// index row would invent Phase/ClaimId/Deps facts.\n\t| \"out-of-scope\"\n\t// A registered key with undispatched work, no live claim and no live run\n\t// (AC-011/T-19): its owner is gone and nothing will ever re-dispatch it —\n\t// the conductor only skips CLAIM_LIVE keys and claiming one is forbidden\n\t// (AUTOPILOT-HANDOFF §5 #13), so the scan repairs it claim-free. The guard itself cannot block;\n\t// observability is the only remaining defence (design DD-08).\n\t| \"write-scope-risk\"\n\t// A registered key whose repair evidence is STALE (T-24/C-30): the index row\n\t// is `idle`/`done` (or its claim is an old legacy Claim-Id) and the key's own\n\t// state documents have not moved in the freshness window. The summary rides `detail`; the PM is woken by a\n\t// separate `deliverPmAlert` ONLY when the suggestion disagrees with the\n\t// dispatched type (and `points.dp1.alert_on_disagreement !== false`).\n\t| \"triage-suggestion\"\n\t// DP-1 could not produce a suggestion (disabled is NOT this kind — disabled is\n\t// a complete bypass). Recorded only when `triage_notify_on_unavailable=true`;\n\t// the dispatch proceeds unchanged and the PM is never woken by it.\n\t| \"triage-unavailable\";\n\nexport interface DispatchAlarm {\n\tkind: DispatchAlarmKind;\n\tcount: number;\n\tdetail?: string;\n}\n\n/** Alarm kinds that are NOT refusals — the scan made a scope/ownership\n * observation. Their text must stay neutral (`[mw] dispatch 提示：…`); only\n * real refusal kinds may say `[mw] dispatch 已拒绝：…` (AC-011/T-19). */\nexport const NOTICE_DISPATCH_ALARM_KINDS: ReadonlySet<DispatchAlarmKind> = new Set([\n\t\"out-of-scope\",\n\t\"orphaned-keys\",\n\t\"orphan-repair-skipped\",\n\t// AC-006: a run of model-error terminals refuses nothing — it is an\n\t// observation about the model layer, so its text must read as `提示`.\n\t\"model-error\",\n\t// T-03: DP-1 triage rows refuse nothing — the advice is advisory and the\n\t// unavailable notice is informational, so both read as `提示`.\n\t\"triage-suggestion\",\n\t\"triage-unavailable\",\n]);\n\n/** Is this alarm a notice (neutral wording) rather than a refusal? */\nexport function isNoticeDispatchAlarm(kind: DispatchAlarmKind): boolean {\n\treturn NOTICE_DISPATCH_ALARM_KINDS.has(kind);\n}\n\n/** Autopilot ledger path (shared with the Python conductor). */\nconst AUTO_DECISIONS_FILE = \"auto-decisions.jsonl\";\n\n/** One-line human text for a refused dispatch scan (AC-020/AC-021). Notice\n * kinds carry neutral wording; the verdict prefix is added by\n * {@link formatDispatchAlarm} (AC-011/T-19). */\nexport function describeDispatchAlarm(alarm: DispatchAlarm): string {\n\tswitch (alarm.kind) {\n\t\tcase \"queue-rows-unparsable\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} unreadable row(s) in _workers.parallel — dispatch refused (fix the row; nothing was queued)${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"queue-unreadable\":\n\t\t\treturn `the queue looks empty while the work has already run (key ${alarm.detail ?? \"?\"}) — dispatch refused instead of re-running ${\n\t\t\t\talarm.count\n\t\t\t} task(s)`;\n\t\tcase \"dispatch-quota\":\n\t\t\treturn `scan quota reached after ${alarm.count} task(s) — the rest of this scan was refused`;\n\t\tcase \"out-of-scope\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} key(s) with undispatched work but no owner record, outside this window's write scope (${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ?? \"?\"\n\t\t\t}) — scanned read-only, nothing written. Action required: register the key first (switch_key <key> or dispatch_worker(key=<key>)), then dispatch; its work sits in {key}/workers/<task-key>/task.md`;\n\t\tcase \"orphaned-keys\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} orphaned key(s) with undispatched work, no live claim and no live run (${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ?? \"?\"\n\t\t\t}) — claim-free repair dispatch applied (the conductor stays eligible); no _index.parallel claim was written`;\n\t\tcase \"orphan-repair-skipped\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} key(s) with work but stale owner evidence — claim-free repair skipped, nothing written (${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ?? \"?\"\n\t\t\t})`;\n\t\tcase \"run-ledger-conflict\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} task(s) already have a terminal run.json while the queue has no row for them — not re-queued${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"no-product\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} read-only run(s) settled without a product — needs-clarification, awaiting human judgement${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"write-scope-risk\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} write-scope residual-risk row(s) (blocked=false, risk=deny-basename)${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? ` on ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t} — the guard allowed them by contract; review the audited target`;\n\t\tcase \"write-face-refusal\":\n\t\t\treturn `write_face gate refused ${alarm.count} task(s)${alarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"} — not queued`;\n\t\tcase \"model-error\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} consecutive worker run(s) ended with model-unavailable evidence${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? ` (latest: ${alarm.detail})` : \"\"\n\t\t\t} — the same key keeps settling against a failing model; check the provider route/credential or the fallback model list before the next dispatch`;\n\t\tcase \"triage-suggestion\":\n\t\t\treturn `${alarm.count} pre-dispatch triage suggestion(s), advisory only — the dispatch type/role/model were NOT changed${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? `: ${alarm.detail}` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t\tcase \"triage-unavailable\":\n\t\t\treturn `pre-dispatch triage produced no suggestion — dispatch proceeds unchanged${\n\t\t\t\talarm.detail ? ` (${alarm.detail})` : \"\"\n\t\t\t}`;\n\t}\n}\n\n/** The full PM alert line for one alarm (AC-011/T-19): only real refusal kinds\n * carry the `已拒绝` verdict — a notice (`out-of-scope` / `orphaned-keys`) says\n * `提示` and never reads as a refusal. */\nexport function formatDispatchAlarm(alarm: DispatchAlarm): string {\n\tconst verdict = isNoticeDispatchAlarm(alarm.kind) ? \"提示\" : \"已拒绝\";\n\treturn `[mw] dispatch ${verdict}：${describeDispatchAlarm(alarm)}`;\n}\n\n/** Append one machine-readable alarm row to the autopilot ledger\n * (`.agenticdoc/_autopilot/auto-decisions.jsonl`, AC-020/AC-021). Decision consumers filter on\n * `phase == \"decide\"`, so `phase: \"dispatch-alarm\"` is invisible to them while\n * staying visible to humans, `mw doctor` and later consumers. Best-effort by\n * design: losing the alarm must never break dispatch. */\nexport function recordDispatchAlarm(agenticdocRoot: string, alarm: DispatchAlarm): void {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst ledger = path.join(agenticdocRoot, \"_autopilot\", AUTO_DECISIONS_FILE);\n\t\tlet seq = 1;\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tseq =\n\t\t\t\tfs\n\t\t\t\t\t.readFileSync(ledger, \"utf8\")\n\t\t\t\t\t.split(\"\\n\")\n\t\t\t\t\t.filter((l) => l.trim() !== \"\").length + 1;\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\tseq = 1;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst row = { seq, phase: \"dispatch-alarm\", kind: alarm.kind, count: alarm.count, detail: alarm.detail ?? \"\" };\n\t\tfs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(ledger), { recursive: true });\n\t\tfs.appendFileSync(ledger, `${JSON.stringify(row)}\\n`, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch (err) {\n\t\tconsole.error(`[mw] dispatch alarm not recorded: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n\t}\n}\n\n/** Count the write-guard residual-risk audit rows in one worker trace\n * (AC-007/T-03): `[WRITE_SCOPE]` lines carrying BOTH `blocked=false` and\n * `risk=deny-basename`. Best-effort — a\n * missing/unreadable trace is zero, never an error. */\nexport function countWriteScopeResidualRisks(taskDir: string): number {\n\tlet raw: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\traw = fs.readFileSync(path.join(taskDir, \"trace.log\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tlet count = 0;\n\tfor (const line of raw.split(\"\\n\")) {\n\t\tif (!line.startsWith(\"[WRITE_SCOPE] \")) continue;\n\t\tif (!line.includes(\"blocked=false\")) continue;\n\t\tif (!line.includes(\"risk=deny-basename\")) continue;\n\t\tcount += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn count;\n}\n\n/** PM-side exit for the write-guard residual risk (AC-007/DD-08): the worker\n * was allowed through by contract, so the ledger row is the remaining defence.\n * Reuses the single dispatch-alarm channel and its unchanged row shape; returns\n * the number of residual-risk rows found (0 ⇒ nothing written). */\nexport function recordWriteScopeResidualRisks(agenticdocRoot: string, taskKey: string, taskDir: string): number {\n\tconst count = countWriteScopeResidualRisks(taskDir);\n\tif (count === 0) return 0;\n\trecordDispatchAlarm(agenticdocRoot, { kind: \"write-scope-risk\", count, detail: taskKey });\n\treturn count;\n}\n\n/** Exit-Reason prefix every model-exhausted worker writes (design §4; the\n * worker-side T-01 half of this key). */\nexport const MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_PREFIX = \"model unavailable:\";\n\n/** Consecutive model-error terminals before the PM records one `model-error`\n * alarm (AC-006; K=2 per design §3.4/D7). */\nexport const MODEL_ERROR_STREAK_K = 2;\n\n/** `run.json.model_exhausted === true` (design §4: the worker sets it on the\n * model-exhausted terminal, exit 3). Reading failures degrade to `false`, never throw. */\nexport function isModelErrorTerminal(taskDir: string): boolean {\n\tif (runModelExhausted(taskDir)) return true;\n\tconst reason = readLastProductSectionBody(taskDir, [\"Exit Reason\"]);\n\treturn (reason ?? \"\").trimStart().startsWith(MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_PREFIX);\n}\n\n/** Bump (model-error) or clear (every other terminal) one key's consecutive\n * model-error streak. The pure half of AC-006, exported so tests can drive the\n * sequence without standing up the poll loop. */\nexport function bumpModelErrorStreak(streaks: Map<string, number>, key: string, modelError: boolean): number {\n\tif (!modelError) {\n\t\tstreaks.delete(key);\n\t\treturn 0;\n\t}\n\tconst next = (streaks.get(key) ?? 0) + 1;\n\tstreaks.set(key, next);\n\treturn next;\n}\n\n/** PM-side model-error perception for one terminal worker row (AC-006, design\n * §3.4/D7). PERCEPTION\n * ONLY: the return value is never used to block or alter a re-dispatch. */\nexport function recordModelErrorTerminal(\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tstreakKey: string,\n\ttaskKey: ─────\n\n/** `settle.outcome` vocabulary of the archive (`decide_archive._OUTCOMES`). */\nexport type DecisionSettleOutcome = \"pending\" | \"ok\" | \"rework\" | \"rollback\" | \"inconclusive\";\n\n/** One `kind=settle` row to append — the exact argument set of\n * `decide_archive.append_settle` (dp is derived from the decision id).\n *\n * `evidenceRef` carries the run id \"pm-auto\" | \"human\";\n\tevidenceRef: string | null;\n\tnote: string | null;\n}\n\n/** Why a terminal row produced no settle row. `no-decision-header` is the\n * explicit non-association bucket demanded by spec §6.2 — PM-local decisions,\n * long-latency (dp10), composite attribution, worker-internal `tool_call`s and\n * cross-key spillover all land there and are NEVER guessed at. */\nexport type DecisionSettleSkipReason =\n\t| \"no-decision-header\"\n\t| \"needs-clarification\"\n\t| \"not-terminal\"\n\t| \"inconsistent-run\"\n\t| \"duplicate-settle\"\n\t| \"rollback-without-ok\"\n\t| \"unreadable-task-md\"\n\t| \"append-failed\";\n\nexport interface DecisionSettleSkip {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\treason: DecisionSettleSkipReason;\n}\n\n/** Mapping verdict for one terminal transition (6-state table of card T-08). */\nexport type DecisionSettleMapping =\n\t| { ok: true; outcome: DecisionSettleOutcome; note?: string }\n\t| { ok: false; reason: DecisionSettleSkipReason };\n\n/** The 6 terminal-state mapping (design D-013):\n *\n * | terminal | outcome |\n * | --- | --- |\n * | `done` (exit 0) | `ok` |\n * | `failed` | `rework` |\n * | `failed` + exit 3 / PM-side oracle could only disagree with the run record. */\nexport function mapTerminalToSettle(input: {\n\tstatus: WorkerStatus;\n\t/** `run.json.exit`; undefined while unknown (`lost`, pre-terminal record). */\n\trunExit?: number;\n\t/** `isModelErrorTerminal(taskDir)`: exit 3 / `model unavailable:` evidence. */\n\tmodelError: boolean;\n}): DecisionSettleMapping {\n\tswitch (input.status) row.evidence_ref : null,\n\t\t});\n\t}\n\treturn rows;\n}\n\n/** Decide whether one settle row may be appended (pure): idempotency on\n * `(decision_id, outcome, run_id)` (a PM restart replay writes nothing) and the\n * `rollback` ordering rule (a rollback only exists for a decision that already\n * settled `ok` — otherwise it would fabricate a reversal that never happened).\n * Multiple settles per decision ARE legal: the fold takes the LAST one, which is\n * the only way `ok → rollback` can ever be recorded (design D-013). */\nexport function planDecisionSettle(input: {\n\tdecisionId: string;\n\townerKey: string;\n\ttaskKey: string | null;\n\trunId: string | null;\n\toutcome: DecisionSettleOutcome;\n\tnote?: string;\n\tprior: readonly DecisionSettleRecord[];\n}): { ok: true; row: DecisionSettleRow } | { ok: false; reason: DecisionSettleSkipReason } {\n\tconst split = splitDecisionId(input.decisionId);\n\tif (!split) return { ok: false, reason: \"no-decision-header\" };\n\t// Both rules are per DECISION: another decision settling `ok` on the same run\n\t// says nothing about this one (and must not license a rollback for it).\n\tconst prior = input.prior.filter((row) => row.decisionId === input.decisionId);\n\tif (input.outcome === \"rollback\" && !prior.some((row) => row.outcome === \"ok\")) {\n\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"rollback-without-ok\" };\n\t}\n\tif (prior.some((row) => row.outcome === input.outcome && row.runId === input.runId)) {\n\t\treturn { ok: false, reason: \"duplicate-settle\" };\n\t}\n\treturn {\n\t\tok: true,\n\t\trow: {\n\t\t\tdecisionId: input.decisionId,\n\t\t\tdp: split.dp,\n\t\t\tkey: input.ownerKey,\n\t\t\ttaskKey: input.taskKey,\n\t\t\toutcome: input.outcome,\n\t\t\tsettledBy: \"pm-auto\",\n\t\t\tevidenceRef: input.runId,\n\t\t\tnote: input.note ?? Fail-soft: an unwritable\n * archive is reported in the result, never thrown into the poll loop. */\nexport function recordDecisionSettle(\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\townerKey: string,\n\tentry: Pick<WorkerEntry, \"taskKey\" | \"status\">,\n\ttaskDir: string,\n\thooks: DecisionSettleHooks = {},\n): DecisionSettleResult {\n\tconst result: DecisionSettleResult = { written: [], skipped: [] };\n\tlet taskContent: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\ttaskContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(taskDir, \"task.md\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"unreadable-task-md\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\tconst decisionId = (readTaskHeaderScalar(taskContent, \"decision\") ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (decisionId === \"\") {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"no-decision-header\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\tconst readRun = hooks.readRun ?? readRunState;\n\tconst run = readRun(taskDir);\n\tconst mapping = mapTerminalToSettle({\n\t\tstatus: entry.status,\n\t\trunExit: run?.exit,\n\t\tmodelError: (hooks.modelError ?? archiveSettleAppender(archivePath);\n\tconst appendOne = (\n\t\ttargetDecisionId: string,\n\t\ttargetTaskKey: string | null,\n\t\trunId: string | null,\n\t\toutcome: DecisionSettleOutcome,\n\t\tnote?: string,\n\t): void => {\n\t\tconst plan = planDecisionSettle({\n\t\t\tdecisionId: targetDecisionId,\n\t\t\townerKey,\n\t\t\ttaskKey: targetTaskKey,\n\t\t\trunId,\n\t\t\toutcome,\n\t\t\tnote,\n\t\t\t// Re-read per append: the rollback leg must see the `ok` settle this same\n\t\t\t// call may have just written, and a restarted PM must see the whole file.\n\t\t\tprior: readDecisionSettles(archivePath),\n\t\t});\n\t\tif (!plan.ok) {\n\t\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: targetDecisionId, reason: plan.reason });\n\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst written = append(plan.row);\n\t\tif (!written.ok) {\n\t\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: targetDecisionId, reason: \"append-failed\" });\n\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t}\n\t\tresult.written.push(plan.row);\n\t};\n\n\tappendOne(decisionId, entry.taskKey, run?.run_id ?? null, mapping.outcome, mapping.note);\n\n\t// Rollback leg (design D-013): `supersedes:` is the only way to replace a\n\t// finished run. Recorded only when the replacement actually landed (`ok`) — a\n\t// half-failed re-dispatch must not rewrite a decision that is still in force.\n\tconst superseded = (parseSupersedes(taskContent) ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (superseded === \"\" || mapping.outcome !== \"ok\") return result;\n\tconst supersededDir = path.join(path.dirname(taskDir), superseded);\n\tlet supersededContent: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tsupersededContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(supersededDir, \"task.md\"), \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"unreadable-task-md\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\tconst supersededDecisionId = (readTaskHeaderScalar(supersededContent, \"decision\") ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (supersededDecisionId === \"\") {\n\t\tresult.skipped.push({ decisionId: \"\", reason: \"no-decision-header\" });\n\t\treturn result;\n\t}\n\t// The rollback belongs to the REPLACED run: its task key and its run id (the\n\t// idempotency discriminator), so a re-dispatch can never dedupe against the\n\t// replacement's settle.\n\tappendOne(supersededDecisionId, superseded, readRun(supersededDir)?.run_id ?? null, \"rollback\");\n\treturn result;\n}\n\n/** The one-line ledger detail for a PM-side write-face refusal (AC-003/D-008).\n * `DispatchRefusal.reason` is byte-identical to the conductor's\n * `DispatchResult.reason`, so it already carries the stable refusal `code`, the\n * `overlap-with:<task_key>` pair and the conflict `sample` when the gate could\n * prove one. Deduplicated per `${gateId}:${n}:${reason}` for this process:\n * the poll loop runs every 4 s, so an undeduped drop would append an entry per\n * tick forever. `reason` is one of the three literal drop causes. */\nexport function recordDroppedGateReminder(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\tseen: Set<string>,\n\treminder: { gateId: string; reminderN: number; gateKey: string },\n\treason: \"no-watch\" | \"other-key\" | \"read-error\",\n\terror?: string,\n): void {\n\tconst dedup = `${reminder.gateId}:${reminder.reminderN}:${reason}`;\n\tif (seen.has(dedup)) return;\n\tseen.add(dedup);\n\tpi.appendEntry(GATE_REMINDER_DROPPED_ENTRY_TYPE, {\n\t\tgateId: reminder.gateId,\n\t\tn: reminder.reminderN,\n\t\tgateKey: reminder.gateKey,\n\t\treason,\n\t\t...(error === undefined ? {} : { error }),\n\t});\n}\n\n// ── dp2 checkpoint request (PM-initiated only; mw-decision-context T03) ──────\n//\n// dp2's registry question and labels stay untouched, but the MACHINE never asks\n// dp2 and never acts on an answer. The checkpoint loop below only wakes the PM\n// (the generic watchdog alert); deciding to narrow / split / take over / ask a\n// human is the PM's own decision, taken through the受管 decision tool (T04)\n// within the PM's existing authority. `split`, `direct-exec` and `escalate`\n// change goals or widen authority, so they were never machine actions; the old\n// `narrow` shortcut (a `steer-dp2.md` written by the poll loop) is removed with\n// the automatic call.\n//\n// {@link decideDp2Checkpoint} remains the request/normalisation seam a PM-\n// initiated dp2 call can use; it has no caller in the machine loop.\n\n/** Decision-point id (registry authority: packages/multi-workers/decision_points.py). */\nexport const DP2_CHECKPOINT_ID = \"dp2-checkpoint-split\";\n\n/** Registry question id whose value carries the dp2 answer. */\nexport const DP2_CHECKPOINT_QUESTION = \"checkpoint_action\";\n\n/** Steer request file the PM writes into the worker's task dir. The worker\n * consumes it at its next checkpoint tick (design §5.3: file transport keeps\n * coordination file-driven and the PM the single writer). */\nexport const DP2_STEER_FILE = \"steer-dp2.md\";\n\n/** Attribution marker of the narrowed-scope steer (the worker injects it as a\n * followUp; kept here so the PM-written request file and its consumer cannot\n * drift). The machine no longer writes a steer itself (T03). */\nexport const DP2_NARROW_MARKER = \"[mw dp2-narrow]\";\n\n/** Machine header line of a PM-written steer request (`steer-dp2.md`). Kept as\n * the consumer-side contract (`worker-mode` strips exactly this line); the\n * machine loop no longer writes the file itself (T03). */\nexport const DP2_STEER_REQUEST_HEADER = \"[dp2-narrow-request]\";\n\n/** dp2 question set in the canonical form Python hashes: `json.dumps(list(\n * questions), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"))`\n * (decision_points.py::_questions_version). */\nconst DP2_QUESTIONS_CANONICAL =\n\t'[{\"choices\":[\"narrow\",\"split\",\"direct-exec\",\"escalate\"],\"id\":\"checkpoint_action\",\"type\":\"choice\"}]';\n\n/** `questions_version` for dp2 = `q-<sha256(canonical questions)[:8]>`, i.e. the\n * exact short code the Python registry derives (D-026). The design's dp2\n * input asks for \"最近 ≤3 条 (elapsed_s, reads, writes)\" — enough to tell \"still\n * climbing\" from \"stalled\" without shipping any L2 material. */\nexport interface Dp2CheckpointPoint {\n\telapsedMin: number;\n\treads: number;\n\twrites: number;\n}\n\n/** Line prefix of the convergence checkpoint (format: worker/output-writer.ts\n * `appendCheckpoint`, parsed in full by shared/heartbeat.ts CHECKPOINT_LINE_RE).\n * Re-scanned here only because {@link readTaskProgress} keeps the LAST line,\n * while dp2 needs the series plus the checkpoint sequence (`#ckpt<N>`). */\nconst DP2_CHECKPOINT_LINE_RE =\n\t/^\\[CHECKPOINT\\] \\S+ elapsed=(\\d+)s reads=(\\d+) writes=(\\d+) phases=\\S+ uniq_targets=\\d+ repeat_top=\\d+ risk=(?:low|mid|high)/;\n\n/** Checkpoint series of one task dir: `total` is the number of `[CHECKPOINT]`\n * lines (the `#ckpt<N>` sequence number), `points` the last `limit` of them in\n * file order. (value as Record<string, unknown>)\n\t\t: undefined;\n}\n\n/** RETIRED (2026-10-23 user revision, mw-decision-context T08): the automatic\n * dp2 seam that lived here (`buildDp2CheckpointState`, `decideDp2Checkpoint`,\n * the artifact/header helpers and the steer/narrow fallback) is gone. dp2 is a\n * PM-INITIATED decision only: the checkpoint loop wakes the PM and the PM asks\n * through the managed `ask_decision` tool with its own business material. Pure; the caller supplies the\n * already-read `acked` set so one tick reads `_workers.acked` at most once. */\nfunction countUnreadTerminal(\n\tentries: readonly WorkerEntry[],\n\tacked: ReadonlySet<string>,\n\treadbackDelivered: ReadonlySet<string>,\n): number {\n\tlet n = 0;\n\tfor (const e of entries) {\n\t\tif (!isTerminal(e.status)) continue;\n\t\tif (acked.has(e.taskKey) || readbackDelivered.has(e.taskKey)) continue;\n\t\tn += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn n;\n}\n\nexport type PhaseDocName = \"spec.md\" | \"design.md\" | \"plan.md\";\n\ninterface DocWriteTarget {\n\tkey: string;\n\tdoc: PhaseDocName;\n}\n\n/** The phase-doc write/edit target, when the tool path resolves to\n * {agenticdocRoot}/{key}/spec.md | design.md | plan.md — the PM phase docs that\n * mean \"this window is now executing this key\". Any other path (or file) is\n * not a claim signal. */\nfunction docWriteTarget(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): DocWriteTarget | undefined {\n\tif (toolName !== \"write\" && toolName !== \"edit\") return undefined;\n\tconst filePath = (args as { path?: unknown } | undefined)?.path;\n\tif (typeof filePath !== \"string\" || filePath === \"\") return undefined;\n\tconst rel = path.relative(path.resolve(agenticdocRoot), path.resolve(projectDir, filePath));\n\tif (rel.startsWith(\"..\") || path.isAbsolute(rel)) return undefined; // outside .agenticdoc\n\tconst parts = rel.split(path.sep);\n\tconst doc = parts.length === 2 ? parts[1] : undefined;\n\tif (doc !== \"spec.md\" && doc !== \"design.md\" && doc !== \"plan.md\") return undefined;\n\tconst key = parts[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (!key || key.startsWith(\"_\") || key.startsWith(\".\")) return undefined;\n\treturn { key, doc };\n}\n\n/** The key a phase-doc write/edit belongs to (see docWriteTarget). */\nexport function keyFromDocWrite(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): string | undefined {\n\treturn docWriteTarget(toolName, args, projectDir, agenticdocRoot)?.key;\n}\n\n/** Which phase doc was written/edited (see docWriteTarget). */\nexport function docFromWrite(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): PhaseDocName | undefined {\n\treturn docWriteTarget(toolName, args, projectDir, agenticdocRoot)?.doc;\n}\n\nexport type EvidencePhase = \"spec\" | \"design\";\n\n/** The evidence-note write target, when the tool path resolves to\n * {agenticdocRoot}/{key}/evidence/research/spec-*.md | design-*.md. Not a\n * claim signal (only phase docs are) — but the moment evidence lands is the\n * moment an already-written phase doc's claims can be re-reviewed against\n * it. */\nexport function evidencePhaseFromWrite(\n\ttoolName: string,\n\targs: unknown,\n\tprojectDir: string,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n): { key: string; phase: EvidencePhase } | undefined {\n\tif (toolName !== \"write\" && toolName !== \"edit\") return undefined;\n\tconst filePath = (args as { path?: unknown } | undefined)?.path;\n\tif (typeof filePath !== \"string\" || filePath === \"\") return undefined;\n\tconst rel = path.relative(path.resolve(agenticdocRoot), path.resolve(projectDir, filePath));\n\tif (rel.startsWith(\"..\") || path.isAbsolute(rel)) return undefined; // outside .agenticdoc\n\tconst parts = rel.split(path.sep);\n\tif (parts.length !== 4 || parts[1] !== \"evidence\" || parts[2] !== \"research\") return undefined;\n\tconst note = parts[3] ?? \"\";\n\tif (!note.endsWith(\".md\")) return undefined;\n\tconst phase: EvidencePhase | undefined = note.startsWith(\"spec-\")\n\t\t? \"spec\"\n\t\t: note.startsWith(\"design-\")\n\t\t\t? \"design\"\n\t\t\t: undefined;\n\tif (!phase) return undefined;\n\tconst key = parts[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (!key || key.startsWith(\"_\") || key.startsWith(\".\")) return undefined;\n\treturn { key, phase };\n}\n\n/** UI notice when a phase doc and its research evidence coexist — the\n * \"re-review when evidence is generated\" protocol, as a *notice*, not an\n * injected instruction (mw-evidence-nudge-notify): the old sendUserMessage\n * form made the model treat the automatic nudge as the user ordering an\n * immediate review pass, so the window agent started rewriting the doc with\n * no consent and no chance to veto, hijacking the turn. Fires once per (key, phase) per session, only when both the phase\n * doc (>= 500 bytes) and >= 1 evidence note exist: the review needs both\n * sides of the comparison. */\nexport function evidenceReviewNotice(\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n\tkey: string,\n\tphase: EvidencePhase,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tnotified: Set<string>,\n): void {\n\tconst dedup = `${key}:${phase}`;\n\tif (notified.has(dedup)) return;\n\tconst docs = readPhaseDocs(agenticdocRoot, key);\n\tconst docOk = phase === \"spec\" ? docs.spec : docs.design;\n\tconst evidence = phase === \"spec\" ? docs.specEvidence : docs.designEvidence;\n\tif (!docOk || evidence < 1) return;\n\tnotified.add(dedup);\n\tconst doc = phase === \"spec\" ? \"spec.md\" : \"design.md\";\n\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t`[mw] ${key}: ${phase} 阶段证据已就位（${evidence} 份 research note）——建议对照 evidence/research/ 复查 ${doc}（断言-证据对照 / 数字口径 / 内部一致性 / 可证伪性）。何时执行复查由你决定。`,\n\t\t\"info\",\n\t);\n}\n\n/** Nudge the user toward the /goal brainstorm when the project goal is not\n * yet established. Writing design.md / plan.md also\n * runs the next-phase evidence gate (mirrors advance_phase.py): the previous\n * phase's research notes must exist, or the user is warned immediately. */\nexport async function autoTakeOverFromDoc(\n\tpi: ExtensionAPI,\n\tindexStore: IndexStore,\n\twatch: PmWatchState,\n\trefreshWatch: (ctx: ExtensionContext) => void,\n\tkey: string,\n\tdoc: PhaseDocName,\n\tagenticdocRoot: string,\n\tctx: ExtensionContext,\n): Promise<void> {\n\t// Next-phase evidence gate: writing design.md means the spec phase should be\n\t// complete (its research notes exist); writing plan.md means design should be.\n\t// Fires regardless of takeover idempotency — the missing evidence is the\n\t// message, and it stays true until the notes are written.\n\tconst docs = readPhaseDocs(agenticdocRoot, key);\n\tif (doc === \"spec.md\" && docs.specEvidence < 1) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/spec-*.md found — write the research notes (or a zero-research declaration) alongside the spec; the advance-to-design gate checks them.`,\n\t\t\t\"warning\",\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tif (doc === \"design.md\" && docs.specEvidence < 1) {\n\t\tctx.ui.notify(\n\t\t\t`[mw] ${key}: no evidence/research/spec-*.md found — the advance-to-design gate requires >= 1 research note (a zero-research declaration counts).
