len: number } | undefined,\n): { char: string; len: number } | undefined {\n\tconst match = CLAIMS_FENCE_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (match === null) return open;\n\tconst marker = match[1] ?? \"\";\n\tconst rest = match[2] ?? \"\";\n\tconst char = marker[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (open === undefined) return { char, len: marker.length };\n\tif (char === open.char && marker.length >= open.len && rest.trim() === \"\") return undefined;\n\treturn open;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fold the full-width forms the card corpus mixes in (P-048): `：` -> `:`,\n * `｜` -> `|`, full-width digits -> ASCII digits, ideographic space -> space.\n */\nfunction normalizeClaimText(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/[\\uFF10-\\uFF19]/g, (digit) => String.fromCharCode(digit.charCodeAt(0) - 0xfee0))\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF1A/g, \":\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF5C/g, \"|\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\u3000/g, \" \")\n\t\t.trim();\n}\n\n/** Cells never carry markdown code fences: strip the backticks a writer adds. */\nfunction stripClaimTicks(text: string): string {\n\treturn text.replace(/`/g, \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** Split a `| a | b |` row into trimmed cells (leading/trailing pipes dropped). */\nfunction splitClaimRow(line: string): string[] {\n\tconst cells = normalizeClaimText(line).split(\"|\");\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[0] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.shift();\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[cells.length - 1] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.pop();\n\treturn cells.map((cell) => cell.trim());\n}\n\n/** Header of a claims table, `undefined` when the row is not a claims header. */\nfunction matchClaimHeader(cells: string[]): ClaimColumns | undefined {\n\tconst columns: ClaimColumns = {};\n\tlet hasClaimColumn = false;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst name = stripClaimTicks(normalizeClaimText(cells[i] ?? \"\"))\n\t\t\t.toLowerCase()\n\t\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t\t.replace(/:$/, \"\");\n\t\tfor (const [field, aliases] of CLAIM_COLUMN_ALIASES) {\n\t\t\tif (!aliases.includes(name)) continue;\n\t\t\tif (columns[field] === undefined) columns[field] = i;\n\t\t\tif (field === \"id\") hasClaimColumn = true;\n\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn hasClaimColumn ? columns : undefined;\n}\n\n/** `| --- | --- |` separator row (any dash count, optional alignment colons). */\nfunction isClaimSeparatorRow(cells: string[]): boolean {\n\tif (cells.length === 0) return false;\n\treturn cells.every((cell) => cell === \"\" || /^:?-{1,}:?$/.test(cell));\n}\n\n/** Cell of `field` in `cells`, `\"\"` when the column is absent (P-048). */\nfunction claimCell(cells: string[], columns: ClaimColumns, field: ClaimField): string {\n\tconst index = columns[field];\n\tif (index === undefined) return \"\";\n\treturn (cells[index] ?? \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse the card's `<!-- mw-claims: v1 -->` block (design §2.1).\n *\n * Tolerance is the contract, not a nicety (P-048: an over-strict schema caused\n * 30 minutes of consecutive false refusals): the block end falls back to the\n * next H2 or EOF, column order is free, extra columns are ignored, header\n * words take aliases, full-width `：｜`/digits fold to ASCII, and fenced code\n * blocks contribute nothing. An unparsable row is reported as\n * `claim:<row>:unparsable` and skipped — this function never throws.\n */\nexport function parseClaimsBlock(text: string): ClaimBlock {\n\tconst block: ClaimBlock = { present: false, claims: [], errors: [] };\n\tconst byId = new Map<string, Claim>();\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tlet inBlock = false;\n\tlet columns: ClaimColumns | undefined;\n\tconst lines = splitLines(text);\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst line = lines[i] ?? \"\";\n\t\tfence = advanceClaimFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tif (!inBlock) {\n\t\t\tif (CLAIMS_OPEN_RE.test(line)) {\n\t\t\t\tinBlock = true;\n\t\t\t\tblock.present = true;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (CLAIMS_CLOSE_RE.test(line) || CLAIMS_STOP_H2_RE.test(line)) {\n\t\t\tinBlock = false;\n\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (!normalizeClaimText(line).startsWith(\"|\")) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst cells = splitClaimRow(line);\n\t\tif (columns === undefined) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = matchClaimHeader(cells);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (isClaimSeparatorRow(cells)) continue;\n\t\tconst claim = claimFromRow(cells, columns, i + 1, byId);\n\t\tif (claim === undefined) {\n\t\t\tblock.errors.push(`claim:${i + 1}:unparsable`);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tblock.claims.push(claim);\n\t\tbyId.set(claim.id, claim);\n\t}\n\treturn block;\n}\n\n/** One table row -> {@link Claim}, `undefined` when the row cannot be parsed. */\nfunction claimFromRow(\n\tcells: string[],\n\tcolumns: ClaimColumns,\n\trow: number,\n\tbyId: ReadonlyMap<string, Claim>,\n): Claim | undefined {\n\tconst idMatch = CLAIM_ID_RE.exec(stripClaimTicks(claimCell(cells, columns, \"id\")));\n\tif (idMatch === null) return undefined;\n\tconst number = idMatch[1] ?? \"\";\n\tconst child = idMatch[2];\n\tconst parent = child === undefined ? \"\" : `C-${number}`;\n\tconst id = `C-${number}${child === undefined ? \"\" : `.${child}`}`;\n\tif (parent !== \"\") {\n\t\t// RQ-3 §5.1 / B-10: a `父.序号` child row is only legal under a `struct`\n\t\t// parent (a struct enumerates the sub-items of one shape).\n\t\tconst parentClaim = byId.get(parent);\n\t\tif (parentClaim === undefined || parentClaim.type !== \"struct\") return undefined;\n\t}\n\tconst declaredType = stripClaimTicks(claimCell(cells, columns, \"type\")).toLowerCase();\n\tconst budgetText = stripClaimTicks(claimCell(cells, columns, \"budget\"));\n\treturn {\n\t\tid,\n\t\t// A struct child restates part of the parent shape, so an empty `类型`\n\t\t// cell inherits `struct` instead of manufacturing a second gap.\n\t\ttype: declaredType === \"\" && parent !== \"\" ? \"struct\" : declaredType,\n\t\tparent,\n\t\tstatement: claimCell(cells, columns, \"statement\"),\n\t\tfalsifier: claimCell(cells, columns, \"falsifier\"),\n\t\tlocator: claimCell(cells, columns, \"locator\"),\n\t\tjudgement: claimCell(cells, columns, \"judgement\"),\n\t\tbudget: /^\\d+$/.test(budgetText) ? Number(budgetText) : Number.NaN,\n\t\trow,\n\t};\n}\n\n// ── claims: 校验 / validation (design §2.1, AC-001) ──────────────────────────\n\n/** `判据` prefix each self-reported type must carry (design §2.1). */\nconst CLAIM_TYPE_PREFIX: Readonly<Record<ClaimType, string>> = {\n\tcmd: \"cmd:\",\n\tgrep: \"grep:\",\n\tstruct: \"shape:\",\n\tmanual: \"manual:\",\n};\n\n/** `Σ预算` cap, manual rows counted twice (AC-001 ⑤). */\nconst CLAIM_BUDGET_SUM_MAX = 40;\n/** `manual` cap numerator of `min(4, ceil(n/3))` (AC-001 ⑤, RQ-3 §6.1). */\nconst CLAIM_MANUAL_CAP = 4;\n/** Normalized-similarity threshold of the tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5). */\nconst CLAIM_TAUTOLOGY_SIMILARITY = 0.9;\n/** Above this size a `定位` must name a line range (AC-001 ④). */\nconst CLAIM_LOCATOR_RANGE_BYTES = 32768;\n/** D-005: a `cmd` locator is the PM's pre-executed evidence file row. */\nconst CLAIM_CMD_LOCATOR_RE = /^evidence\\/claims\\/[^#\\s]+#(C-\\d{2,3}(?:\\.\\d+)?)$/i;\n\n/** Resolution outcome of one `定位` cell. */\ninterface ClaimLocatorTarget {\n\tkind: \"skipped\" | \"unresolved\" | \"resolved\";\n\tsize: number;\n\t/** The locator named an explicit `path:a-b` line segment. */\n\tranged: boolean;\n}\n\n/** A locator names a file when it has a separator or a file extension. */\nfunction looksLikeClaimPath(text: string): boolean {\n\tif (text.includes(\"/\")) return true;\n\treturn /\\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,7}$/.test(text);\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve a `定位` cell against `projectDir` without reading content: only\n * `statSync` runs (design §3.1). A bare symbol, a missing file, a non-file and\n * a path outside `projectDir` are all `unresolved` (never a throw).\n */\nfunction resolveClaimLocator(locator: string, projectDir: string): ClaimLocatorTarget {\n\tconst raw = stripClaimTicks(locator);\n\tif (raw === \"\" || raw === \"-\") return { kind: \"skipped\", size: 0, ranged: false };\n\tconst withoutFragment = raw.replace(/#.*$/, \"\");\n\tconst range = /^(.*?):(\\d+)(?:-(\\d+))?$/.exec(withoutFragment);\n\tconst pathText = (range === null ? withoutFragment : (range[1] ?? \"\")).trim();\n\tconst ranged = range !== null && range[3] !== undefined;\n\tif (pathText === \"\" || !looksLikeClaimPath(pathText)) return { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\tconst absolute = path.resolve(projectDir, pathText);\n\tconst relative = path.relative(projectDir, absolute);\n\tif (relative === \"\" || relative === \"..\" || relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {\n\t\treturn { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\t}\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst stat = fs.statSync(absolute);\n\t\tif (!stat.isFile()) return { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\t\treturn { kind: \"resolved\", size: stat.size, ranged };\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\t}\n}\n\n/**\n * Negation / absence words plus aspect fillers stripped before the tautology\n * similarity test, so that \"X 已修复\" vs \"X 未修复\" compares the same\n * remainder (RQ-3 B-5: the whole point is that a minimal rewrite only differs\n * by these words). Longest-first so `不再` wins over `不` and `已经` over `已`.\n */\nconst CLAIM_NEGATION_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\n\t\"已经\",\n\t\"不再\",\n\t\"不会\",\n\t\"不能\",\n\t\"不得\",\n\t\"没有\",\n\t\"无法\",\n\t\"禁止\",\n\t\"absent\",\n\t\"cannot\",\n\t\"didn't\",\n\t\"doesn't\",\n\t\"failed\",\n\t\"fails\",\n\t\"isn't\",\n\t\"aren't\",\n\t\"missing\",\n\t\"never\",\n\t\"without\",\n\t\"can't\",\n\t\"fail\",\n\t\"not\",\n\t\"已\",\n\t\"不\",\n\t\"未\",\n\t\"无\",\n\t\"非\",\n\t\"否\",\n\t\"缺\",\n].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length);\n\n/** Drop negation words (ASCII ones with word boundaries), then all separators. */\nfunction normalizeClaimSimilarityText(text: string): string {\n\tlet out = text.toLowerCase().replace(/`/g, \" \");\n\tfor (const token of CLAIM_NEGATION_TOKENS) {\n\t\tout = /^[a-z']+$/.test(token) ? out.replace(new RegExp(`\\\\b${token}\\\\b`, \"gi\"), \" \") : out.split(token).join(\" \");\n\t}\n\treturn out.replace(/[^\\p{L}\\p{N}]+/gu, \"\");\n}\n\n/** Levenshtein distance over code points (both inputs are short in practice). */\nfunction claimEditDistance(a: string, b: string): number {\n\tconst left = Array.from(a);\n\tconst right = Array.from(b);\n\tlet previous: number[] = right.map((_, index) => index);\n\tprevious = [0, ...previous];\n\tfor (let i = 1; i <= left.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst current: number[] = [i];\n\t\tfor (let j = 1; j <= right.length; j++) {\n\t\t\tconst cost = left[i - 1] === right[j - 1] ? 0 : 1;\n\t\t\tcurrent[j] = Math.min(\n\t\t\t\t(previous[j] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) + 1,\n\t\t\t\t(current[j - 1] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) + 1,\n\t\t\t\t(previous[j - 1] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) + cost,\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t}\n\t\tprevious = current;\n\t}\n\treturn previous[right.length] ?? 0;\n}\n\n/** Artifact tokens (paths, symbols, commands) that a `判据` can point at. */\nconst CLAIM_ARTIFACT_TOKEN_RE = /[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*/g;\n\n/** Artifact tokens of a `判据`, with the leading type prefix removed. */\nfunction claimJudgementArtifacts(judgement: string): string[] {\n\tconst body = judgement.replace(/^\\s*(?:cmd|grep|shape|manual)\\s*:\\s*/i, \"\");\n\tconst tokens = body.match(CLAIM_ARTIFACT_TOKEN_RE) ?? [];\n\treturn tokens.filter((token) => token.length >= 3);\n}\n\n/**\n * Tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5): `陈述` and `反证条件` become the same text once\n * negation words are dropped (similarity >= 0.90) AND the `判据` names no\n * artifact that `陈述` does not already name. Any new artifact (path, symbol,\n * command) means the claim is still falsifiable, so it is not tautological.\n */\nfunction isTautologicalClaim(claim: Claim): boolean {\n\tif (claim.statement === \"\" || claim.falsifier === \"\" || claim.judgement === \"\") return false;\n\tconst statement = normalizeClaimSimilarityText(claim.statement);\n\tconst falsifier = normalizeClaimSimilarityText(claim.falsifier);\n\tif (statement === \"\" || falsifier === \"\") return false;\n\tconst distance = claimEditDistance(statement, falsifier);\n\tconst similarity = 1 - distance / Math.max(statement.length, falsifier.length);\n\tif (similarity < CLAIM_TAUTOLOGY_SIMILARITY) return false;\n\tconst haystack = claim.statement.toLowerCase();\n\treturn !claimJudgementArtifacts(claim.judgement).some((token) => !haystack.includes(token.toLowerCase()));\n}\n\n/** Options of {@link claimsGaps}. */\nexport interface ClaimsGapOptions {\n\t/** Absolute project root the `定位` paths resolve against. */\n\tprojectDir: string;\n\t/** `true` upgrades the advisory findings to gaps (D-006 grey release). */\n\tenforce: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge a parsed claims block (design §2.1/§3.1, AC-001). Never throws.\n *\n * Structural gaps (`type` / `statement` / `falsifier` / `locator` /\n * `judgement` / `budget`) are gaps in both modes: a claim missing a required\n * cell is not a claim. The soft findings — `type-prefix`, `cmd-locator`,\n * `locator-unresolved`, `locator-range`, `tautology` and the two `claims:*`\n * aggregates — are returned only when `opts.enforce` is true; an advisory\n * caller gets `[]` for them here and can re-query with `enforce: true` to\n * render the same string list as warnings (D-006: advisory warns, never\n * refuses).\n *\n * Item shapes are frozen because T-02 concatenates them into the refusal text:\n * `claim:<id>:<element>` and `claims:<rule>:<detail>`.\n */\nexport function claimsGaps(block: ClaimBlock, opts: ClaimsGapOptions): string[] {\n\tconst structural: string[] = [];\n\tconst advisory: string[] = [];\n\tlet budgetSum = 0;\n\tlet manualCount = 0;\n\tfor (const claim of block.claims) {\n\t\tconst type = claim.type.toLowerCase();\n\t\tconst known = (CLAIM_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(type);\n\t\tbudgetSum += type === \"manual\" ? 2 : 1;\n\t\tif (type === \"manual\") manualCount += 1;\n\t\tif (!known) structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:type`);\n\t\tif (claim.statement === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:statement`);\n\t\tif (claim.falsifier === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:falsifier`);\n\t\tif (claim.locator === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:locator`);\n\t\tif (claim.judgement === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:judgement`);\n\t\tif (!Number.isInteger(claim.budget) || claim.budget < 0) structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:budget`);\n\t\tif (!known) continue;\n\t\tif (claim.judgement !== \"\") {\n\t\t\tconst prefix = CLAIM_TYPE_PREFIX[type as ClaimType];\n\t\t\tif (!claim.judgement.trim().toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix)) advisory.push(`claim:${claim.id}:type-prefix`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (type === \"cmd\" && claim.locator !== \"\") {\n\t\t\tconst cmdLocator = CLAIM_CMD_LOCATOR_RE.exec(stripClaimTicks(claim.locator));\n\t\t\tif (cmdLocator === null || (cmdLocator[1] ?? \"\").toUpperCase() !== claim.id.toUpperCase()) {\n\t\t\t\tadvisory.push(`claim:${claim.id}:cmd-locator`);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst target = resolveClaimLocator(claim.locator, opts.projectDir);\n\t\tif (target.kind === \"unresolved\") advisory.push(`claim:${claim.id}:locator-unresolved`);\n\t\tif (target.kind === \"resolved\" && target.size > CLAIM_LOCATOR_RANGE_BYTES && !target.ranged) {\n\t\t\tadvisory.push(`claim:${claim.id}:locator-range`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (isTautologicalClaim(claim)) advisory.push(`claim:${claim.id}:tautology`);\n\t}\n\tconst total = block.claims.length;\n\tif (budgetSum > CLAIM_BUDGET_SUM_MAX) advisory.push(`claims:budget-sum:${budgetSum}>${CLAIM_BUDGET_SUM_MAX}`);\n\tconst manualCap = Math.min(CLAIM_MANUAL_CAP, Math.ceil(total / 3));\n\tif (manualCount > manualCap) advisory.push(`claims:manual-overflow:${manualCount}/${total}`);\n\treturn opts.enforce ? [...structural, ...advisory] : structural;\n}\n\n// ── claims: 预算 / budget (design §4, AC-003) ────────────────────────────────\n\n/**\n * Read-scope caps derived from the claims block (design §4):\n * `fileCap = min(30, Σ(manual ? 2 : 1))`, `byteCap = min(393,216, 65,536 × n)`.\n * No claims means no derived cap — `{ fileCap: 0, byteCap: 0 }` lets the caller\n * keep the project-level default instead of zeroing a read budget.\n */\nexport function claimBudgetCaps(claims: Claim[]): { fileCap: number; byteCap: number } {\n\tif (claims.length === 0) return { fileCap: 0, byteCap: 0 };\n\tlet weightSum = 0;\n\tfor (const claim of claims) weightSum += claim.type.toLowerCase() === \"manual\" ? 2 : 1;\n\treturn {\n\t\tfileCap: Math.min(CLAIM_BUDGET.callCap, weightSum),\n\t\tbyteCap: Math.min(CLAIM_BUDGET.byteCapMax, CLAIM_BUDGET.claimByteCap * claims.length),\n\t};\n}\n"]}

Adding a role means changing\n * this tuple once.\n */\nexport const DISPATCH_TYPE_VOCABULARY = [\n\t\"coding\",\n\t\"review\",\n\t\"research\",\n\t\"rag-research\",\n\t\"vision\",\n\t// Decision-book writer (mw-decision-substitution W8, renamed W10): a role\n\t// that only fills a decision book from evidence, never edits code. The type\n\t// value is `decide_prepare` (was `decision`; no alias kept).\n\t\"decide_prepare\",\n\t\"verifier\",\n\t\"reviewer\",\n\t\"repair\",\n\t\"phase-writer\",\n\t\"roadmap-writer\",\n\t\"codex\",\n] as const;\n\n/** Is `type` part of the single-source dispatch vocabulary? */\nexport function isKnownDispatchType(type: string): boolean {\n\treturn (DISPATCH_TYPE_VOCABULARY as readonly string[]).includes(type);\n}\n\n/**\n * Known dispatchable roles that carry no envelope extras in this key.\n * Kept as an exported subset of {@link DISPATCH_TYPE_VOCABULARY} for the\n * Python mirror and audit consumers; the extras check now consults the\n * vocabulary directly, so this is descriptive rather than exhaustive.\n */\nexport const TYPES_WITHOUT_EXTRA_RULES: readonly string[] = [\"vision\", \"rag-research\"];\n\n/** Item-name patterns for `typeExtrasMissing`; keys mirror `TYPE_EXTRA_SECTIONS`. */\nconst TYPE_EXTRA_PATTERNS: Readonly<Record<string, ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, RegExp]>>> = {\n\tcoding: [\n\t\t[\"写入允许面\", /写入允许面|允许写入|允许写|写入范围|写面|write_scope|allow[-_ ]?write/i],\n\t\t[\"写入禁止面\", /写入禁止面|禁止写入|禁止写|不得写|写入禁区|禁止范围|deny[-_ ]?write|forbid/i],\n\t\t[\"验收命令\", /验收命令|验证命令|验收标准|验收判据|验收方式|验收|完成判据|acceptance/i],\n\t\t[\"改动历史\", /改动历史|改动清单|变更历史|写入事件|trace\\.log|write[-_ ]?history|change[-_ ]?log/i],\n\t],\n\tresearch: [[\"唯一证据文件\", /唯一证据文件|唯一证据|唯一产物|仅此一写|sole[-_ ]?evidence/i]],\n\tdecide_prepare: [\n\t\t[\"dp\", /^\\s*(?:[-*+]\\s*)?(?:\\*\\*)?dp(?:\\*\\*)?\\s*[:：]/im],\n\t\t[\"证据来源\", /证据来源|证据清单|证据出处|evidence[-_ ]?sources?/i],\n\t\t[\"分支后果\", /分支后果|各分支|后果说明|branch[-_ ]?(consequences?|outcomes?)/i],\n\t\t[\"allow-send\", /allow[-_ ]?send/i],\n\t],\n\treview: [\n\t\t[\"审计目标\", /审计目标|审计问题|审计对象|审计范围|审计维度|问题域|要回答|audit[-_ ]?(target|scope|question)/i],\n\t\t[\n\t\t\t\"未覆盖面声明\",\n\t\t\t/未覆盖面|未覆盖声明|未覆盖范围|未及范围|未查看|未探索|未涉及|not[-_ ]?covered|out[-_ ]?of[-_ ]?scope/i,\n\t\t],\n\t],\n};\n\n// ── Text primitives ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nconst HEADING_RE = /^(#{2,6})\\s+(.*)$/;\nconst BULLET_LABEL_RE = /^\\s*(?:[-*+]|\\d+[.)])\\s+(?:\\*\\*)?([^:：]{1,48}?)(?:\\*\\*)?\\s*[:：]/;\nconst FIELD_LABEL_RE = /^\\s*(?:\\*\\*)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,40})(?:\\*\\*)?\\s*:/;\n\n/**\n * A `type:` declaration anywhere in the card prologue. The historical card\n * corpus has almost no fenced `type:` header (0/345 cards, RQ-2), while the\n * live PM convention writes it inline in the metadata prologue\n * (`- Key: …｜type: coding`, `> key: … | type: coding`); a header-only reader\n * would reject every real card, so the prologue is the card-level header.\n * The lookbehind alternation also accepts the bare `type: …` frontmatter form.\n */\nconst CARD_TYPE_RE = /(?:^|[\\s|｜>*+-])type:\\s*([^\\s|｜]+)/;\n\n/**\n * Same newline folding as `shared/task-frontmatter.ts` so both sides index one\n * `\\n` space: `\\r\\n`, `\\r`, U+2028, U+2029 fold to `\\n`, one trailing empty\n * line drops, each line trims. A leading BOM is stripped first.\n */\nfunction splitLines(text: string): string[] {\n\tconst lines = (text.startsWith(\"\\uFEFF\") ? text.slice(1) : text).replace(/\\r\\n?|[\\u2028\\u2029]/g, \"\\n\").split(\"\\n\");\n\tif (lines.length > 1 && lines[lines.length - 1] === \"\") lines.pop();\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) lines[i] = lines[i].replace(/\\r$/, \"\").trim();\n\treturn lines;\n}\n\n/**\n * First `type:` declaration in the card prologue (lines before the first H2\n * heading), `\"\"` when absent or empty. Everything at or below the first H2 is\n * body: a `type:` written there must not flip the role (the same rule as\n * `task-frontmatter.ts::readTaskType`'s F-10 body-type exclusion).\n */\nfunction readCardType(lines: string[]): string {\n\t// P-08 single source (T-07): `shared/task-frontmatter.ts::readTaskType` owns\n\t// the `type:` header semantics (fence -> first blank line -> key run; a body\n\t// `type:` never flips the role). A live PM card that writes\n\t// `- Key: ...｜type: coding` below a blank line sits outside that header\n\t// region, so the card-prologue scan below is the fallback — it never\n\t// overrides a value the shared reader already found, and it never reads a\n\t// `type:` below the first H2 (F-10). readEnvelope's verdict is unchanged.\n\tconst shared = readTaskType(lines.join(\"\\n\")).type;\n\tif (shared !== undefined && shared !== \"\") return shared.trim();\n\tconst firstHeading = lines.findIndex((line) => HEADING_RE.test(line));\n\tconst end = firstHeading === -1 ? lines.length : firstHeading;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < end; i++) {\n\t\tconst match = CARD_TYPE_RE.exec(lines[i]);\n\t\tif (match) return match[1].trim();\n\t}\n\treturn \"\";\n}\n\n/** Strip a leading `1.` / `1.2.` / `(2)` / `A.` / `一、` numbering prefix. */\nfunction stripNumbering(text: string): string {\n\tlet out = text.trim();\n\tout = out.replace(/^[（(]\\s*[0-9A-Za-z一二三四五六七八九十]+\\s*[)）]\\s*/, \"\");\n\tout = out.replace(/^[0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]+)*\\s*[.、)）]\\s*/, \"\");\n\tout = out.replace(/^[A-Za-z]\\s*[.、)）]\\s*/, \"\");\n\tout = out.replace(/^[一二三四五六七八九十]+\\s*[、.)）]\\s*/, \"\");\n\treturn out.trim();\n}\n\n/** First heading family the heading belongs to (deliverables > context > requirements). */\nfunction classifyHeading(heading: string): EnvelopeSection | undefined {\n\tconst lower = heading.toLowerCase();\n\tfor (const [section, tokens] of ENVELOPE_HEADING_FAMILIES) {\n\t\tfor (const token of tokens) {\n\t\t\tif (lower.startsWith(token.toLowerCase())) return section;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn undefined;\n}\n\n/** A bullet/field label in the card (`- 允许写：…`, `write_scope: …`). */\nfunction labelOf(line: string): string | undefined {\n\tconst bullet = BULLET_LABEL_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (bullet) return bullet[1].trim();\n\tconst field = FIELD_LABEL_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (field) return field[1].trim();\n\treturn undefined;\n}\n\nfunction anyLabelMatches(lines: string[], keyRe: RegExp): boolean {\n\tfor (const line of lines) {\n\t\tconst label = labelOf(line);\n\t\tif (label !== undefined && keyRe.test(label)) return true;\n\t}\n\treturn false;\n}\n\ninterface Heading {\n\tlevel: number;\n\ttext: string;\n\tline: number;\n}\n\nfunction collectHeadings(lines: string[]): Heading[] {\n\tconst headings: Heading[] = [];\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst match = HEADING_RE.exec(lines[i]);\n\t\tif (match) headings.push({ level: match[1].length, text: stripNumbering(match[2]), line: i });\n\t}\n\treturn headings;\n}\n\nfunction bodySemanticHit(section: EnvelopeSection, lines: string[]): boolean {\n\tif (lines.some((line) => ENVELOPE_BODY_HINTS[section].test(line))) return true;\n\treturn anyLabelMatches(lines, ENVELOPE_BULLET_KEYS[section]);\n}\n\nfunction detectSections(lines: string[]): EnvelopeDetected {\n\tconst detected: EnvelopeDetected = { context: \"\", requirements: \"\", deliverables: \"\" };\n\tconst headings = collectHeadings(lines);\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < headings.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst heading = headings[i];\n\t\tconst section = classifyHeading(heading.text);\n\t\tif (section === undefined || detected[section] !== \"\") continue;\n\t\tlet end = lines.length;\n\t\tfor (let j = i + 1; j < headings.length; j++) {\n\t\t\tif (headings[j].level <= heading.level) {\n\t\t\t\tend = headings[j].line;\n\t\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tlet hasBody = false;\n\t\tfor (let k = heading.line + 1; k < end; k++) {\n\t\t\tif (lines[k] !== \"\") {\n\t\t\t\thasBody = true;\n\t\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (hasBody) detected[section] = `heading:${heading.text}`;\n\t}\n\tfor (const section of ENVELOPE_SECTIONS) {\n\t\tif (detected[section] === \"\" && bodySemanticHit(section, lines)) detected[section] = \"semantics\";\n\t}\n\treturn detected;\n}\n\n// ── Public judgement ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/** The empty detection record (used for unreadable cards). */\nfunction emptyDetected(): EnvelopeDetected {\n\treturn { context: \"\", requirements: \"\", deliverables: \"\" };\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge an already-read card body (pure; no fs). Exported so a caller that\n * already holds the text (queue row, corpus scan) shares the exact judgement\n * instead of re-implementing it.\n */\nexport function inspectEnvelope(text: string): EnvelopeCheck {\n\tconst lines = splitLines(text);\n\tconst type = readCardType(lines);\n\tconst detected = detectSections(lines);\n\tconst missing: string[] = [];\n\tif (type === \"\") missing.push(\"type\");\n\tfor (const section of ENVELOPE_SECTIONS) {\n\t\tif (detected[section] === \"\") missing.push(section);\n\t}\n\treturn { ok: missing.length === 0, missing, type, detected };\n}\n\n/**\n * Read a task card and report its envelope status. A missing/unreadable card\n * yields `missing: [\"file\"]` (all sections absent) so the caller can name the\n * path it was given; every other finding is a normal `ok: false` report.\n */\nexport function readEnvelope(cardPath: string): EnvelopeCheck {\n\tlet text: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\ttext = fs.readFileSync(cardPath, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn { ok: false, missing: [\"file\"], type: \"\", detected: emptyDetected() };\n\t}\n\treturn inspectEnvelope(text);\n}\n\n/**\n * Type-specific gaps of `text` for `type`: the item names listed in\n * design.md §1.2 that the card does not declare, `[]` when none. An\n * unrecognised type returns `[\"unknown-type:<type>\"]` so the gate names the\n * role rather than silently passing it. Every role in the single-source\n * `DISPATCH_TYPE_VOCABULARY` (dispatchable roles + the runtime aliases +\n * legacy `codex`) is recognised here and carries no extras in this key.\n *\n * \"Declared\" is wide on purpose (heading, bullet/field label, or the canonical\n * item name anywhere in the card): the per-type extras exist to catch an\n * omitted contract, not to police wording (P-03).\n */\nexport function typeExtrasMissing(type: string, text: string): string[] {\n\tconst patterns = TYPE_EXTRA_PATTERNS[type];\n\tif (patterns === undefined) {\n\t\t// P-08: every in-use role is in the single-source vocabulary; only a\n\t\t// genuinely unknown value is named (keeps the unknown-type branch\n\t\t// discriminating without over-blocking the legacy/runtime roles).\n\t\treturn isKnownDispatchType(type) ? [] : [`unknown-type:${type}`];\n\t}\n\tconst lines = splitLines(text);\n\tconst missing: string[] = [];\n\tfor (const [item, pattern] of patterns) {\n\t\tif (text.includes(item)) continue;\n\t\tif (anyLabelMatches(lines, pattern)) continue;\n\t\tlet headingHit = false;\n\t\tfor (const line of lines) {\n\t\t\tconst heading = HEADING_RE.exec(line);\n\t\t\tif (heading && pattern.test(stripNumbering(heading[2]))) {\n\t\t\t\theadingHit = true;\n\t\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (!headingHit) missing.push(item);\n\t}\n\treturn missing;\n}\n\n// ── Seed minimum (T-12/F-05, AC-002 ①②) ─────────────────────────────────────\n\n/**\n * The seed four-item acceptance (AC-002 ①②) had no machine judge, so a card\n * that handed the worker no starting anchor passed the tool gate (F-05). The\n * judged minimum is deliberately just two items, both WIDE (P-03):\n *\n *  - a literal `goal.md` reference — the project-level goal anchor; and\n *  - at least one `path:line` reference — a resolvable starting point.\n *\n * The card's own 上下文/要求 sections are delivered verbatim as the seed already,\n * so they need no separate judgement here. This is the tool-layer (G-1)\n * criterion; the service layer re-checks the envelope + type extras on the\n * derived task.md, into which the card context (and so these references) is\n * injected.\n */\nexport const GOAL_ANCHOR = \"goal.md\";\nexport const SEED_GOAL_ITEM = \"seed:goal.md\";\nexport const SEED_PATH_ITEM = \"seed:path:line\";\n\n/** `name.ext:123` — a file reference with a line number. The dot + letter-init\n * extension requirement keeps times (`12:30`) and extensionless tokens out. */\nconst PATH_LINE_RE = /[A-Za-z0-9_][\\w./-]*\\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,7}:\\d+/;\n\n/** Seed items the card does not declare, `[]` when it declares both. */\nexport function seedItemsMissing(text: string): string[] {\n\tconst missing: string[] = [];\n\tif (!text.includes(GOAL_ANCHOR)) missing.push(SEED_GOAL_ITEM);\n\tif (!PATH_LINE_RE.test(text)) missing.push(SEED_PATH_ITEM);\n\treturn missing;\n}\n\n// ── claims: constants (design §2.1/§2.3, parity-locked by T-06) ─────────────\n\n/**\n * Self-reported judgement kind of one claim. The classifier never infers the\n * kind (agreement with the corpus is only 63.5%, RQ-3 §2.4); the card declares\n * it and {@link claimsGaps} only checks that the `判据` prefix agrees.\n */\nexport const CLAIM_TYPES = [\"cmd\", \"grep\", \"struct\", \"manual\"] as const;\n\n/** One member of {@link CLAIM_TYPES}. */\nexport type ClaimType = (typeof CLAIM_TYPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * `unverified` reason vocabulary (design §2.3). Single source: the Python\n * mirror (`autopilot/dispatch.py`) and the T-06 parity lock read this tuple\n * verbatim. Never write a second copy — the `ESCALATED_REASONS` precedent\n * (`packages/multi-workers/decision_points.py:111-120`) records exactly that\n * drift lesson.\n */\nexport const UNVERIFIED_REASONS = [\n\t\"budget\",\n\t\"no-access\",\n\t\"not-found\",\n\t\"ambiguous\",\n\t\"environment\",\n\t\"out-of-scope\",\n\t\"awaiting-input\",\n] as const;\n\n/** One member of {@link UNVERIFIED_REASONS}. */\nexport type UnverifiedReason = (typeof UNVERIFIED_REASONS)[number];\n\n/**\n * Default gate mode (D-006): `advisory` warns only, `enforce` refuses with zero\n * side effects. `MW_CLAIM_GATE=enforce` overrides it at runtime; both sides of\n * the TS/Python pair use the same constant and the same env name.\n */\nexport const CLAIM_GATE_DEFAULT = \"advisory\" as const;\n\n/**\n * Calibrated read budget of one dispatch unit (RQ-1 §5, D-007): 30 calls,\n * 393,216 B cumulative, from the p90 single-fetch cost (4,854 tokens) and the\n * <400k chars safe band. `perClaim` is the fetch allowance ONE claim buys\n * (D-014: `6 × n`, capped at `callCap`), `hardCap` the floor(177856/4977)\n * ceiling and `claimByteCap` the per-claim byte allowance. The separate `Σ预算`\n * planning weight (`manual` = 2) only prices the card for `claimsGaps`.\n */\nexport const CLAIM_BUDGET = {\n\tperClaim: 6,\n\tcallCap: 30,\n\thardCap: 35,\n\tclaimByteCap: 65536,\n\tbyteCapMax: 393216,\n} as const;\n\n/** One parsed claim row of the card's `<!-- mw-claims: v1 -->` block. */\nexport interface Claim {\n\t/** Normalized `C-01` / `C-01.3` id. */\n\tid: string;\n\t/** Lower-cased self-reported 类型, `\"\"` when the cell or column is absent. */\n\ttype: string;\n\t/** Parent id of a `C-01.3` child row, `\"\"` for a top-level claim. */\n\tparent: string;\n\tstatement: string;\n\tfalsifier: string;\n\tlocator: string;\n\tjudgement: string;\n\t/** Parsed 预算; `Number.NaN` when missing or not a non-negative integer. */\n\tbudget: number;\n\t/** 1-based line of the row in the parsed text (diagnostics only). */\n\trow: number;\n}\n\n/** Result of {@link parseClaimsBlock}. Never throws (P-048). */\nexport interface ClaimBlock {\n\t/** A `<!-- mw-claims: v1 -->` marker was seen outside a fence. */\n\tpresent: boolean;\n\tclaims: Claim[];\n\t/** `claim:<row>:unparsable` findings, row = 1-based source line. */\n\terrors: string[];\n}\n\n// ── claims: 解析 / parsing (design §2.1, P-048 tolerance) ────────────────────\n\n/** Opening marker of the card's claims block. */\nconst CLAIMS_OPEN_RE = /^<!--\\s*mw-claims\\s*:\\s*v1\\s*-->$/i;\n/** Closing marker; when absent the block tolerates up to the next H2. */\nconst CLAIMS_CLOSE_RE = /^<!--\\s*\\/\\s*mw-claims\\s*-->$/i;\n/** H2 on an already-trimmed line: the tolerance end of an unterminated block. */\nconst CLAIMS_STOP_H2_RE = /^##(?!#)\\s+/;\n/** Fence opener/closer; same semantics as `worker/output-sections.ts`. */\nconst CLAIMS_FENCE_RE = /^(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/;\n\n/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` (the `C` is case-insensitive, digits are 2-3 wide). */\nconst CLAIM_ID_RE = /^C-(\\d{2,3})(?:\\.(\\d+))?$/i;\n\ntype ClaimField = \"id\" | \"type\" | \"statement\" | \"falsifier\" | \"locator\" | \"judgement\" | \"budget\";\n\n/** Field -> header index of one parsed table, filled in header order. */\ntype ClaimColumns = Partial<Record<ClaimField, number>>;\n\n/**\n * Header aliases per field (P-048, RQ-3 §5.6): column order is free, extra\n * columns are ignored, and either script of the header word is accepted.\n */\nconst CLAIM_COLUMN_ALIASES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [ClaimField, readonly string[]]> = [\n\t[\"id\", [\"claim\", \"claim id\", \"claim id /\", \"断言\", \"断言 id\"]],\n\t[\"type\", [\"类型\", \"type\", \"类别\"]],\n\t[\"statement\", [\"陈述\", \"statement\", \"主张\", \"断言内容\"]],\n\t[\"falsifier\", [\"反证条件\", \"反证\", \"falsifier\", \"refutation\"]],\n\t[\"locator\", [\"定位\", \"locator\", \"anchor\", \"锚点\"]],\n\t[\"judgement\", [\"判据\", \"judgement\", \"judgment\", \"criterion\"]],\n\t[\"budget\", [\"预算\", \"budget\"]],\n];\n\n/** Tracks fenced-code-block state across lines (mirror of the worker copy). */\nfunction advanceClaimFence(\n\tline: string,\n\topen: { char: string; len: number } | undefined,\n): { char: string; len: number } | undefined {\n\tconst match = CLAIMS_FENCE_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (match === null) return open;\n\tconst marker = match[1] ?? \"\";\n\tconst rest = match[2] ?? \"\";\n\tconst char = marker[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (open === undefined) return { char, len: marker.length };\n\tif (char === open.char && marker.length >= open.len && rest.trim() === \"\") return undefined;\n\treturn open;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fold the full-width forms the card corpus mixes in (P-048): `：` -> `:`,\n * `｜` -> `|`, full-width digits -> ASCII digits, ideographic space -> space.\n */\nfunction normalizeClaimText(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/[\\uFF10-\\uFF19]/g, (digit) => String.fromCharCode(digit.charCodeAt(0) - 0xfee0))\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF1A/g, \":\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF5C/g, \"|\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\u3000/g, \" \")\n\t\t.trim();\n}\n\n/** Cells never carry markdown code fences: strip the backticks a writer adds. */\nfunction stripClaimTicks(text: string): string {\n\treturn text.replace(/`/g, \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** Split a `| a | b |` row into trimmed cells (leading/trailing pipes dropped). */\nfunction splitClaimRow(line: string): string[] {\n\tconst cells = normalizeClaimText(line).split(\"|\");\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[0] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.shift();\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[cells.length - 1] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.pop();\n\treturn cells.map((cell) => cell.trim());\n}\n\n/** Header of a claims table, `undefined` when the row is not a claims header. */\nfunction matchClaimHeader(cells: string[]): ClaimColumns | undefined {\n\tconst columns: ClaimColumns = {};\n\tlet hasClaimColumn = false;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst name = stripClaimTicks(normalizeClaimText(cells[i] ?? \"\"))\n\t\t\t.toLowerCase()\n\t\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t\t.replace(/:$/, \"\");\n\t\tfor (const [field, aliases] of CLAIM_COLUMN_ALIASES) {\n\t\t\tif (!aliases.includes(name)) continue;\n\t\t\tif (columns[field] === undefined) columns[field] = i;\n\t\t\tif (field === \"id\") hasClaimColumn = true;\n\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn hasClaimColumn ? columns : undefined;\n}\n\n/** `| --- | --- |` separator row (any dash count, optional alignment colons). */\nfunction isClaimSeparatorRow(cells: string[]): boolean {\n\tif (cells.length === 0) return false;\n\treturn cells.every((cell) => cell === \"\" || /^:?-{1,}:?$/.test(cell));\n}\n\n/** Cell of `field` in `cells`, `\"\"` when the column is absent (P-048). */\nfunction claimCell(cells: string[], columns: ClaimColumns, field: ClaimField): string {\n\tconst index = columns[field];\n\tif (index === undefined) return \"\";\n\treturn (cells[index] ?? \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse the card's `<!-- mw-claims: v1 -->` block (design §2.1).\n *\n * Tolerance is the contract, not a nicety (P-048: an over-strict schema caused\n * 30 minutes of consecutive false refusals): the block end falls back to the\n * next H2 or EOF, column order is free, extra columns are ignored, header\n * words take aliases, full-width `：｜`/digits fold to ASCII, and fenced code\n * blocks contribute nothing. An unparsable row is reported as\n * `claim:<row>:unparsable` and skipped — this function never throws.\n */\nexport function parseClaimsBlock(text: string): ClaimBlock {\n\tconst block: ClaimBlock = { present: false, claims: [], errors: [] };\n\tconst byId = new Map<string, Claim>();\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tlet inBlock = false;\n\tlet columns: ClaimColumns | undefined;\n\tconst lines = splitLines(text);\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst line = lines[i] ?? \"\";\n\tconst child = idMatch[2];\n\tconst parent = child === undefined ? \"\" : `C-${number}`;\n\tconst id = `C-${number}${child === undefined ? \"\" : `.${child}`}`;\n\tif (parent !== \"\") {\n\t\t// RQ-3 §5.1 / B-10: a `父.序号` child row is only legal under a `struct`\n\t\t// parent (a struct enumerates the sub-items of one shape).\n\t\tconst parentClaim = byId.get(parent);\n\t\tif (parentClaim === undefined || parentClaim.type !== \"struct\") return undefined;\n\t}\n\tconst declaredType = stripClaimTicks(claimCell(cells, columns, \"type\")).toLowerCase();\n\tconst budgetText = stripClaimTicks(claimCell(cells, columns, \"budget\"));\n\treturn {\n\t\tid,\n\t\t// A struct child restates part of the parent shape, so an empty `类型`\n\t\t// cell inherits `struct` instead of manufacturing a second gap.\n\t\ttype: declaredType === \"\" && parent !== \"\" ? \"struct\" : declaredType,\n\t\tparent,\n\t\tstatement: claimCell(cells, columns, \"statement\"),\n\t\tfalsifier: claimCell(cells, columns, \"falsifier\"),\n\t\tlocator: claimCell(cells, columns, \"locator\"),\n\t\tjudgement: claimCell(cells, columns, \"judgement\"),\n\t\tbudget: /^\\d+$/.test(budgetText) ? Number(budgetText) : Number.NaN,\n\t\trow,\n\t};\n}\n\n// ── claims: 校验 / validation (design §2.1, AC-001) ──────────────────────────\n\n/** `判据` prefix each self-reported type must carry (design §2.1). */\nconst CLAIM_TYPE_PREFIX: Readonly<Record<ClaimType, string>> = {\n\tcmd: \"cmd:\",\n\tgrep: \"grep:\",\n\tstruct: \"shape:\",\n\tmanual: \"manual:\",\n};\n\n/** `Σ预算` cap, manual rows counted twice (AC-001 ⑤). */\nconst CLAIM_BUDGET_SUM_MAX = 40;\n/** `manual` cap numerator of `min(4, ceil(n/3))` (AC-001 ⑤, RQ-3 §6.1). */\nconst CLAIM_MANUAL_CAP = 4;\n/** Normalized-similarity threshold of the tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5). */\nconst CLAIM_TAUTOLOGY_SIMILARITY = 0.9;\n/** Above this size a `定位` must name a line range (AC-001 ④). */\nconst CLAIM_LOCATOR_RANGE_BYTES = 32768;\n/** D-005: a `cmd` locator is the PM's pre-executed evidence file row. */\nconst CLAIM_CMD_LOCATOR_RE = /^evidence\\/claims\\/[^#\\s]+#(C-\\d{2,3}(?:\\.\\d+)?)$/i;\n\n/** Resolution outcome of one `定位` cell. */\ninterface ClaimLocatorTarget {\n\tkind: \"skipped\" | \"unresolved\" | \"resolved\";\n\tsize: number;\n\t/** The locator named an explicit `path:a-b` line segment. */\n\tranged: boolean;\n}\n\n/** A locator names a file when it has a separator or a file extension. */\nfunction looksLikeClaimPath(text: string): boolean {\n\tif (text.includes(\"/\")) return true;\n\treturn /\\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,7}$/.test(text);\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve a `定位` cell against `projectDir` without reading content: only\n * `statSync` runs (design §3.1). A bare symbol, a missing file, a non-file and\n * a path outside `projectDir` are all `unresolved` (never a throw).\n */\nfunction resolveClaimLocator(locator: string, projectDir: string): ClaimLocatorTarget {\n\tconst raw = stripClaimTicks(locator);\n\tif (raw === \"\" || raw === \"-\") return { kind: \"skipped\", size: 0, ranged: false };\n\tconst withoutFragment = raw.replace(/#.*$/, \"\");\n\tconst range = /^(.*?):(\\d+)(?:-(\\d+))?$/.exec(withoutFragment);\n\tconst pathText = (range === null ? withoutFragment : (range[1] ?? \"\")).trim();\n\tconst ranged = range !== null && range[3] !== undefined;\n\tif (pathText === \"\" || !looksLikeClaimPath(pathText)) return { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\tconst absolute = path.resolve(projectDir, pathText);\n\tconst relative = path.relative(projectDir, absolute);\n\tif (relative === \"\" || relative === \"..\" || relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {\n\t\treturn { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\t}\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst stat = fs.statSync(absolute);\n\t\tif (!stat.isFile()) return { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\t\treturn { kind: \"resolved\", size: stat.size, ranged };\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn { kind: \"unresolved\", size: 0, ranged };\n\t}\n}\n\n/**\n * Negation / absence words plus aspect fillers stripped before the tautology\n * similarity test, so that \"X 已修复\" vs \"X 未修复\" compares the same\n * remainder (RQ-3 B-5: the whole point is that a minimal rewrite only differs\n * by these words). Longest-first so `不再` wins over `不` and `已经` over `已`.\n */\nconst CLAIM_NEGATION_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\n\t\"已经\",\n\t\"不再\",\n\t\"不会\",\n\t\"不能\",\n\t\"不得\",\n\t\"没有\",\n\t\"无法\",\n\t\"禁止\",\n\t\"absent\",\n\t\"cannot\",\n\t\"didn't\",\n\t\"doesn't\",\n\t\"failed\",\n\t\"fails\",\n\t\"isn't\",\n\t\"aren't\",\n\t\"missing\",\n\t\"never\",\n\t\"without\",\n\t\"can't\",\n\t\"fail\",\n\t\"not\",\n\t\"已\",\n\t\"不\",\n\t\"未\",\n\t\"无\",\n\t\"非\",\n\t\"否\",\n\t\"缺\",\n].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length);\n\n/** Drop negation words (ASCII ones with word boundaries), then all separators. */\nfunction normalizeClaimSimilarityText(text: string): string {\n\tlet out = text.toLowerCase().replace(/`/g, \" \");\n\tfor (const token of CLAIM_NEGATION_TOKENS) {\n\t\tout = /^[a-z']+$/.test(token) ? out.replace(new RegExp(`\\\\b${token}\\\\b`, \"gi\"), \" \") : out.split(token).join(\" \");\n\t}\n\treturn out.replace(/[^\\p{L}\\p{N}]+/gu, \"\");\n}\n\n/** Levenshtein distance over code points (both inputs are short in practice). */\nfunction claimEditDistance(a: string, b: string): number {\n\tconst left = Array.from(a);\n\tconst right = Array.from(b);\n\tlet previous: number[] = right.map((_, index) => index);\n\tprevious = [0, ...previous];\n\tfor (let i = 1; i <= left.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst current: number[] = [i];\n\t\tfor (let j = 1; j <= right.length; j++) {\n\t\t\tconst cost = left[i - 1] === right[j - 1] ? 0 : 1;\n\t\t\tcurrent[j] = Math.min(\n\t\t\t\t(previous[j] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) + 1,\n\t\t\t\t(current[j - 1] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) + 1,\n\t\t\t\t(previous[j - 1] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) + cost,\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t}\n\t\tprevious = current;\n\t}\n\treturn previous[right.length] ?? 0;\n}\n\n/** Artifact tokens (paths, symbols, commands) that a `判据` can point at. */\nconst CLAIM_ARTIFACT_TOKEN_RE = /[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*/g;\n\n/** Artifact tokens of a `判据`, with the leading type prefix removed. */\nfunction claimJudgementArtifacts(judgement: string): string[] {\n\tconst body = judgement.replace(/^\\s*(?:cmd|grep|shape|manual)\\s*:\\s*/i, \"\");\n\tconst tokens = body.match(CLAIM_ARTIFACT_TOKEN_RE) ?? [];\n\treturn tokens.filter((token) => token.length >= 3);\n}\n\n/**\n * Tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5): `陈述` and `反证条件` become the same text once\n * negation words are dropped (similarity >= 0.90) AND the `判据` names no\n * artifact that `陈述` does not already name. Any new artifact (path, symbol,\n * command) means the claim is still falsifiable, so it is not tautological.\n */\nfunction isTautologicalClaim(claim: Claim): boolean {\n\tif (claim.statement === \"\" || claim.falsifier === \"\" || claim.judgement === \"\") return false;\n\tconst statement = normalizeClaimSimilarityText(claim.statement);\n\tconst falsifier = normalizeClaimSimilarityText(claim.falsifier);\n\tif (statement === \"\" || falsifier === \"\") return false;\n\tconst distance = claimEditDistance(statement, falsifier);\n\tconst similarity = 1 - distance / Math.max(statement.length, falsifier.length);\n\tif (similarity < CLAIM_TAUTOLOGY_SIMILARITY) return false;\n\tconst haystack = claim.statement.toLowerCase();\n\treturn !claimJudgementArtifacts(claim.judgement).some((token) => !haystack.includes(token.toLowerCase()));\n}\n\n/** Options of {@link claimsGaps}. */\nexport interface ClaimsGapOptions {\n\t/** Absolute project root the `定位` paths resolve against. */\n\tprojectDir: string;\n\t/** `true` upgrades the advisory findings to gaps (D-006 grey release). */\n\tenforce: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge a parsed claims block (design §2.1/§3.1, AC-001). Never throws.\n *\n * Structural gaps (`type` / `statement` / `falsifier` / `locator` /\n * `judgement` / `budget`) are gaps in both modes: a claim missing a required\n * cell is not a claim. 2 : 1;\n\t\tif (type === \"manual\") manualCount += 1;\n\t\tif (!known) structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:type`);\n\t\tif (claim.statement === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:statement`);\n\t\tif (claim.falsifier === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:falsifier`);\n\t\tif (claim.locator === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:locator`);\n\t\tif (claim.judgement === \"\") structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:judgement`);\n\t\tif (!Number.isInteger(claim.budget) || claim.budget < 0) structural.push(`claim:${claim.id}:budget`);\n\t\tif (!known) continue;\n\t\tif (claim.judgement !== \"\") {\n\t\t\tconst prefix = CLAIM_TYPE_PREFIX[type as ClaimType];\n\t\t\tif (!claim.judgement.trim().toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix)) advisory.push(`claim:${claim.id}:type-prefix`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (type === \"cmd\" && claim.locator !== \"\") {\n\t\t\tconst cmdLocator = CLAIM_CMD_LOCATOR_RE.exec(stripClaimTicks(claim.locator));\n\t\t\tif (cmdLocator === null || (cmdLocator[1] ?? */\nfunction verdictToken(cell: string): string {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell).replace(/\\s+/g, \"\").toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/** Evidence ref separators (`;`, RQ-3 §5.1) and the `-` empty marker. \"-\");\n}\n\n/** `cmdref` verbs (RQ-3 §5.3 verb whitelist). */\nconst CMD_REF_VERBS: readonly string[] = [\n\t\"node\",\n\t\"npm\",\n\t\"npx\",\n\t\"python\",\n\t\"python3\",\n\t\"pytest\",\n\t\"vitest\",\n\t\"git\",\n\t\"mw\",\n\t\"rg\",\n\t\"grep\",\n\t\"bash\",\n];\n\n/** `cmdref` result half: `rc=<digits>` plus optional `key=value` pairs. */\nconst CMD_RESULT_RE = /^rc=-?\\d+(?:\\s+[\\w.-]+=\\S+)*$/;\n\n/** One parsed evidence ref: a path with a line/line range, or a command. */\ninterface EvidenceRef {\n\tkind: \"path\" | \"cmd\";\n\t/** Repo-relative path (`\"\"` for a command ref). */\n\tpath: string;\n\tfirst: number;\n\tlast: number;\n}\n\n/** A path ref is repo-relative: no absolute path, no `./` prefix, no `..`. */\nfunction isRepoRelativePath(text: string): boolean {\n\tif (text === \"\" || text.startsWith(\"/\") || /^[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]/.test(text) || text.startsWith(\"./\")) return false;\n\treturn !text.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\");\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse one evidence ref (RQ-3 §5.3): `path:line`, `path:a-b`, optionally with\n * a `「excerpt」` suffix, or `verb rest => rc=N [k=v]`. `undefined` means the\n * ref does not match the frozen grammar (a `claim:<id>:evidence` gap).\n */\nfunction parseEvidenceRef(raw: string): EvidenceRef | undefined {\n\tconst ref = stripVerdictTicks(raw);\n\tif (ref === \"\" || ref === \"-\") return undefined;\n\tconst halves = ref.split(\"=>\");\n\tif (halves.length > 2) return undefined;\n\tif (halves.length === 2) {\n\t\tconst left = (halves[0] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\tconst right = (halves[1] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\t// RQ-3 §5.3: no `&&` / `;` (split above) / `>` / backticks inside a cmdref.\n\t\tif (left === \"\" || left.includes(\"&&\") || left.includes(\">\") || left.includes(\"<\") || left.includes(\"`\")) {\n\t\t\treturn undefined;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst verb = /^([A-Za-z0-9]+)\\s+/.exec(left)?.[1]?.toLowerCase() ?? \"\";\n\t\tif (!CMD_REF_VERBS.includes(verb) || !CMD_RESULT_RE.test(right)) return undefined;\n\t\treturn { kind: \"cmd\", path: \"\", first: 0, last: 0 };\n\t}\n\tconst withoutExcerpt = ref.replace(/「[^」]*」\\s*$/, \"\").trim();\n\tconst match = /^(.+?):(\\d+)(?:-(\\d+))?$/.exec(withoutExcerpt);\n\tif (match === null) return undefined;\n\tconst pathText = (match[1] ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (!isRepoRelativePath(pathText)) return undefined;\n\tconst first = Number(match[2] ?? \"\");\n\tconst last = match[3] === undefined ? first : Number(match[3]);\n\tif (!Number.isInteger(first) || !Number.isInteger(last) || first < 1 || last < first) return undefined;\n\treturn { kind: \"path\", path: pathText, first, last };\n}\n\n/** Line count of a text file, trailing newline not counted as a line. */\nfunction lineCount(text: string): number {\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\treturn text.endsWith(\"\\n\") ? lines.length - 1 : lines.length;\n}\n\n/** True when a parsed path ref is not a usable citation: outside the project\n * root, not a file, a line past EOF, or a range wider than 200 lines. */\nfunction evidenceRefInvalid(ref: EvidenceRef, projectDir: string): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind === \"cmd\") return false;\n\tconst absolute = path.resolve(projectDir, ref.path);\n\tconst relative = path.relative(projectDir, absolute);\n\tif (relative === \"\" || relative === \"..\" || relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tlet text: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tif (!fs.statSync(absolute).isFile()) return true;\n\t\ttext = fs.readFileSync(absolute, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tif (ref.last > lineCount(text)) return true;\n\treturn ref.last - ref.first > 200;\n}\n\n/** Self-witness set of RQ-3 §4 (B-1/B-4): a claim citing only these files has\n * cited the report that contains it, not evidence. `progress.md` is allowed as\n * SECONDARY evidence (one real ref alongside it is enough), never as the only\n * one — which is exactly what \"every ref is self-witness\" means here. */\nconst SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES: readonly RegExp[] = [\n\t/^report.*\\.md$/i,\n\t/^output\\.md$/i,\n\t/^progress\\.md$/i,\n\t/^task\\.md$/i,\n];\n\n/** True when a path ref points into the self-witness set (any depth). */\nfunction isSelfEvidenceRef(ref: EvidenceRef): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind !== \"path\") return false;\n\tconst basename = ref.path.split(/[\\\\/]/).pop() ?? \"\";\n\treturn SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES.some((pattern) => pattern.test(basename));\n}\n\n/** `Σ预算` of the card's claims; a card that declares no `预算` at all falls\n * back to the calibrated call cap so a missing field cannot make every fetch a\n * gap (T-01's `claim:<id>:budget` already refuses that card at G1). */\nfunction declaredBudget(claims: Claim[]): number {\n\tlet sum = 0;\n\tlet declared = 0;\n\tfor (const claim of claims) {\n\t\tif (!Number.isFinite(claim.budget) || claim.budget < 0) continue;\n\t\tsum += claim.budget;\n\t\tdeclared += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn declared === 0 ? CLAIM_BUDGET.callCap : sum;\n}\n\n/** `取数` cell as a non-negative integer, `undefined` when it is not one. */\nfunction fetchCount(cell: string): number | undefined {\n\tconst text = stripVerdictTicks(cell);\n\treturn /^\\d+$/.test(text) ? Number(text) : undefined;\n}\n\n/** Ids T-01's own tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5) flags for this claim set. []));\n\treturn required;\n}\n\n/**\n * The `## 交付段契约（本角色）` block for `task_type`, or `\"\"` outside\n * `RECOVERY_CONTRACT_TYPES`. Every required section is rendered as a copyable\n * `- \\`## <段名>\\`` line so the worker can paste the canonical heading the\n * settle judge looks for — never an invented alias. Byte-shape mirror of\n * `dispatch.py::recovery_contract_section` so the two producers inject the same\n * section (idempotent on re-application).\n */\nexport function recoveryContractSection(type: string | undefined): string {\n\tif (type === undefined || !RECOVERY_CONTRACT_TYPES.includes(type)) return \"\";\n\tconst sections = recoverySectionsFor(type);\n\tif (sections.length === 0) return \"\";\n\treturn [\n\t\tRECOVERY_CONTRACT_HEADING,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t\t`本角色（type: ${type}）的恢复契约段：report.md / output.md 必须按下列标题成节（可直接复制；缺任一段即 settle 判缺失）：`,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t\t...sections.map((name) => `- \\`## ${name}\\``),\n\t].join(\"\\n\");\n}\n\n/** Fence opener/closer: 0-3 spaces then at least three backticks or tildes. */\nconst FENCE_RE = /^( {0,3})(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/;\n\n/** An H2 heading line: 0-3 leading spaces, exactly two `#` (never `###`), then\n * horizontal whitespace, then the heading text. */\nconst H2_RE = /^ {0,3}##(?!#)[ \\t]+(.*)$/;\n\n/** A blockquote line: its `#` is quoted data, not a heading. */\nconst BLOCKQUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}>/;\n\n/** Tracks fenced-code-block state across lines. An opening fence records its\n * marker char and length; the matching closing fence must use the same char,\n * the same-or-longer marker and carry nothing but whitespace after it. */\nfunction advanceFence(\n\tline: string,\n\topen: { char: string; len: number } | undefined,\n): { char: string; len: number } | undefined {\n\tconst match = FENCE_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (match === null) return open;\n\tconst marker = match[2] ?? \"\";\n\tconst rest = match[3] ?? \"\";\n\tconst char = marker[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (open === undefined) return { char, len: marker.length };\n\tif (char === open.char && marker.length >= open.len && rest.trim() === \"\") return undefined;\n\treturn open;\n}\n\n/** Normalize one H2 heading: strip the trailing `#` closing sequence, trim,\n * collapse internal whitespace, ASCII-lower. */\nfunction normalizeHeading(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/#+\\s*$/, \"\")\n\t\t.trim()\n\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t.toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/**\n * The normalized H2 headings of `text`, in document order (design §4.1).\n * Fenced code blocks and blockquote lines contribute nothing; `###` is not an\n * H2. Exported for the AC-001 8-case matrix and for tests that lock the\n * normalization.\n */\nexport function h2Headings(text: string): string[] {\n\tconst out: string[] = [];\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tfor (const line of text.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n\t\tfence = advanceFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tif (BLOCKQUOTE_RE.test(line)) continue;\n\t\tconst match = H2_RE.exec(line);\n\t\tif (match === null) continue;\n\t\tout.push(normalizeHeading(match[1] ?? \"\"));\n\t}\n\treturn out;\n}\n\n/** One alias hit on one heading. */\nfunction headingHitsAlias(heading: string, aliases: readonly string[]): boolean {\n\treturn aliases.some((alias) => heading.includes(alias.toLowerCase()));\n}\n\nexport interface RecoveryVerdict {\n\t/** True when every required section is present. */\n\tok: boolean;\n\t/** Required sections with no H2 heading hit, in contract order. Empty iff `ok`. */\n\tmissing: string[];\n\t/** The full required list for the given type (diagnostic/tests). */\n\trequired: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge an agent-authored product text against the recovery contract.\n *\n * `text` is the agent's report (what `report.md` / `output.md` already carries,\n * or the final reply) — never the harness block the writer appends afterwards.\n * `type` is the header `type:` of the dispatch; `undefined` (legacy/manual task\n * book) yields the base four, and the caller is responsible for only asking at\n * all when the dispatch is forward (see `worker/output-writer.ts`).\n *\n * Never throws: any string (including empty) yields a verdict.\n */\nexport function checkRecovery(text: string, type: string | undefined): RecoveryVerdict {\n\tconst required = recoverySectionsFor(type);\n\tconst headings = h2Headings(text);\n\tconst missing = required.filter((name) => {\n\t\tconst aliases = RECOVERY_SECTION_ALIASES[name] ?? [name];\n\t\treturn !headings.some((heading) => headingHitsAlias(heading, aliases));\n\t});\n\treturn { ok: missing.length === 0, missing, required };\n}\n\n// ── T-04a: the `## 断言裁决` verdict table (design §2.2/§3.3, RQ-3 §5) ────────\n//\n// The L3 settle layer judges what the worker CLAIMS to have settled. The\n// table is agent-authored (`## 断言裁决`), seven columns, free column order,\n// extra columns ignored, fenced code blocks excluded, full-width forms folded\n// (RQ-3 §5.6, the P-048 tolerance lesson). Every gap string below is frozen:\n// `claim:<id>:<element>` / `claims:<rule>:<detail>` — the same shape T-01's\n// `claimsGaps` already froze, so the refusal text and the settle readback can\n// concatenate either list without a second vocabulary.\n\n/** H2 aliases of the verdict table. `## 断言裁决（claims）` still hits because\n * the match is `includes`, exactly like `RECOVERY_SECTION_ALIASES`. */\nconst VERDICT_TABLE_ALIASES: readonly string[] = [\"断言裁决\", \"claim verdict\", \"claims verdict\", \"verdict table\"];\n\n/** The seven judged columns (RQ-3 §5.1). */\ntype VerdictField = \"id\" | \"type\" | \"verdict\" | \"finding\" | \"evidence\" | \"fetches\" | \"reason\";\n\n/** Header aliases per column, both scripts (RQ-3 §5.6). */\nconst VERDICT_COLUMN_ALIASES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [VerdictField, readonly string[]]> = [\n\t[\"id\", [\"claim\", \"断言\", \"claim id\"]],\n\t[\"type\", [\"类型\", \"type\", \"类别\"]],\n\t[\"verdict\", [\"裁决\", \"verdict\"]],\n\t[\"finding\", [\"判定\", \"finding\", \"判断\"]],\n\t[\"evidence\", [\"证据\", \"evidence\"]],\n\t[\"fetches\", [\"取数\", \"fetches\", \"reads\"]],\n\t[\"reason\", [\"原因\", \"reason\"]],\n];\n\n/** One parsed `## 断言裁决` row, all cells trimmed (never normalized away: the\n * raw cell text is what the diagnostics quote). */\nexport interface VerdictRow {\n\t/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` id, upper-cased. */\n\tid: string;\n\t/** `类型` cell, lower-cased, `\"\"` when the column is absent. */\n\ttype: string;\n\tverdict: string;\n\tfinding: string;\n\tevidence: string;\n\tfetches: string;\n\treason: string;\n\t/** 1-based line of the row in the parsed text (diagnostics only). */\n\trow: number;\n}\n\n/** Result of {@link parseVerdictTable}. Never throws (P-048). */\nexport interface VerdictTable {\n\t/** The `## 断言裁决` H2 was seen outside a fence. */\n\tpresent: boolean;\n\trows: VerdictRow[];\n\t/** `claim:<row>:unparsable` findings, row = 1-based source line. */\n\terrors: string[];\n}\n\n/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` (the same id shape `parseClaimsBlock` accepts). */\nconst VERDICT_ID_RE = /^C-(\\d{2,3})(?:\\.(\\d+))?$/i;\n\n/** Header index per judged column, filled in header order. */\ntype VerdictColumns = Partial<Record<VerdictField, number>>;\n\n/** Fold the full-width forms the card corpus mixes in (RQ-3 §5.6): `：` -> `:`,\n * `｜` -> `|`, full-width digits -> ASCII digits, ideographic space -> space.\n * Mirror of the private helper in `shared/dispatch-card.ts` (the claims block\n * parser); the exported constants are imported, never copied. */\nfunction normalizeVerdictText(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/[\\uFF10-\\uFF19]/g, (digit) => String.fromCharCode(digit.charCodeAt(0) - 0xfee0))\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF1A/g, \":\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF5C/g, \"|\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\u3000/g, \" \")\n\t\t.trim();\n}\n\n/** Cells never carry markdown code fences: strip the backticks a writer adds. */\nfunction stripVerdictTicks(text: string): string {\n\treturn text.replace(/`/g, \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** Split a `| a | b |` row into trimmed cells (leading/trailing pipes dropped). */\nfunction splitVerdictRow(line: string): string[] {\n\tconst cells = normalizeVerdictText(line).split(\"|\");\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[0] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.shift();\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[cells.length - 1] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.pop();\n\treturn cells.map((cell) => cell.trim());\n}\n\n/** Header of a verdict table, `undefined` when the row is not a header. */\nfunction matchVerdictHeader(cells: string[]): VerdictColumns | undefined {\n\tconst columns: VerdictColumns = {};\n\tlet hasClaimColumn = false;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst name = stripVerdictTicks(normalizeVerdictText(cells[i] ?? \"\"))\n\t\t\t.toLowerCase()\n\t\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t\t.replace(/:$/, \"\");\n\t\tfor (const [field, aliases] of VERDICT_COLUMN_ALIASES) {\n\t\t\tif (!aliases.includes(name)) continue;\n\t\t\tif (columns[field] === undefined) columns[field] = i;\n\t\t\tif (field === \"id\") hasClaimColumn = true;\n\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn hasClaimColumn ? columns : undefined;\n}\n\n/** `| --- | --- |` separator row (any dash count, optional alignment colons). */\nfunction isVerdictSeparatorRow(cells: string[]): boolean {\n\tif (cells.length === 0) return false;\n\treturn cells.every((cell) => cell === \"\" || /^:?-{1,}:?$/.test(cell));\n}\n\n/** Cell of `field` in `cells`, `\"\"` when the column is absent (tolerance). */\nfunction verdictCell(cells: string[], columns: VerdictColumns, field: VerdictField): string {\n\tconst index = columns[field];\n\tif (index === undefined) return \"\";\n\treturn (cells[index] ?? \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** One table row -> {@link VerdictRow}, `undefined` when the id is unparsable. */\nfunction verdictRowFrom(cells: string[], columns: VerdictColumns, row: number): VerdictRow | undefined {\n\tconst idMatch = VERDICT_ID_RE.exec(stripVerdictTicks(verdictCell(cells, columns, \"id\")));\n\tif (idMatch === null) return undefined;\n\tconst number = idMatch[1] ?? \"\";\n\tconst child = idMatch[2];\n\treturn {\n\t\tid: `C-${number}${child === undefined ? \"\" : `.${child}`}`,\n\t\ttype: stripVerdictTicks(verdictCell(cells, columns, \"type\")).toLowerCase(),\n\t\tverdict: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"verdict\"),\n\t\tfinding: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"finding\"),\n\t\tevidence: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"evidence\"),\n\t\tfetches: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"fetches\"),\n\t\treason: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"reason\"),\n\t\trow,\n\t};\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse the agent-authored `## 断言裁决` table (RQ-3 §5.1/§5.6).\n *\n * Tolerance is the contract (P-048): the heading may carry a suffix, column\n * order is free, extra columns are ignored, header words take both scripts,\n * full-width `：｜`/digits fold to ASCII, and fenced code blocks contribute\n * nothing (the same fence state machine `h2Headings` uses). A row whose\n * `claim` cell is not a claim id is reported as `claim:<row>:unparsable` and\n * skipped; this function never throws.\n */\nexport function parseVerdictTable(text: string): VerdictTable {\n\tconst table: VerdictTable = { present: false, rows: [], errors: [] };\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tlet inSection = false;\n\tlet columns: VerdictColumns | undefined;\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst line = lines[i] ?? \"\";\n\t\tfence = advanceFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tconst heading = H2_RE.exec(line);\n\t\tif (heading !== null) {\n\t\t\tconst normalized = normalizeHeading(heading[1] ?? \"\");\n\t\t\tif (inSection) {\n\t\t\t\tinSection = false;\n\t\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif (!table.present && VERDICT_TABLE_ALIASES.some((alias) => normalized.includes(alias))) {\n\t\t\t\t// RQ-3 §5.6: `## 断言裁决（claims）` hits, the body starts below it.\n\t\t\t\ttable.present = true;\n\t\t\t\tinSection = true;\n\t\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (!inSection) continue;\n\t\tif (BLOCKQUOTE_RE.test(line)) continue;\n\t\tif (!normalizeVerdictText(line).startsWith(\"|\")) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst cells = splitVerdictRow(line);\n\t\tif (columns === undefined) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = matchVerdictHeader(cells);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (isVerdictSeparatorRow(cells)) continue;\n\t\tconst row = verdictRowFrom(cells, columns, i + 1);\n\t\tif (row === undefined) {\n\t\t\ttable.errors.push(`claim:${i + 1}:unparsable`);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\ttable.rows.push(row);\n\t}\n\treturn table;\n}\n\n/** `裁决` closed set (RQ-3 §5.2; no `done`/`PASS`/`ok`/`verified`/`N/A`). */\nconst VERDICT_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\"closed\", \"partial\", \"unverified\"];\n\n/** `判定` closed set (RQ-3 §5.1) plus the `partial` render token `部分成立` —\n * §5.1's own mapping (`partial` -> 部分成立) has no other representable form,\n * so excluding it here would make `partial` unusable. */\nconst FINDING_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\"成立\", \"不成立\", \"无法判定\", \"部分成立\"];\n\n/** Allowed `判定` per `裁决` (RQ-3 §5.1: `closed` settles either way). */\nconst VERDICT_FINDINGS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {\n\tclosed: [\"成立\", \"不成立\"],\n\tpartial: [\"部分成立\"],\n\tunverified: [\"无法判定\"],\n};\n\n/** Fold a closed-set cell to its token form (ticks, whitespace, ASCII case). */\nfunction verdictToken(cell: string): string {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell).replace(/\\s+/g, \"\").toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/** Evidence ref separators (`;` and the full-width `；` — a real review emitted\n * `a.py:1-4；b.ts:7` on the first live e2e and the ASCII-only split read the whole\n * cell as one nonexistent path, costing two false gaps, P-048) and the `-` empty\n * marker. */\nfunction splitEvidenceRefs(cell: string): string[] {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell)\n\t\t.split(/[;；]/)\n\t\t.map((ref) => ref.trim())\n\t\t.filter((ref) => ref !== \"\" && ref !== \"-\");\n}\n\n/** `cmdref` verbs (RQ-3 §5.3 verb whitelist). */\nconst CMD_REF_VERBS: readonly string[] = [\n\t\"node\",\n\t\"npm\",\n\t\"npx\",\n\t\"python\",\n\t\"python3\",\n\t\"pytest\",\n\t\"vitest\",\n\t\"git\",\n\t\"mw\",\n\t\"rg\",\n\t\"grep\",\n\t\"bash\",\n];\n\n/** `cmdref` result half: `rc=<digits>` plus optional `key=value` pairs. */\nconst CMD_RESULT_RE = /^rc=-?\\d+(?:\\s+[\\w.-]+=\\S+)*$/;\n\n/** One parsed evidence ref: a path with a line/line range, or a command. */\ninterface EvidenceRef {\n\tkind: \"path\" | \"cmd\";\n\t/** Repo-relative path (`\"\"` for a command ref). */\n\tpath: string;\n\tfirst: number;\n\tlast: number;\n}\n\n/** A path ref is repo-relative: no absolute path, no `./` prefix, no `..`. */\nfunction isRepoRelativePath(text: string): boolean {\n\tif (text === \"\" || text.startsWith(\"/\") || /^[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]/.test(text) || text.startsWith(\"./\")) return false;\n\treturn !text.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\");\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse one evidence ref (RQ-3 §5.3): `path:line`, `path:a-b`, optionally with\n * a `「excerpt」` suffix, or `verb rest => rc=N [k=v]`. `undefined` means the\n * ref does not match the frozen grammar (a `claim:<id>:evidence` gap).\n */\nfunction parseEvidenceRef(raw: string): EvidenceRef | undefined {\n\tconst ref = stripVerdictTicks(raw);\n\tif (ref === \"\" || ref === \"-\") return undefined;\n\tconst halves = ref.split(\"=>\");\n\tif (halves.length > 2) return undefined;\n\tif (halves.length === 2) {\n\t\tconst left = (halves[0] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\tconst right = (halves[1] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\t// RQ-3 §5.3: no `&&` / `;` (split above) / `>` / backticks inside a cmdref.\n\t\tif (left === \"\" || left.includes(\"&&\") || left.includes(\">\") || left.includes(\"<\") || left.includes(\"`\")) {\n\t\t\treturn undefined;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst verb = /^([A-Za-z0-9]+)\\s+/.exec(left)?.[1]?.toLowerCase() ?? \"\";\n\t\tif (!CMD_REF_VERBS.includes(verb) || !CMD_RESULT_RE.test(right)) return undefined;\n\t\treturn { kind: \"cmd\", path: \"\", first: 0, last: 0 };\n\t}\n\tconst withoutExcerpt = ref.replace(/「[^」]*」\\s*$/, \"\").trim();\n\tconst match = /^(.+?):(\\d+)(?:-(\\d+))?$/.exec(withoutExcerpt);\n\tif (match === null) return undefined;\n\tconst pathText = (match[1] ?? \"\").trim();\n\tif (!isRepoRelativePath(pathText)) return undefined;\n\tconst first = Number(match[2] ?? \"\");\n\tconst last = match[3] === undefined ? first : Number(match[3]);\n\tif (!Number.isInteger(first) || !Number.isInteger(last) || first < 1 || last < first) return undefined;\n\treturn { kind: \"path\", path: pathText, first, last };\n}\n\n/** Line count of a text file, trailing newline not counted as a line. */\nfunction lineCount(text: string): number {\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\treturn text.endsWith(\"\\n\") ? lines.length - 1 : lines.length;\n}\n\n/** True when a parsed path ref is not a usable citation: outside the project\n * root, not a file, a line past EOF, or a range wider than 200 lines. */\nfunction evidenceRefInvalid(ref: EvidenceRef, projectDir: string): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind === \"cmd\") return false;\n\tconst absolute = path.resolve(projectDir, ref.path);\n\tconst relative = path.relative(projectDir, absolute);\n\tif (relative === \"\" || relative === \"..\" || relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tlet text: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tif (!fs.statSync(absolute).isFile()) return true;\n\t\ttext = fs.readFileSync(absolute, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tif (ref.last > lineCount(text)) return true;\n\treturn ref.last - ref.first > 200;\n}\n\n/** Self-witness set of RQ-3 §4 (B-1/B-4): a claim citing only these files has\n * cited the report that contains it, not evidence. `progress.md` is allowed as\n * SECONDARY evidence (one real ref alongside it is enough), never as the only\n * one — which is exactly what \"every ref is self-witness\" means here. */\nconst SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES: readonly RegExp[] = [\n\t/^report.*\\.md$/i,\n\t/^output\\.md$/i,\n\t/^progress\\.md$/i,\n\t/^task\\.md$/i,\n];\n\n/** True when a path ref points into the self-witness set (any depth). */\nfunction isSelfEvidenceRef(ref: EvidenceRef): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind !== \"path\") return false;\n\tconst basename = ref.path.split(/[\\\\/]/).pop() ?? \"\";\n\treturn SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES.some((pattern) => pattern.test(basename));\n}\n\n/** `Σ预算` of the card's claims; a card that declares no `预算` at all falls\n * back to the calibrated call cap so a missing field cannot make every fetch a\n * gap (T-01's `claim:<id>:budget` already refuses that card at G1). */\nfunction declaredBudget(claims: Claim[]): number {\n\tlet sum = 0;\n\tlet declared = 0;\n\tfor (const claim of claims) {\n\t\tif (!Number.isFinite(claim.budget) || claim.budget < 0) continue;\n\t\tsum += claim.budget;\n\t\tdeclared += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn declared === 0 ? CLAIM_BUDGET.callCap : sum;\n}\n\n/** `取数` cell as a non-negative integer, `undefined` when it is not one. */\nfunction fetchCount(cell: string): number | undefined {\n\tconst text = stripVerdictTicks(cell);\n\treturn /^\\d+$/.test(text) ? Number(text) : undefined;\n}\n\n/** Ids T-01's own tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5) flags for this claim set. Reuses\n * `claimsGaps` so the `陈述`/`反证条件` similarity + new-artifact rule has ONE\n * implementation (the card forbids rewriting it and `shared/**` is out of the\n * write face, so the exported validator is the only legal handle). */\nfunction tautologyIds(claims: Claim[], projectDir: string): Set<string> {\n\tconst ids = new Set<string>();\n\tif (claims.length === 0) return ids;\n\tconst gaps = claimsGaps({ present: true, claims, errors: [] }, { projectDir, enforce: true });\n\tfor (const gap of gaps) {\n\t\tconst match = /^claim:(C-\\d{2,3}(?:\\.\\d+)?):tautology$/.exec(gap);\n\t\tif (match !== null && match[1] !== undefined) ids.add(match[1]);\n\t}\n\treturn ids;\n}\n\n/** Options of {@link claimCoverage}. `projectDir` is the root the evidence path\n * refs resolve against (the launcher's cwd in production, a fixture in tests). */\nexport interface ClaimCoverageOptions {\n\tprojectDir?: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge the `## 断言裁决` table against the card's claim set (RQ-3 §5, B-1/B-4/\n * B-10). Every returned string is one frozen criterion; the string IS the\n * diagnostic, so no second vocabulary is introduced.\n *\n * Criteria (in emission order):\n *   `claims:missing-table`            no `## 断言裁决` H2 at all\n *   `claim:<id>:missing-row`          a card claim the table never adjudicates\n *   `claims:extra-row:<id>`           a table row the card never declared\n *   `claim:<id>:verdict`              `裁决` outside closed|partial|unverified\n *   `claim:<id>:finding`              `判定` outside 成立|不成立|无法判定\n *   `claim:<id>:verdict-finding`      the two columns disagree (§5.1 mapping)\n *   `claim:<id>:evidence`             no evidence for closed/partial, or a ref\n *                                     that is unparsable / missing on disk /\n *                                     past EOF / wider than 200 lines\n *   `claim:<id>:reason`               `unverified` without a 7-word reason\n *   `claim:<id>:self-evidence`        every ref is `report*`/output/progress/task\n *   `claim:<id>:struct-held`          a `struct` row counted as `closed` (B-10)\n *   `claim:<id>:budget`               `取数` not a count, or > min(Σ预算, 30)\n *   `claim:<id>:tautology`            T-01's B-5 tautology judge fired\n *\n * Never throws. A claim-free card returns `[]` (nothing to adjudicate), and a\n * table-only run without claims is likewise not judged.\n */\nexport function claimCoverage(claims: Claim[], table: VerdictTable, opts: ClaimCoverageOptions = {}): string[] {\n\tconst gaps: string[] = [];\n\tif (claims.length === 0) return gaps;\n\tif (!table.present) return [\"claims:missing-table\"];\n\tconst projectDir = opts.projectDir ?? process.cwd();\n\tconst rows = new Map<string, VerdictRow>();\n\tfor (const row of table.rows) if (!rows.has(row.id)) rows.set(row.id, row);\n\tconst budgetCap = Math.min(declaredBudget(claims), CLAIM_BUDGET.callCap);\n\tconst tautological = tautologyIds(claims, projectDir);\n\tfor (const claim of claims) {\n\t\tconst row = rows.get(claim.id);\n\t\tif (row === undefined) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:missing-row`);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst verdict = verdictToken(row.verdict);\n\t\tconst finding = verdictToken(row.finding);\n\t\tif (!VERDICT_TOKENS.includes(verdict)) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:verdict`);\n\t\tif (!FINDING_TOKENS.includes(finding)) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:finding`);\n\t\tif (\n\t\t\tVERDICT_FINDINGS[verdict] !== undefined &&\n\t\t\tFINDING_TOKENS.includes(finding) &&\n\t\t\t!(VERDICT_FINDINGS[verdict] ?? []).includes(finding)\n\t\t) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:verdict-finding`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst refs = splitEvidenceRefs(row.evidence);\n\t\tconst parsed: Array<EvidenceRef | undefined> = refs.map((ref) => parseEvidenceRef(ref));\n\t\tconst needsEvidence = verdict === \"closed\" || verdict === \"partial\";\n\t\tif (needsEvidence && refs.length === 0) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:evidence`);\n\t\telse if (parsed.some((ref) => ref === undefined || evidenceRefInvalid(ref, projectDir))) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:evidence`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (verdict === \"unverified\" && !(UNVERIFIED_REASONS as readonly string[]).includes(verdictToken(row.reason))) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:reason`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst parsedAll: EvidenceRef[] = parsed.filter((ref): ref is EvidenceRef => ref !== undefined);\n\t\tif (parsedAll.length > 0 && parsedAll.length === refs.length && parsedAll.every(isSelfEvidenceRef)) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:self-evidence`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst declaredType = row.type === \"\" ? claim.type.toLowerCase() : row.type;\n\t\tif (declaredType === \"struct\" && verdict === \"closed\") gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:struct-held`);\n\t\tconst fetches = fetchCount(row.fetches);\n\t\tif (fetches === undefined || fetches > budgetCap) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:budget`);\n\t\tif (tautological.has(claim.id)) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:tautology`);\n\t}\n\tconst declaredIds = new Set(claims.map((claim) => claim.id));\n\tfor (const row of table.rows) {\n\t\tif (!declaredIds.has(row.id)) gaps.push(`claims:extra-row:${row.id}`);\n\t}\n\treturn gaps;\n}\n"]}
