Every other section — `结论`, `证据`,\n * `残留与未验证`, `改动清单`, `未覆盖面声明`, and `## Questions` — is a\n * substantive judgement and is NEVER auto-generated; a whitelist (not a\n * blacklist) so a future section cannot be auto-filled by accident.\n */\nexport const MECHANICAL_SECTIONS: readonly string[] = [\"上下文来源\"];\n\n/** True when `name` is on the mechanical-backfill whitelist (R2). */\nexport function isMechanicalSection(name: string): boolean {\n\treturn MECHANICAL_SECTIONS.includes(name);\n}\n\n/** Which sections `type` must carry: the base four plus its role extra. */\nexport function recoverySectionsFor(type: string | undefined): string[] {\n\tconst required: string[] = [...RECOVERY_SECTIONS];\n\tif (type !== undefined) required.push(...(RECOVERY_TYPE_SECTIONS[type] ?? []));\n\treturn required;\n}\n\n/**\n * The `## 交付段契约（本角色）` block for `task_type`, or `\"\"` outside\n * `RECOVERY_CONTRACT_TYPES`. Every required section is rendered as a copyable\n * `- \\`## <段名>\\`` line so the worker can paste the canonical heading the\n * settle judge looks for — never an invented alias. Byte-shape mirror of\n * `dispatch.py::recovery_contract_section` so the two producers inject the same\n * section (idempotent on re-application).\n */\nexport function recoveryContractSection(type: string | undefined): string {\n\tif (type === undefined || !RECOVERY_CONTRACT_TYPES.includes(type)) return \"\";\n\tconst sections = recoverySectionsFor(type);\n\tif (sections.length === 0) return \"\";\n\treturn [\n\t\tRECOVERY_CONTRACT_HEADING,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t\t`本角色（type: ${type}）的恢复契约段：report.md / output.md 必须按下列标题成节（可直接复制；缺任一段即 settle 判缺失）：`,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t\t...sections.map((name) => `- \\`## ${name}\\``),\n\t].join(\"\\n\");\n}\n\n/** Fence opener/closer: 0-3 spaces then at least three backticks or tildes. */\nconst FENCE_RE = /^( {0,3})(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/;\n\n/** An H2 heading line: 0-3 leading spaces, exactly two `#` (never `###`), then\n * horizontal whitespace, then the heading text. */\nconst H2_RE = /^ {0,3}##(?!#)[ \\t]+(.*)$/;\n\n/** A blockquote line: its `#` is quoted data, not a heading. */\nconst BLOCKQUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}>/;\n\n/** Tracks fenced-code-block state across lines. An opening fence records its\n * marker char and length; the matching closing fence must use the same char,\n * the same-or-longer marker and carry nothing but whitespace after it. */\nfunction advanceFence(\n\tline: string,\n\topen: { char: string; len: number } | undefined,\n): { char: string; len: number } | undefined {\n\tconst match = FENCE_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (match === null) return open;\n\tconst marker = match[2] ?? \"\";\n\tconst rest = match[3] ?? \"\";\n\tconst char = marker[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (open === undefined) return { char, len: marker.length };\n\tif (char === open.char && marker.length >= open.len && rest.trim() === \"\") return undefined;\n\treturn open;\n}\n\n/** Normalize one H2 heading: strip the trailing `#` closing sequence, trim,\n * collapse internal whitespace, ASCII-lower. */\nfunction normalizeHeading(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/#+\\s*$/, \"\")\n\t\t.trim()\n\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t.toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/**\n * The normalized H2 headings of `text`, in document order (design §4.1).\n * Fenced code blocks and blockquote lines contribute nothing; `###` is not an\n * H2. Exported for the AC-001 8-case matrix and for tests that lock the\n * normalization.\n */\nexport function h2Headings(text: string): string[] {\n\tconst out: string[] = [];\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tfor (const line of text.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n\t\tfence = advanceFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tif (BLOCKQUOTE_RE.test(line)) continue;\n\t\tconst match = H2_RE.exec(line);\n\t\tif (match === null) continue;\n\t\tout.push(normalizeHeading(match[1] ?? \"\"));\n\t}\n\treturn out;\n}\n\n/** One alias hit on one heading. */\nfunction headingHitsAlias(heading: string, aliases: readonly string[]): boolean {\n\treturn aliases.some((alias) => heading.includes(alias.toLowerCase()));\n}\n\nexport interface RecoveryVerdict {\n\t/** True when every required section is present. */\n\tok: boolean;\n\t/** Required sections with no H2 heading hit, in contract order. Empty iff `ok`. */\n\tmissing: string[];\n\t/** The full required list for the given type (diagnostic/tests). */\n\trequired: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge an agent-authored product text against the recovery contract.\n *\n * `text` is the agent's report (what `report.md` / `output.md` already carries,\n * or the final reply) — never the harness block the writer appends afterwards.\n * `type` is the header `type:` of the dispatch; `undefined` (legacy/manual task\n * book) yields the base four, and the caller is responsible for only asking at\n * all when the dispatch is forward (see `worker/output-writer.ts`).\n *\n * Never throws: any string (including empty) yields a verdict.\n */\nexport function checkRecovery(text: string, type: string | undefined): RecoveryVerdict {\n\tconst required = recoverySectionsFor(type);\n\tconst headings = h2Headings(text);\n\tconst missing = required.filter((name) => {\n\t\tconst aliases = RECOVERY_SECTION_ALIASES[name] ?? [name];\n\t\treturn !headings.some((heading) => headingHitsAlias(heading, aliases));\n\t});\n\treturn { ok: missing.length === 0, missing, required };\n}\n\n// ── T-04a: the `## 断言裁决` verdict table (design §2.2/§3.3, RQ-3 §5) ────────\n//\n// The L3 settle layer judges what the worker CLAIMS to have settled. The\n// table is agent-authored (`## 断言裁决`), seven columns, free column order,\n// extra columns ignored, fenced code blocks excluded, full-width forms folded\n// (RQ-3 §5.6, the P-048 tolerance lesson). Every gap string below is frozen:\n// `claim:<id>:<element>` / `claims:<rule>:<detail>` — the same shape T-01's\n// `claimsGaps` already froze, so the refusal text and the settle readback can\n// concatenate either list without a second vocabulary.\n\n/** H2 aliases of the verdict table. `## 断言裁决（claims）` still hits because\n * the match is `includes`, exactly like `RECOVERY_SECTION_ALIASES`. */\nconst VERDICT_TABLE_ALIASES: readonly string[] = [\"断言裁决\", \"claim verdict\", \"claims verdict\", \"verdict table\"];\n\n/** The seven judged columns (RQ-3 §5.1). */\ntype VerdictField = \"id\" | \"type\" | \"verdict\" | \"finding\" | \"evidence\" | \"fetches\" | \"reason\";\n\n/** Header aliases per column, both scripts (RQ-3 §5.6). */\nconst VERDICT_COLUMN_ALIASES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [VerdictField, readonly string[]]> = [\n\t[\"id\", [\"claim\", \"断言\", \"claim id\"]],\n\t[\"type\", [\"类型\", \"type\", \"类别\"]],\n\t[\"verdict\", [\"裁决\", \"verdict\"]],\n\t[\"finding\", [\"判定\", \"finding\", \"判断\"]],\n\t[\"evidence\", [\"证据\", \"evidence\"]],\n\t[\"fetches\", [\"取数\", \"fetches\", \"reads\"]],\n\t[\"reason\", [\"原因\", \"reason\"]],\n];\n\n/** One parsed `## 断言裁决` row, all cells trimmed (never normalized away: the\n * raw cell text is what the diagnostics quote). */\nexport interface VerdictRow {\n\t/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` id, upper-cased. */\n\tid: string;\n\t/** `类型` cell, lower-cased, `\"\"` when the column is absent. */\n\ttype: string;\n\tverdict: string;\n\tfinding: string;\n\tevidence: string;\n\tfetches: string;\n\treason: string;\n\t/** 1-based line of the row in the parsed text (diagnostics only). */\n\trow: number;\n}\n\n/** Result of {@link parseVerdictTable}. Never throws (P-048). */\nexport interface VerdictTable {\n\t/** The `## 断言裁决` H2 was seen outside a fence. */\n\tpresent: boolean;\n\trows: VerdictRow[];\n\t/** `claim:<row>:unparsable` findings, row = 1-based source line. */\n\terrors: string[];\n}\n\n/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` (the same id shape `parseClaimsBlock` accepts). */\nconst VERDICT_ID_RE = /^C-(\\d{2,3})(?:\\.(\\d+))?$/i;\n\n/** Header index per judged column, filled in header order. */\ntype VerdictColumns = Partial<Record<VerdictField, number>>;\n\n/** Fold the full-width forms the card corpus mixes in (RQ-3 §5.6): `：` -> `:`,\n * `｜` -> `|`, full-width digits -> ASCII digits, ideographic space -> space.\n * Mirror of the private helper in `shared/dispatch-card.ts` (the claims block\n * parser); the exported constants are imported, never copied. */\nfunction normalizeVerdictText(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/[\\uFF10-\\uFF19]/g, (digit) => String.fromCharCode(digit.charCodeAt(0) - 0xfee0))\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF1A/g, \":\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF5C/g, \"|\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\u3000/g, \" \")\n\t\t.trim();\n}\n\n/** Cells never carry markdown code fences: strip the backticks a writer adds. */\nfunction stripVerdictTicks(text: string): string {\n\treturn text.replace(/`/g, \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** Split a `| a | b |` row into trimmed cells (leading/trailing pipes dropped). */\nfunction splitVerdictRow(line: string): string[] {\n\tconst cells = normalizeVerdictText(line).split(\"|\");\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[0] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.shift();\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[cells.length - 1] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.pop();\n\treturn cells.map((cell) => cell.trim());\n}\n\n/** Header of a verdict table, `undefined` when the row is not a header. */\nfunction matchVerdictHeader(cells: string[]): VerdictColumns | undefined {\n\tconst columns: VerdictColumns = {};\n\tlet hasClaimColumn = false;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst name = stripVerdictTicks(normalizeVerdictText(cells[i] ?? \"\"))\n\t\t\t.toLowerCase()\n\t\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t\t.replace(/:$/, \"\");\n\t\tfor (const [field, aliases] of VERDICT_COLUMN_ALIASES) {\n\t\t\tif (!aliases.includes(name)) continue;\n\t\t\tif (columns[field] === undefined) columns[field] = i;\n\t\t\tif (field === \"id\") hasClaimColumn = true;\n\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn hasClaimColumn ? columns : undefined;\n}\n\n/** `| --- | --- |` separator row (any dash count, optional alignment colons). */\nfunction isVerdictSeparatorRow(cells: string[]): boolean {\n\tif (cells.length === 0) return false;\n\treturn cells.every((cell) => cell === \"\" || /^:?-{1,}:?$/.test(cell));\n}\n\n/** Cell of `field` in `cells`, `\"\"` when the column is absent (tolerance). */\nfunction verdictCell(cells: string[], columns: VerdictColumns, field: VerdictField): string {\n\tconst index = columns[field];\n\tif (index === undefined) return \"\";\n\treturn (cells[index] ?? \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** One table row -> {@link VerdictRow}, `undefined` when the id is unparsable. */\nfunction verdictRowFrom(cells: string[], columns: VerdictColumns, row: number): VerdictRow | undefined {\n\tconst idMatch = VERDICT_ID_RE.exec(stripVerdictTicks(verdictCell(cells, columns, \"id\")));\n\tif (idMatch === null) return undefined;\n\tconst number = idMatch[1] ?? \"\";\n\tconst child = idMatch[2];\n\treturn {\n\t\tid: `C-${number}${child === undefined ? \"\" : `.${child}`}`,\n\t\ttype: stripVerdictTicks(verdictCell(cells, columns, \"type\")).toLowerCase(),\n\t\tverdict: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"verdict\"),\n\t\tfinding: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"finding\"),\n\t\tevidence: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"evidence\"),\n\t\tfetches: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"fetches\"),\n\t\treason: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"reason\"),\n\t\trow,\n\t};\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse the agent-authored `## 断言裁决` table (RQ-3 §5.1/§5.6).\n *\n * Tolerance is the contract (P-048): the heading may carry a suffix, column\n * order is free, extra columns are ignored, header words take both scripts,\n * full-width `：｜`/digits fold to ASCII, and fenced code blocks contribute\n * nothing (the same fence state machine `h2Headings` uses). A row whose\n * `claim` cell is not a claim id is reported as `claim:<row>:unparsable` and\n * skipped; this function never throws.\n */\nexport function parseVerdictTable(text: string): VerdictTable {\n\tconst table: VerdictTable = { present: false, rows: [], errors: [] };\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tlet inSection = false;\n\tlet columns: VerdictColumns | undefined;\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst line = lines[i] ?? \"\";\n\t\tfence = advanceFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tconst heading = H2_RE.exec(line);\n\t\tif (heading !== null) {\n\t\t\tconst normalized = normalizeHeading(heading[1] ?? \"\");\n\t\t\tif (inSection) {\n\t\t\t\tinSection = false;\n\t\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif (!table.present && VERDICT_TABLE_ALIASES.some((alias) => normalized.includes(alias))) {\n\t\t\t\t// RQ-3 §5.6: `## 断言裁决（claims）` hits, the body starts below it.\n\t\t\t\ttable.present = true;\n\t\t\t\tinSection = true;\n\t\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (!inSection) continue;\n\t\tif (BLOCKQUOTE_RE.test(line)) continue;\n\t\tif (!normalizeVerdictText(line).startsWith(\"|\")) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst cells = splitVerdictRow(line);\n\t\tif (columns === undefined) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = matchVerdictHeader(cells);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (isVerdictSeparatorRow(cells)) continue;\n\t\tconst row = verdictRowFrom(cells, columns, i + 1);\n\t\tif (row === undefined) {\n\t\t\ttable.errors.push(`claim:${i + 1}:unparsable`);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\ttable.rows.push(row);\n\t}\n\treturn table;\n}\n\n/** `裁决` closed set (RQ-3 §5.2; no `done`/`PASS`/`ok`/`verified`/`N/A`). */\nconst VERDICT_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\"closed\", \"partial\", \"unverified\"];\n\n/** `判定` closed set (RQ-3 §5.1) plus the `partial` render token `部分成立` —\n * §5.1's own mapping (`partial` -> 部分成立) has no other representable form,\n * so excluding it here would make `partial` unusable. */\nconst FINDING_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\"成立\", \"不成立\", \"无法判定\", \"部分成立\"];\n\n/** Allowed `判定` per `裁决` (RQ-3 §5.1: `closed` settles either way). */\nconst VERDICT_FINDINGS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {\n\tclosed: [\"成立\", \"不成立\"],\n\tpartial: [\"部分成立\"],\n\tunverified: [\"无法判定\"],\n};\n\n/** Fold a closed-set cell to its token form (ticks, whitespace, ASCII case). */\nfunction verdictToken(cell: string): string {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell).replace(/\\s+/g, \"\").toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/** Evidence ref separators (`;`, RQ-3 §5.1) and the `-` empty marker. */\nfunction splitEvidenceRefs(cell: string): string[] {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell)\n\t\t.split(\";\")\n\t\t.map((ref) => ref.trim())\n\t\t.filter((ref) => ref !== \"\" && ref !== \"-\");\n}\n\n/** `cmdref` verbs (RQ-3 §5.3 verb whitelist). */\nconst CMD_REF_VERBS: readonly string[] = [\n\t\"node\",\n\t\"npm\",\n\t\"npx\",\n\t\"python\",\n\t\"python3\",\n\t\"pytest\",\n\t\"vitest\",\n\t\"git\",\n\t\"mw\",\n\t\"rg\",\n\t\"grep\",\n\t\"bash\",\n];\n\n/** `cmdref` result half: `rc=<digits>` plus optional `key=value` pairs. */\nconst CMD_RESULT_RE = /^rc=-?\\d+(?:\\s+[\\w.-]+=\\S+)*$/;\n\n/** One parsed evidence ref: a path with a line/line range, or a command. */\ninterface EvidenceRef {\n\tkind: \"path\" | \"cmd\";\n\t/** Repo-relative path (`\"\"` for a command ref). */\n\tpath: string;\n\tfirst: number;\n\tlast: number;\n}\n\n/** A path ref is repo-relative: no absolute path, no `./` prefix, no `..`. */\nfunction isRepoRelativePath(text: string): boolean {\n\tif (text === \"\" || text.startsWith(\"/\") || /^[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]/.test(text) || text.startsWith(\"./\")) return false;\n\treturn !text.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\");\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse one evidence ref (RQ-3 §5.3): `path:line`, `path:a-b`, optionally with\n * a `「excerpt」` suffix, or `verb rest => rc=N [k=v]`. `undefined` means the\n * ref does not match the frozen grammar (a `claim:<id>:evidence` gap).\n */\nfunction parseEvidenceRef(raw: string): EvidenceRef | undefined {\n\tconst ref = stripVerdictTicks(raw);\n\tif (ref === \"\" || ref === \"-\") return undefined;\n\tconst halves = ref.split(\"=>\");\n\tif (halves.length > 2) return undefined;\n\tif (halves.length === 2) {\n\t\tconst left = (halves[0] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\tconst right = (halves[1] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\t// RQ-3 §5.3: no `&&` / `;` (split above) / `>` / backticks inside a cmdref.\n\t\tif (left === \"\" || left.includes(\"&&\") || left.includes(\">\") || left.includes(\"<\") || left.includes(\"`\")) {\n\t\t\treturn undefined;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst verb = /^([A-Za-z0-9]+)\\s+/.exec(left)?.[1]?.toLowerCase() ?? \"\";\n\t\tif (!CMD_REF_VERBS.includes(verb) || !CMD_RESULT_RE.test(right)) return undefined;\n\t\treturn { kind: \"cmd\", path: \"\", first: 0, last: 0 };\n\t}\n\tconst withoutExcerpt = ref.replace(/「[^」]*」\\s*$/, \"\").trim();\n\tconst match = /^(.+?):(\\d+)(?:-(\\d+))?$/.exec(withoutExcerpt);\n\tif (match === null) return first : Number(match[3]);\n\tif (!Number.isInteger(first) || !Number.isInteger(last) || first < 1 || last < first) return undefined;\n\treturn { kind: \"path\", path: pathText, first, last };\n}\n\n/** Line count of a text file, trailing newline not counted as a line. */\nfunction lineCount(text: string): number {\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\treturn text.endsWith(\"\\n\") ? lines.length - 1 : lines.length;\n}\n\n/** True when a parsed path ref is not a usable citation: outside the project\n * root, not a file, a line past EOF, or a range wider than 200 lines. */\nfunction evidenceRefInvalid(ref: EvidenceRef, projectDir: string): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind === \"cmd\") return false;\n\tconst absolute = path.resolve(projectDir, ref.path);\n\tconst relative = path.relative(projectDir, absolute);\n\tif (relative === \"\" || relative === \"..\" || relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tlet text: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tif (!fs.statSync(absolute).isFile()) return true;\n\t\ttext = fs.readFileSync(absolute, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tif (ref.last > lineCount(text)) return true;\n\treturn ref.last - ref.first > 200;\n}\n\n/** Self-witness set of RQ-3 §4 (B-1/B-4): a claim citing only these files has\n * cited the report that contains it, not evidence. `progress.md` is allowed as\n * SECONDARY evidence (one real ref alongside it is enough), never as the only\n * one — which is exactly what \"every ref is self-witness\" means here. */\nconst SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES: readonly RegExp[] = [\n\t/^report.*\\.md$/i,\n\t/^output\\.md$/i,\n\t/^progress\\.md$/i,\n\t/^task\\.md$/i,\n];\n\n/** True when a path ref points into the self-witness set (any depth). */\nfunction isSelfEvidenceRef(ref: EvidenceRef): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind !== \"path\") return false;\n\tconst basename = ref.path.split(/[\\\\/]/).pop() ?? \"\";\n\treturn SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES.some((pattern) => pattern.test(basename));\n}\n\n/** `Σ预算` of the card's claims; a card that declares no `预算` at all falls\n * back to the calibrated call cap so a missing field cannot make every fetch a\n * gap (T-01's `claim:<id>:budget` already refuses that card at G1). */\nfunction declaredBudget(claims: Claim[]): number {\n\tlet sum = 0;\n\tlet declared = 0;\n\tfor (const claim of claims) {\n\t\tif (!Number.isFinite(claim.budget) || claim.budget < 0) continue;\n\t\tsum += claim.budget;\n\t\tdeclared += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn declared === 0 ? CLAIM_BUDGET.callCap : sum;\n}\n\n/** `取数` cell as a non-negative integer, `undefined` when it is not one. */\nfunction fetchCount(cell: string): number | undefined {\n\tconst text = stripVerdictTicks(cell);\n\treturn /^\\d+$/.test(text) ? Number(text) : undefined;\n}\n\n/** Ids T-01's own tautology judge (RQ-3 B-5) flags for this claim set. Reuses\n * `claimsGaps` so the `陈述`/`反证条件` similarity + new-artifact rule has ONE\n * implementation (the card forbids rewriting it and `shared/**` is out of the\n * write face, so the exported validator is the only legal handle). */\nfunction tautologyIds(claims: Claim[], projectDir: string): Set<string> {\n\tconst ids = new Set<string>();\n\tif (claims.length === 0) return ids;\n\tconst gaps = claimsGaps({ present: true, claims, errors: [] }, { projectDir, enforce: true });\n\tfor (const gap of gaps) {\n\t\tconst match = /^claim:(C-\\d{2,3}(?:\\.\\d+)?):tautology$/.exec(gap);\n\t\tif (match !== null && match[1] !== undefined) ids.add(match[1]);\n\t}\n\treturn ids;\n}\n\n/** Options of {@link claimCoverage}. `projectDir` is the root the evidence path\n * refs resolve against (the launcher's cwd in production, a fixture in tests). */\nexport interface ClaimCoverageOptions {\n\tprojectDir?: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge the `## 断言裁决` table against the card's claim set (RQ-3 §5, B-1/B-4/\n * B-10). Every returned string is one frozen criterion; the string IS the\n * diagnostic, so no second vocabulary is introduced.\n *\n * Criteria (in emission order):\n *   `claims:missing-table`            no `## 断言裁决` H2 at all\n *   `claim:<id>:missing-row`          a card claim the table never adjudicates\n *   `claims:extra-row:<id>`           a table row the card never declared\n *   `claim:<id>:verdict`              `裁决` outside closed|partial|unverified\n *   `claim:<id>:finding`              `判定` outside 成立|不成立|无法判定\n *   `claim:<id>:verdict-finding`      the two columns disagree (§5.1 mapping)\n *   `claim:<id>:evidence`             no evidence for closed/partial, or a ref\n *                                     that is unparsable / missing on disk /\n *                                     past EOF / wider than 200 lines\n *   `claim:<id>:reason`               `unverified` without a 7-word reason\n *   `claim:<id>:self-evidence`        every ref is `report*`/output/progress/task\n *   `claim:<id>:struct-held`          a `struct` row counted as `closed` (B-10)\n *   `claim:<id>:budget`               `取数` not a count, or > min(Σ预算, 30)\n *   `claim:<id>:tautology`            T-01's B-5 tautology judge fired\n *\n * Never throws. A claim-free card returns `[]` (nothing to adjudicate), and a\n * table-only run without claims is likewise not judged.\n */\nexport function claimCoverage(claims: Claim[], table: VerdictTable, opts: ClaimCoverageOptions = {}): string[] {\n\tconst gaps: string[] = [];\n\tif (claims.length === 0) return gaps;\n\tif (!table.present) return [\"claims:missing-table\"];\n\tconst projectDir = opts.projectDir ?? process.cwd();\n\tconst rows = new Map<string, VerdictRow>();\n\tfor (const row of table.rows) if (!rows.has(row.id)) rows.set(row.id, row);\n\tconst budgetCap = Math.min(declaredBudget(claims), CLAIM_BUDGET.callCap);\n\tconst tautological = tautologyIds(claims, projectDir);\n\tfor (const claim of claims) {\n\t\tconst row = rows.get(claim.id);\n\t\tif (row === undefined) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:missing-row`);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst verdict = verdictToken(row.verdict);\n\t\tconst finding = verdictToken(row.finding);\n\t\tif (!VERDICT_TOKENS.includes(verdict)) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:verdict`);\n\t\tif (!FINDING_TOKENS.includes(finding)) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:finding`);\n\t\tif (\n\t\t\tVERDICT_FINDINGS[verdict] !== undefined &&\n\t\t\tFINDING_TOKENS.includes(finding) &&\n\t\t\t!(VERDICT_FINDINGS[verdict] ?? []).includes(finding)\n\t\t) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:verdict-finding`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst refs = splitEvidenceRefs(row.evidence);\n\t\tconst parsed: Array<EvidenceRef | undefined> = refs.map((ref) => parseEvidenceRef(ref));\n\t\tconst needsEvidence = verdict === \"closed\" || verdict === \"partial\";\n\t\tif (needsEvidence && refs.length === 0) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:evidence`);\n\t\telse if (parsed.some((ref) => ref === undefined || evidenceRefInvalid(ref, projectDir))) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:evidence`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (verdict === \"unverified\" && !(UNVERIFIED_REASONS as readonly string[]).includes(verdictToken(row.reason))) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:reason`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst parsedAll: EvidenceRef[] = parsed.filter((ref): ref is EvidenceRef => ref !== undefined);\n\t\tif (parsedAll.length > 0 && parsedAll.length === refs.length && parsedAll.every(isSelfEvidenceRef)) {\n\t\t\tgaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:self-evidence`);\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst declaredType = row.type === \"\" ? claim.type.toLowerCase() : row.type;\n\t\tif (declaredType === \"struct\" && verdict === \"closed\") gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:struct-held`);\n\t\tconst fetches = fetchCount(row.fetches);\n\t\tif (fetches === undefined || fetches > budgetCap) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:budget`);\n\t\tif (tautological.has(claim.id)) gaps.push(`claim:${claim.id}:tautology`);\n\t}\n\tconst declaredIds = new Set(claims.map((claim) => claim.id));\n\tfor (const row of table.rows) {\n\t\tif (!declaredIds.has(row.id)) gaps.push(`claims:extra-row:${row.id}`);\n\t}\n\treturn gaps;\n}\n"]}

Every other section — `结论`, `证据`,\n * `残留与未验证`, `改动清单`, `未覆盖面声明`, and `## Questions` — is a\n * substantive judgement and is NEVER auto-generated; a whitelist (not a\n * blacklist) so a future section cannot be auto-filled by accident.\n */\nexport const MECHANICAL_SECTIONS: readonly string[] = [\"上下文来源\"];\n\n/** True when `name` is on the mechanical-backfill whitelist (R2). */\nexport function isMechanicalSection(name: string): boolean {\n\treturn MECHANICAL_SECTIONS.includes(name);\n}\n\n/** Which sections `type` must carry: the base four plus its role extra. */\nexport function recoverySectionsFor(type: string | undefined): string[] {\n\tconst required: string[] = [...RECOVERY_SECTIONS];\n\tif (type !== undefined) required.push(...(RECOVERY_TYPE_SECTIONS[type] ?? []));\n\treturn required;\n}\n\n/**\n * The `## 交付段契约（本角色）` block for `task_type`, or `\"\"` outside\n * `RECOVERY_CONTRACT_TYPES`. Every required section is rendered as a copyable\n * `- \\`## <段名>\\`` line so the worker can paste the canonical heading the\n * settle judge looks for — never an invented alias. Byte-shape mirror of\n * `dispatch.py::recovery_contract_section` so the two producers inject the same\n * section (idempotent on re-application).\n */\nexport function recoveryContractSection(type: string | undefined): string {\n\tif (type === undefined || !RECOVERY_CONTRACT_TYPES.includes(type)) return \"\";\n\tconst sections = recoverySectionsFor(type);\n\tif (sections.length === 0) return \"\";\n\treturn [\n\t\tRECOVERY_CONTRACT_HEADING,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t\t`本角色（type: ${type}）的恢复契约段：report.md / output.md 必须按下列标题成节（可直接复制；缺任一段即 settle 判缺失）：`,\n\t\t\"\",\n\t\t...sections.map((name) => `- \\`## ${name}\\``),\n\t].join(\"\\n\");\n}\n\n/** Fence opener/closer: 0-3 spaces then at least three backticks or tildes. */\nconst FENCE_RE = /^( {0,3})(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/;\n\n/** An H2 heading line: 0-3 leading spaces, exactly two `#` (never `###`), then\n * horizontal whitespace, then the heading text. */\nconst H2_RE = /^ {0,3}##(?!#)[ \\t]+(.*)$/;\n\n/** A blockquote line: its `#` is quoted data, not a heading. */\nconst BLOCKQUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}>/;\n\n/** Tracks fenced-code-block state across lines. An opening fence records its\n * marker char and length; the matching closing fence must use the same char,\n * the same-or-longer marker and carry nothing but whitespace after it. */\nfunction advanceFence(\n\tline: string,\n\topen: { char: string; len: number } | undefined,\n): { char: string; len: number } | undefined {\n\tconst match = FENCE_RE.exec(line);\n\tif (match === null) return open;\n\tconst marker = match[2] ?? \"\";\n\tconst rest = match[3] ?? \"\";\n\tconst char = marker[0] ?? \"\";\n\tif (open === undefined) return { char, len: marker.length };\n\tif (char === open.char && marker.length >= open.len && rest.trim() === \"\") return undefined;\n\treturn open;\n}\n\n/** Normalize one H2 heading: strip the trailing `#` closing sequence, trim,\n * collapse internal whitespace, ASCII-lower. */\nfunction normalizeHeading(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/#+\\s*$/, \"\")\n\t\t.trim()\n\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t.toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/**\n * The normalized H2 headings of `text`, in document order (design §4.1).\n * Fenced code blocks and blockquote lines contribute nothing; `###` is not an\n * H2. Exported for the AC-001 8-case matrix and for tests that lock the\n * normalization.\n */\nexport function h2Headings(text: string): string[] {\n\tconst out: string[] = [];\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tfor (const line of text.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n\t\tfence = advanceFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tif (BLOCKQUOTE_RE.test(line)) continue;\n\t\tconst match = H2_RE.exec(line);\n\t\tif (match === null) continue;\n\t\tout.push(normalizeHeading(match[1] ?? \"\"));\n\t}\n\treturn out;\n}\n\n/** One alias hit on one heading. */\nfunction headingHitsAlias(heading: string, aliases: readonly string[]): boolean {\n\treturn aliases.some((alias) => heading.includes(alias.toLowerCase()));\n}\n\nexport interface RecoveryVerdict {\n\t/** True when every required section is present. */\n\tok: boolean;\n\t/** Required sections with no H2 heading hit, in contract order. Empty iff `ok`. */\n\tmissing: string[];\n\t/** The full required list for the given type (diagnostic/tests). */\n\trequired: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Judge an agent-authored product text against the recovery contract.\n *\n * `text` is the agent's report (what `report.md` / `output.md` already carries,\n * or the final reply) — never the harness block the writer appends afterwards.\n * `type` is the header `type:` of the dispatch; `undefined` (legacy/manual task\n * book) yields the base four, and the caller is responsible for only asking at\n * all when the dispatch is forward (see `worker/output-writer.ts`).\n *\n * Never throws: any string (including empty) yields a verdict.\n */\nexport function checkRecovery(text: string, type: string | undefined): RecoveryVerdict {\n\tconst required = recoverySectionsFor(type);\n\tconst headings = h2Headings(text);\n\tconst missing = required.filter((name) => {\n\t\tconst aliases = RECOVERY_SECTION_ALIASES[name] ?? [name];\n\t\treturn !headings.some((heading) => headingHitsAlias(heading, aliases));\n\t});\n\treturn { ok: missing.length === 0, missing, required };\n}\n\n// ── T-04a: the `## 断言裁决` verdict table (design §2.2/§3.3, RQ-3 §5) ────────\n//\n// The L3 settle layer judges what the worker CLAIMS to have settled. The\n// table is agent-authored (`## 断言裁决`), seven columns, free column order,\n// extra columns ignored, fenced code blocks excluded, full-width forms folded\n// (RQ-3 §5.6, the P-048 tolerance lesson). Every gap string below is frozen:\n// `claim:<id>:<element>` / `claims:<rule>:<detail>` — the same shape T-01's\n// `claimsGaps` already froze, so the refusal text and the settle readback can\n// concatenate either list without a second vocabulary.\n\n/** H2 aliases of the verdict table. `## 断言裁决（claims）` still hits because\n * the match is `includes`, exactly like `RECOVERY_SECTION_ALIASES`. */\nconst VERDICT_TABLE_ALIASES: readonly string[] = [\"断言裁决\", \"claim verdict\", \"claims verdict\", \"verdict table\"];\n\n/** The seven judged columns (RQ-3 §5.1). */\ntype VerdictField = \"id\" | \"type\" | \"verdict\" | \"finding\" | \"evidence\" | \"fetches\" | \"reason\";\n\n/** Header aliases per column, both scripts (RQ-3 §5.6). */\nconst VERDICT_COLUMN_ALIASES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [VerdictField, readonly string[]]> = [\n\t[\"id\", [\"claim\", \"断言\", \"claim id\"]],\n\t[\"type\", [\"类型\", \"type\", \"类别\"]],\n\t[\"verdict\", [\"裁决\", \"verdict\"]],\n\t[\"finding\", [\"判定\", \"finding\", \"判断\"]],\n\t[\"evidence\", [\"证据\", \"evidence\"]],\n\t[\"fetches\", [\"取数\", \"fetches\", \"reads\"]],\n\t[\"reason\", [\"原因\", \"reason\"]],\n];\n\n/** One parsed `## 断言裁决` row, all cells trimmed (never normalized away: the\n * raw cell text is what the diagnostics quote). */\nexport interface VerdictRow {\n\t/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` id, upper-cased. */\n\tid: string;\n\t/** `类型` cell, lower-cased, `\"\"` when the column is absent. */\n\ttype: string;\n\tverdict: string;\n\tfinding: string;\n\tevidence: string;\n\tfetches: string;\n\treason: string;\n\t/** 1-based line of the row in the parsed text (diagnostics only). */\n\trow: number;\n}\n\n/** Result of {@link parseVerdictTable}. Never throws (P-048). */\nexport interface VerdictTable {\n\t/** The `## 断言裁决` H2 was seen outside a fence. */\n\tpresent: boolean;\n\trows: VerdictRow[];\n\t/** `claim:<row>:unparsable` findings, row = 1-based source line. */\n\terrors: string[];\n}\n\n/** `C-01` / `C-01.3` (the same id shape `parseClaimsBlock` accepts). */\nconst VERDICT_ID_RE = /^C-(\\d{2,3})(?:\\.(\\d+))?$/i;\n\n/** Header index per judged column, filled in header order. */\ntype VerdictColumns = Partial<Record<VerdictField, number>>;\n\n/** Fold the full-width forms the card corpus mixes in (RQ-3 §5.6): `：` -> `:`,\n * `｜` -> `|`, full-width digits -> ASCII digits, ideographic space -> space.\n * Mirror of the private helper in `shared/dispatch-card.ts` (the claims block\n * parser); the exported constants are imported, never copied. */\nfunction normalizeVerdictText(text: string): string {\n\treturn text\n\t\t.replace(/[\\uFF10-\\uFF19]/g, (digit) => String.fromCharCode(digit.charCodeAt(0) - 0xfee0))\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF1A/g, \":\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\uFF5C/g, \"|\")\n\t\t.replace(/\\u3000/g, \" \")\n\t\t.trim();\n}\n\n/** Cells never carry markdown code fences: strip the backticks a writer adds. */\nfunction stripVerdictTicks(text: string): string {\n\treturn text.replace(/`/g, \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** Split a `| a | b |` row into trimmed cells (leading/trailing pipes dropped). */\nfunction splitVerdictRow(line: string): string[] {\n\tconst cells = normalizeVerdictText(line).split(\"|\");\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[0] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.shift();\n\tif (cells.length > 0 && (cells[cells.length - 1] ?? \"\").trim() === \"\") cells.pop();\n\treturn cells.map((cell) => cell.trim());\n}\n\n/** Header of a verdict table, `undefined` when the row is not a header. */\nfunction matchVerdictHeader(cells: string[]): VerdictColumns | undefined {\n\tconst columns: VerdictColumns = {};\n\tlet hasClaimColumn = false;\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < cells.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst name = stripVerdictTicks(normalizeVerdictText(cells[i] ?? \"\"))\n\t\t\t.toLowerCase()\n\t\t\t.replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n\t\t\t.replace(/:$/, \"\");\n\t\tfor (const [field, aliases] of VERDICT_COLUMN_ALIASES) {\n\t\t\tif (!aliases.includes(name)) continue;\n\t\t\tif (columns[field] === undefined) columns[field] = i;\n\t\t\tif (field === \"id\") hasClaimColumn = true;\n\t\t\tbreak;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn hasClaimColumn ? columns : undefined;\n}\n\n/** `| --- | --- |` separator row (any dash count, optional alignment colons). */\nfunction isVerdictSeparatorRow(cells: string[]): boolean {\n\tif (cells.length === 0) return false;\n\treturn cells.every((cell) => cell === \"\" || /^:?-{1,}:?$/.test(cell));\n}\n\n/** Cell of `field` in `cells`, `\"\"` when the column is absent (tolerance). */\nfunction verdictCell(cells: string[], columns: VerdictColumns, field: VerdictField): string {\n\tconst index = columns[field];\n\tif (index === undefined) return \"\";\n\treturn (cells[index] ?? \"\").trim();\n}\n\n/** One table row -> {@link VerdictRow}, `undefined` when the id is unparsable. */\nfunction verdictRowFrom(cells: string[], columns: VerdictColumns, row: number): VerdictRow | undefined {\n\tconst idMatch = VERDICT_ID_RE.exec(stripVerdictTicks(verdictCell(cells, columns, \"id\")));\n\tif (idMatch === null) return undefined;\n\tconst number = idMatch[1] ?? \"\";\n\tconst child = idMatch[2];\n\treturn {\n\t\tid: `C-${number}${child === undefined ? \"\" : `.${child}`}`,\n\t\ttype: stripVerdictTicks(verdictCell(cells, columns, \"type\")).toLowerCase(),\n\t\tverdict: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"verdict\"),\n\t\tfinding: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"finding\"),\n\t\tevidence: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"evidence\"),\n\t\tfetches: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"fetches\"),\n\t\treason: verdictCell(cells, columns, \"reason\"),\n\t\trow,\n\t};\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse the agent-authored `## 断言裁决` table (RQ-3 §5.1/§5.6).\n *\n * Tolerance is the contract (P-048): the heading may carry a suffix, column\n * order is free, extra columns are ignored, header words take both scripts,\n * full-width `：｜`/digits fold to ASCII, and fenced code blocks contribute\n * nothing (the same fence state machine `h2Headings` uses). A row whose\n * `claim` cell is not a claim id is reported as `claim:<row>:unparsable` and\n * skipped; this function never throws.\n */\nexport function parseVerdictTable(text: string): VerdictTable {\n\tconst table: VerdictTable = { present: false, rows: [], errors: [] };\n\tlet fence: { char: string; len: number } | undefined;\n\tlet inSection = false;\n\tlet columns: VerdictColumns | undefined;\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\tfor (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n\t\tconst line = lines[i] ?? \"\";\n\t\tfence = advanceFence(line, fence);\n\t\tif (fence !== undefined) continue;\n\t\tconst heading = H2_RE.exec(line);\n\t\tif (heading !== null) {\n\t\t\tconst normalized = normalizeHeading(heading[1] ?? \"\");\n\t\t\tif (inSection) {\n\t\t\t\tinSection = false;\n\t\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif (!table.present && VERDICT_TABLE_ALIASES.some((alias) => normalized.includes(alias))) {\n\t\t\t\t// RQ-3 §5.6: `## 断言裁决（claims）` hits, the body starts below it.\n\t\t\t\ttable.present = true;\n\t\t\t\tinSection = true;\n\t\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (!inSection) continue;\n\t\tif (BLOCKQUOTE_RE.test(line)) continue;\n\t\tif (!normalizeVerdictText(line).startsWith(\"|\")) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = undefined;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst cells = splitVerdictRow(line);\n\t\tif (columns === undefined) {\n\t\t\tcolumns = matchVerdictHeader(cells);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (isVerdictSeparatorRow(cells)) continue;\n\t\tconst row = verdictRowFrom(cells, columns, i + 1);\n\t\tif (row === undefined) {\n\t\t\ttable.errors.push(`claim:${i + 1}:unparsable`);\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\ttable.rows.push(row);\n\t}\n\treturn table;\n}\n\n/** `裁决` closed set (RQ-3 §5.2; no `done`/`PASS`/`ok`/`verified`/`N/A`). */\nconst VERDICT_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\"closed\", \"partial\", \"unverified\"];\n\n/** `判定` closed set (RQ-3 §5.1) plus the `partial` render token `部分成立` —\n * §5.1's own mapping (`partial` -> 部分成立) has no other representable form,\n * so excluding it here would make `partial` unusable. */\nconst FINDING_TOKENS: readonly string[] = [\"成立\", \"不成立\", \"无法判定\", \"部分成立\"];\n\n/** Allowed `判定` per `裁决` (RQ-3 §5.1: `closed` settles either way). */\nconst VERDICT_FINDINGS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {\n\tclosed: [\"成立\", \"不成立\"],\n\tpartial: [\"部分成立\"],\n\tunverified: [\"无法判定\"],\n};\n\n/** Fold a closed-set cell to its token form (ticks, whitespace, ASCII case). */\nfunction verdictToken(cell: string): string {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell).replace(/\\s+/g, \"\").toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/** Evidence ref separators (`;` and the full-width `；` — a real review emitted\n * `a.py:1-4；b.ts:7` on the first live e2e and the ASCII-only split read the whole\n * cell as one nonexistent path, costing two false gaps, P-048) and the `-` empty\n * marker. */\nfunction splitEvidenceRefs(cell: string): string[] {\n\treturn stripVerdictTicks(cell)\n\t\t.split(/[;；]/)\n\t\t.map((ref) => ref.trim())\n\t\t.filter((ref) => ref !== \"\" && ref !== \"-\");\n}\n\n/** `cmdref` verbs (RQ-3 §5.3 verb whitelist). */\nconst CMD_REF_VERBS: readonly string[] = [\n\t\"node\",\n\t\"npm\",\n\t\"npx\",\n\t\"python\",\n\t\"python3\",\n\t\"pytest\",\n\t\"vitest\",\n\t\"git\",\n\t\"mw\",\n\t\"rg\",\n\t\"grep\",\n\t\"bash\",\n];\n\n/** `cmdref` result half: `rc=<digits>` plus optional `key=value` pairs. */\nconst CMD_RESULT_RE = /^rc=-?\\d+(?:\\s+[\\w.-]+=\\S+)*$/;\n\n/** One parsed evidence ref: a path with a line/line range, or a command. */\ninterface EvidenceRef {\n\tkind: \"path\" | \"cmd\";\n\t/** Repo-relative path (`\"\"` for a command ref). */\n\tpath: string;\n\tfirst: number;\n\tlast: number;\n}\n\n/** A path ref is repo-relative: no absolute path, no `./` prefix, no `..`. */\nfunction isRepoRelativePath(text: string): boolean {\n\tif (text === \"\" || text.startsWith(\"/\") || /^[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]/.test(text) || text.startsWith(\"./\")) return false;\n\treturn !text.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\");\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse one evidence ref (RQ-3 §5.3): `path:line`, `path:a-b`, optionally with\n * a `「excerpt」` suffix, or `verb rest => rc=N [k=v]`. `undefined` means the\n * ref does not match the frozen grammar (a `claim:<id>:evidence` gap).\n */\nfunction parseEvidenceRef(raw: string): EvidenceRef | undefined {\n\tconst ref = stripVerdictTicks(raw);\n\tif (ref === \"\" || ref === \"-\") return undefined;\n\tconst halves = ref.split(\"=>\");\n\tif (halves.length > 2) return undefined;\n\tif (halves.length === 2) {\n\t\tconst left = (halves[0] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\tconst right = (halves[1] ?? \"\").trim();\n\t\t// RQ-3 §5.3: no `&&` / `;` (split above) / `>` / backticks inside a cmdref.\n\t\tif (left === \"\" || left.includes(\"&&\") || left.includes(\">\") || left.includes(\"<\") || left.includes(\"`\")) {\n\t\t\treturn undefined;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst verb = /^([A-Za-z0-9]+)\\s+/.exec(left)?.[1]?.toLowerCase() ?? \"\";\n\t\tif (!CMD_REF_VERBS.includes(verb) || !CMD_RESULT_RE.test(right)) return undefined;\n\t\treturn { kind: \"cmd\", path: \"\", first: 0, last: 0 };\n\t}\n\tconst withoutExcerpt = ref.replace(/「[^」]*」\\s*$/, \"\").trim();\n\tconst match = /^(.+?):(\\d+)(?:-(\\d+))?$/.exec(withoutExcerpt);\n\tif (match === null) return first : Number(match[3]);\n\tif (!Number.isInteger(first) || !Number.isInteger(last) || first < 1 || last < first) return undefined;\n\treturn { kind: \"path\", path: pathText, first, last };\n}\n\n/** Line count of a text file, trailing newline not counted as a line. */\nfunction lineCount(text: string): number {\n\tconst lines = text.split(/\\r?\\n/);\n\treturn text.endsWith(\"\\n\") ? lines.length - 1 : lines.length;\n}\n\n/** True when a parsed path ref is not a usable citation: outside the project\n * root, not a file, a line past EOF, or a range wider than 200 lines. */\nfunction evidenceRefInvalid(ref: EvidenceRef, projectDir: string): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind === \"cmd\") return false;\n\tconst absolute = path.resolve(projectDir, ref.path);\n\tconst relative = path.relative(projectDir, absolute);\n\tif (relative === \"\" || relative === \"..\" || relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tlet text: string;\n\ttry {\n\t\tif (!fs.statSync(absolute).isFile()) return true;\n\t\ttext = fs.readFileSync(absolute, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn true;\n\t}\n\tif (ref.last > lineCount(text)) return true;\n\treturn ref.last - ref.first > 200;\n}\n\n/** Self-witness set of RQ-3 §4 (B-1/B-4): a claim citing only these files has\n * cited the report that contains it, not evidence. `progress.md` is allowed as\n * SECONDARY evidence (one real ref alongside it is enough), never as the only\n * one — which is exactly what \"every ref is self-witness\" means here. */\nconst SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES: readonly RegExp[] = [\n\t/^report.*\\.md$/i,\n\t/^output\\.md$/i,\n\t/^progress\\.md$/i,\n\t/^task\\.md$/i,\n];\n\n/** True when a path ref points into the self-witness set (any depth). */\nfunction isSelfEvidenceRef(ref: EvidenceRef): boolean {\n\tif (ref.kind !== \"path\") return false;\n\tconst basename = ref.path.split(/[\\\\/]/).pop() ?? \"\";\n\treturn SELF_EVIDENCE_BASENAMES.some((pattern) => pattern.test(basename));\n}\n\n/** `Σ预算` of the card's claims; a card that declares no `预算` at all falls\n * back to the calibrated call cap so a missing field cannot make every fetch a\n * gap (T-01's `claim:<id>:budget` already refuses that card at G1). */\nfunction declaredBudget(claims: Claim[]): number {\n\tlet sum = 0;\n\tlet declared = 0;\n\tfor (const claim of claims) {\n\t\tif (!Number.isFinite(claim.budget) || claim.budget < 0) continue;\n\t\tsum += claim.budget;\n\t\tdeclared += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn declared === 0 ? The runtime\n * write-surface guard must cover these roles on the `write`/`edit` channel even\n * when they have no `bash` (`roadmap-writer` was unguarded before D-115). */\nexport function hasWriteTools(taskType: string): boolean {\n\tconst tools = activeToolsForType(taskType);\n\treturn tools.includes(\"write\") || tools.includes(\"edit\");\n}\n\n// ── decision worker type (mw-decision-substitution W8, renamed W10) ──────────\n//\n// W10: the dispatch type value is `decide_prepare` (was `decision`); no alias\n// is kept, so `type: decision` is now an unknown type.\n//\n// A `decide_prepare` worker writes ONE decision book: scaffold it, fill every field\n// from real evidence, pass `mw decide book check`, and hand the book back. It\n// never edits code and never sends the book: the send (`decide run|ask --book`)\n// is the PM's call unless the card explicitly says `allow-send: yes`.\n//\n// Three runtime pieces live here:\n//   1. the fixed prompt (`DECISION_TYPE_PROMPT`) — injected into the system\n//      prompt of every turn of a decision worker, so the contract cannot be\n//      lost by compaction or by a terse card;\n//   2. a read-only bash policy (`decisionBashBlockReason`) that blocks every\n//      command except `mw decide book check`, `git diff|status|log`, `rg`,\n//      `cat`, `ls`, `head`, `tail`, `wc` — and blocks `decide run|ask` unless\n//      the card authorized the send;\n//   3. a `worker_file` target policy (`decisionWorkerFilePathAllowed`) that\n//      keeps the only write channel inside `<key>/evidence/books/**`.\n\nexport const DECIDE_PREPARE_TYPE = \"decide_prepare\";\n/** Card item carrying the send authority (`yes` = the worker may send). */\nexport const DECISION_ALLOW_SEND_ITEM = \"allow-send\";\n/** The one directory a decision book may be written to. */\nexport const DECISION_BOOK_SUBDIR = \"evidence/books\";\n\n/** The fixed decision-worker prompt (card requirement 2). */\nexport const DECISION_TYPE_PROMPT = [\n\t\"[mw decide_prepare worker] 你写决策本，不改代码。\",\n\t\"1. 先跑 `mw decide book new <dp> --out <key>/evidence/books/<dp>-<slug>.json`；<dp> 与 book 路径见 task.md 的「决策本参数」段。\",\n\t\"2. 按每个字段的 description 从证据里填值；`notes.evidence` 每条给 `path:line` 或命令原文。\",\n\t\"3. 最后跑 `mw decide book check <book>`；失败就继续填，直到通过。\",\n\t\"不要改阈值、不要填预期答案、不要改任何代码（packages/ 只读）。\",\n\t\"bash 只允许 `mw decide book check`、`git diff --stat`、`rg`、`cat` 这类只读命令。\",\n\t\"`allow-send: no` 时不要调用 `decide run` / `decide ask`（含 `--book`）；发送由 PM 做。\",\n].join(\"\\n\");\n\n/** Does the task authorize the worker itself to send the book?\n *\n * Only an explicit `allow-send: yes` line does (`- allow-send: yes` or\n * `allow-send: yes`); every other shape — absent, `no`, garbage — is the\n * closed state (W8 requirement 4: the default is `no`). */\nexport function decisionAllowsSend(taskContent: string): boolean {\n\tfor (const raw of taskContent.split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n\t\tconst m = /^\\s*(?:[-*+]\\s*)?(?:\\*\\*)?allow-send(?:\\*\\*)?\\s*[:：]\\s*(\\S+)/i.exec(raw);\n\t\tif (m) return m[1].trim().toLowerCase() === \"yes\";\n\t}\n\treturn false;\n}\n\n/** Commands a decision worker may run (read-only subset, card requirement 2).\n * Order matters only for the audit message. */\nconst DECISION_ALLOWED_COMMANDS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [RegExp, string]> = [\n\t[/^mw\\s+decide\\s+book\\s+check\\b/, \"mw decide book status\"],\n\t[/^git\\s+log\\b/, \"git log\"],\n\t[/^rg\\b/, \"rg\"],\n\t[/^cat\\b/, \"cat\"],\n\t[/^ls\\b/, \"ls\"],\n\t[/^head\\b/, \"head\"],\n\t[/^tail\\b/, \"tail\"],\n\t[/^wc\\b/, \"wc\"],\n];\n\n/** Shell metacharacters a read-only decision command may never carry. */\nconst DECISION_BASH_REDIRECT_RE =\n\t/[<>]|\\btee\\b|\\brm\\b|\\bmv\\b|\\bcp\\b|\\bsed\\s+-i\\b|\\bgit\\s+(?:add|commit|checkout|reset)\\b|\\bpython\\S*\\s+-c\\b/;\n\n/** The `decide run|ask` invocations (with or without `--book`). */\nconst DECISION_SEND_RE = /\\bdecide\\s+(?:run|ask)\\b/;\n\n/** The scaffold call (`book new`), which may WRITE exactly one file: its\n * `--out` target (W8: the prompt's first step, still bounded to the books dir).\n * Without `--out` it only prints to stdout — that shape writes nothing. */\nconst DECISION_BOOK_NEW_RE = /^(?:mw\\s+decide\\s+book\\s+new|python\\S*\\s+.*\\bmw\\.py\\s+decide\\s+book\\s+new)\\b/;\n\n/** Block reason for one decision-worker bash command, or `null` when allowed.\n *\n * Splits on the shell control operators (`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, newline) so a\n * chained write (`rg x && rm -rf y`) cannot hide behind an allowed prefix, and\n * refuses redirections/known mutators outright (P1: for this role a false\n * block costs one retry, a miss writes outside the books dir).\n *\n * `mw decide book new` is allowed on top of the card's read-only list because\n * the prompt's FIRST step is that scaffold; its `--out` must stay inside\n * `evidence/books/**` and the no-`--out` shape only prints to stdout. */\nexport function decisionBashBlockReason(command: string, allowSend: boolean): string | null {\n\tconst send = DECISION_SEND_RE.exec(command);\n\tif (send && !allowSend) {\n\t\treturn (\n\t\t\t`decision: \\`decide ${send[0].split(/\\s+/)[1]}\\` is the PM's call — this card says ` +\n\t\t\t`\\`allow-send: no\\` (or nothing), so only \\`mw decide book check\\` is allowed`\n\t\t);\n\t}\n\tconst allowed = DECISION_ALLOWED_COMMANDS.map(([, label]) => label).join(\", \");\n\tfor (const raw of command.split(/&&|\\|\\||[;|\\n]/)) {\n\t\tconst segment = raw.trim();\n\t\tif (segment === \"\") continue;\n\t\tif (DECISION_BASH_REDIRECT_RE.test(segment)) {\n\t\t\treturn `decision: bash is read-only for this role (no redirect/mutation); allowed: ${allowed}`;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (DECISION_BOOK_NEW_RE.test(segment)) {\n\t\t\tconst out = /--out(?:=|\\s+)(\\S+)/.exec(segment);\n\t\t\tconst target = out?.[1]?.replace(/^[\"']|[\"']$/g, \"\") ?? \"\";\n\t\t\tif (target !== \"\" && !decisionWorkerFilePathAllowed(target)) {\n\t\t\t\treturn (\n\t\t\t\t\t`decision: \\`book new --out\\` must target ${DECISION_BOOK_SUBDIR}/** ` +\n\t\t\t\t\t`(got ${JSON.stringify(target)})`\n\t\t\t\t);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (send && segment.includes(send[0]) && allowSend) continue;\n\t\tif (!DECISION_ALLOWED_COMMANDS.some(([pattern]) => pattern.test(segment))) {\n\t\t\treturn (\n\t\t\t\t`decision: bash is read-only for this role; \\`${segment.split(/\\s+/)[0]}\\` is not allowed ` +\n\t\t\t\t`(allowed: ${allowed})`\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn null;\n}\n\n/** Is this `worker_file` target inside the decision book directory?\n *\n * Accepts both spellings the tool documents: `evidence/books/<f>` (taskDir\n * relative) and `.agenticdoc/<key>/evidence/books/<f>`. Everything else — the\n * broader `<key>/evidence/**` face, `progress.md`, a source file — is refused\n * (W8 requirement 3: the write face narrows to the books dir). */\nexport function decisionWorkerFilePathAllowed(file: string): boolean {\n\tconst normalized = file.trim().replace(/\\\\/g, \"/\").replace(/^\\.\\//, \"\");\n\tif (normalized === \"\" || normalized.startsWith(\"/\") || /^[A-Za-z]:\\//.test(normalized)) {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n\tif (normalized.split(\"/\").includes(\"..\")) return false;\n\treturn normalized.includes(`${DECISION_BOOK_SUBDIR}/`);\n}\n\n/** Checkpoint self-assessment steer text, split by role (D-104/VC-004).\n * - `hasWriteTools === true`: the pre-change wording byte for byte — the\n *   agent appends its own CKPT line to progress.md with its write tool.\n * - `hasWriteTools === false`: never tells the agent to append to a file it\n *   cannot write. The machine evidence is already on disk (framework-written),\n *   and the self-assessment goes through the narrow tool or the reply.\n * `deliverAs` stays `followUp` for both branches (decided by the caller). */\nexport function checkpointSteerText(opts: {\n\telapsedMs: number;\n\tbudgetMs: number;\n\tprogressPath: string;\n\thasWriteTools: boolean;\n\tnarrowTool: string;\n}): string {\n\tif (opts.hasWriteTools) {\n\t\treturn `[mw checkpoint] 运行 ${formatHeartbeatAge(opts.elapsedMs)}（总预算 ${formatHeartbeatAge(\n\t\t\topts.budgetMs,\n\t\t)}）。请立即自评收敛性，把一行追加到 ${opts.progressPath}：CKPT ${Math.round(\n\t\t\topts.elapsedMs / 60_000,\n\t\t)}m converging=yes|no eta≈<X>m <一句话理由>。若不收敛：立即收窄范围，优先保证已完成部分可交付，不要展开新工作。`;\n\t}\n\treturn `[mw checkpoint] 运行 ${formatHeartbeatAge(opts.elapsedMs)}（总预算 ${formatHeartbeatAge(\n\t\topts.budgetMs,\n\t)}）。检查点机器证据（reads/writes/phases/risk）已由框架写入 ${opts.progressPath}。请立即自评收敛性：用 ${\n\t\topts.narrowTool\n\t} 工具把一行自评写入该文件，或在本回复中直接给出一行 CKPT ${Math.round(\n\t\topts.elapsedMs / 60_000,\n\t)}m converging=yes|no eta≈<X>m <一句话理由>。若不收敛：立即收窄范围，优先保证已完成部分可交付，不要展开新工作。`;\n}\n\n// ── Watchdog budgets (GC-4 as amended 2026-09-09: activity-based hang\n// detection + per-task wall budget) ─────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/** Default wall budget. The old 30m value killed healthy tasks (OverCode\n * cpr-004/005: actively working 28s/9s before the kill); 60m covers every\n * observed successful run (7–14m) with margin for generation-heavy tasks. */\nexport const DEFAULT_BUDGET_MS = 60 * 60_000;\n\n/** Default hang threshold: no activity (token deltas, tools, turns) for this\n * long while the task is unfinished means a dead API call. Conservative —\n * above the 7m legit single-generation observed on glm-5.3 (cpr-003); tighten\n * after confirming streaming deltas arrive on the timi route. */\nexport const DEFAULT_IDLE_MS = 10 * 60_000;\n\nconst CHECKPOINT_ANCHOR_MS = 30 * 60_000;\nconst CHECKPOINT_REFRESH_MS = 10 * 60_000;\nconst STEER_MIN_MS = 5 * 60_000;\n\n/** Wall budget: task.md `timeout:` (minutes) > PI_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS > default. */\nexport function resolveBudgetMs(timeoutMin: number | undefined, env: string | undefined): number {\n\tif (timeoutMin !== undefined) return timeoutMin * 60_000;\n\tconst envMs = Number(env);\n\tif (Number.isFinite(envMs) && envMs > 0) return envMs;\n\treturn DEFAULT_BUDGET_MS;\n}\n\n/** Hang threshold from PI_WORKER_IDLE_MS (falling back to the default). */\nexport function resolveIdleMs(env: string | undefined): number {\n\tconst envMs = Number(env);\n\tif (Number.isFinite(envMs) && envMs > 0) return envMs;\n\treturn DEFAULT_IDLE_MS;\n}\n\n/** Max silence allowed while a tool is in flight, before the in-flight branch\n * of the idle watchdog kills. Root cause (measured 2026-09-26, T-04/AC-005):\n * 22/24 idle kills died while a bash call was in flight with zero\n * `tool_execution_update` — bash updates are output-driven (core/tools/bash.ts),\n * so a long command that prints nothing looked like a hung worker. A tool that\n * is still running legitimately owns the activity clock, but only up to a\n * bound: a genuinely hung tool must still die (VC-006). 30m mirrors the\n * design's floor (D-016) and sits inside the 60m default wall budget, which\n * remains the outer guard. Deliberately a code constant: T-04 forbids a new\n * config key, so this is NOT wired through `_autopilot/config.json`.\n *\n * Deliberately does not change `DEFAULT_IDLE_MS` or the PI_WORKER_IDLE_MS\n * semantics: the threshold was never the root cause. */\nexport const DEFAULT_TOOL_IDLE_MS = 30 * 60_000;\n\n/** Effective in-flight tool-idle bound: the configured raw idle threshold\n * (lower bound, so a tightened PI_WORKER_IDLE_MS also tightens this) vs the\n * 30m floor. */\nexport function resolveToolIdleMs(idleMs: number): number {\n\treturn Math.max(idleMs, DEFAULT_TOOL_IDLE_MS);\n}\n\n/** First convergence-checkpoint time: the 30m anchor, scaled down\n * proportionally for small budgets so smoke runs exercise the whole path. */\nexport function checkpointAnchorMs(budgetMs: number): number {\n\treturn Math.min(CHECKPOINT_ANCHOR_MS, Math.max(1_000, Math.round(budgetMs / 2)));\n}\n\n/** Deadline-steer time: budget minus min(5m, budget/4). */\nexport function steerAtMs(budgetMs: number): number {\n\treturn Math.max(1_000, budgetMs - Math.min(STEER_MIN_MS, Math.round(budgetMs / 4)));\n}\n\n/** Read-ish tools for checkpoint convergence signals. */\nconst READ_TOOLS = new Set([\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\", \"glob\"]);\n/** Write-ish tools for checkpoint convergence signals. */\nconst WRITE_TOOLS = new Set([\"write\", \"edit\"]);\n\n/** T-04/AC-009: freshness floor for a landing — one minute, so a small smoke\n * budget (anchor 60s) still has an exercisable window. */\nexport const LAND_FRESH_FLOOR_MS = 60_000;\n\n/** T-04/AC-009: how recent the newest landing must be to count as \"fresh\"\n * (a writeless run that is still producing). `anchor/3` floored at 1m: the\n * default anchor (30m) yields 10m, exactly the checkpoint refresh cadence. */\nexport function landFreshMs(anchorMs: number): number {\n\treturn Math.max(LAND_FRESH_FLOOR_MS, Math.round(anchorMs / 3));\n}\n\nexport interface ConvergenceSignals {\n\telapsedMs: number;\n\t/** Checkpoint anchor (min(30m, budget/2)) — the point past which zero\n\t * output stops being \"warming up\" and starts being divergence. */\n\tanchorMs: number;\n\twrites: number;\n\tphasesTotal: number;\n\tphasesDone: number;\n\t/** Highest per-target repeat count for reads. */\n\trepeatTop: number;\n\t/** T-04/AC-009 writeless landing signals, sourced from `parseWriteFileEvents`\n\t * (the change ledger the settle judgement reads — never `[TOOL] worker_file`\n\t * counts). Undefined for write roles ⇒ the legacy rule below applies byte for\n\t * byte; `landed: 0` is a signal, not an absence of one. */\n\tlanded?: number;\n\t/** Age of the newest landing on disk (ms). Undefined = no surviving target. */\n\tlastLandingAgeMs?: number;\n\t/** A non-empty product exists on disk (channel-independent ground truth). */\n\tartifactPresent?: boolean;\n\t/** `progress.md` carries the role's own completion record. */\n\tprogressDone?: boolean;\n}\n\n/** Machine divergence heuristic (AC-004, advisory only — the PM with the\n * fullest context judges and decides):\n * - high: past the anchor with ZERO writes — pure exploration, the cpr-007\n *   pattern (22 minutes of reads, generation never got time to land).\n * - mid: phase framework present but nothing completed past the anchor, or\n *   the same target read ≥4 times (spinning).\n * - low: writes advancing — implementation underway.\n *\n * T-04/AC-009: when the caller supplies landing signals (`landed !== undefined`,\n * writeless roles), the counts `writes`/`uniq_targets` stop being the criterion\n * (they are structurally 0 for those roles) and the ledger + disk facts decide:\n * - W2a: a non-empty product on disk ⇒ low (strongest convergence evidence;\n *   outranks a missed ledger event).\n * - W1: nothing landed at all past the anchor ⇒ high (unchanged intent).\n * - W2b: a fresh landing plus the role's own `converging=yes` note ⇒ low.\n * - W3/W4: landed-but-stale (or nothing before the anchor) — only read spin or\n *   stalled phases are mid, everything else is low. */\nexport function computeRisk(s: ConvergenceSignals): \"low\" | \"mid\" | \"high\" {\n\tif (s.landed !== undefined) {\n\t\tconst stalled = s.phasesTotal > 0 && s.phasesDone === 0 && s.elapsedMs >= s.anchorMs;\n\t\tif (s.artifactPresent === true) return \"low\";\n\t\tif (s.landed === 0 && s.elapsedMs >= s.anchorMs) return \"high\";\n\t\tconst fresh = s.lastLandingAgeMs !== undefined && s.lastLandingAgeMs <= landFreshMs(s.anchorMs);\n\t\tif (s.landed > 0 && fresh && s.progressDone === true) return \"low\";\n\t\treturn stalled || s.repeatTop >= 4 ? \"mid\" : \"low\";\n\t}\n\tif (s.writes === 0 && s.elapsedMs >= s.anchorMs) return \"high\";\n\tif ((s.phasesTotal > 0 && s.phasesDone === 0 && s.elapsedMs >= s.anchorMs) || s.repeatTop >= 4) return \"mid\";\n\treturn \"low\";\n}\n\n/** T-04/AC-009: what the writeless checkpoint actually observes. */\nexport interface LandingSignals {\n\t/** Distinct `[WRITE_FILE]` targets (parseWriteFileEvents dedup). */\n\tlanded: number;\n\t/** Age of the newest surviving landing; undefined = no target on disk. */\n\tlastLandingAgeMs: number | undefined;\n\t/** A non-empty product exists on disk. */\n\tartifactPresent: boolean;\n\t/** `progress.md` carries the role's own completion record. */\n\tprogressDone: boolean;\n}\n\n/** T-04/AC-009: the role's own completion record in progress.md — the heading\n * report shape or the `CKPT <n>m converging=yes` self-assessment line the\n * checkpoint steer asks for (`[machine]` lines are framework-written and do\n * not count). */\nconst PROGRESS_DONE_RE = /(^|\\n)(?:##\\s*完成记录|CKPT\\s+\\d+m\\s+(?!\\[machine\\])(?=[^\\n]*converging=yes))/;\n\n/** Bounded read-only scan of the key's `evidence/` tree (depth ≤5, ≤500\n * entries, symlinks skipped) for a file fresher than the run start — the\n * writeless deliverable channel lives outside taskDir. Returns the newest\n * qualifying mtime, or undefined. */\nfunction newestEvidenceMtimeMs(keyDir: string, startedAtMs: number, nowMs: number): number | undefined {\n\tconst maxDepth = 5;\n\tconst maxEntries = 500;\n\tlet visited = 0;\n\tlet newest: number | undefined;\n\tconst walk = (dir: string, depth: number): void => {\n\t\tif (depth > maxDepth || visited >= maxEntries) return;\n\t\tlet entries: fs.Dirent[];\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tentries = fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true });\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor (const entry of entries) {\n\t\t\tif (visited >= maxEntries) return;\n\t\t\tvisited++;\n\t\t\tconst abs = path.join(dir, entry.name);\n\t\t\tif (entry.isSymbolicLink()) continue;\n\t\t\tif (entry.isDirectory()) {\n\t\t\t\twalk(abs, depth + 1);\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif (!entry.isFile()) continue;\n\t\t\ttry {\n\t\t\t\tconst stat = fs.statSync(abs);\n\t\t\t\tif (stat.size === 0 || stat.mtimeMs < startedAtMs) continue;\n\t\t\t\t// T-12: a mtime past `nowMs` only means \"just landed\" (clock\n\t\t\t\t// granularity / write-read race). Clamp it to `nowMs` (age 0)\n\t\t\t\t// instead of dropping a real landing.\n\t\t\t\tconst mtimeMs = stat.mtimeMs > nowMs ? nowMs : stat.mtimeMs;\n\t\t\t\tif (newest === undefined || mtimeMs > newest) newest = mtimeMs;\n\t\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t\t// Best-effort: an unreadable entry is not a landing.\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\twalk(path.join(keyDir, \"evidence\"), 0);\n\treturn newest;\n}\n\n/** T-04/AC-009: landing signals for a writeless run, from the SAME ledger the\n * settle judgement reads. `parseWriteFileEvents` (not the `[TOOL] worker_file`\n * lines, not a second extractor) supplies the target set, so the two views\n * cannot diverge; disk truth (non-empty artifact, surviving targets, fresh\n * evidence) is the fallback when the ledger missed an event. Read-only. */\nexport function collectLandingSignals(opts: {\n\ttaskDir: string;\n\ttraceText: string;\n\tprogressText: string;\n\tstartedAtMs: number;\n\tnowMs: number;\n}): LandingSignals {\n\tconst targets = parseWriteFileEvents(opts.traceText);\n\tlet newestMtimeMs: number | undefined;\n\tconst touch = (mtimeMs: number): void => {\n\t\tif (newestMtimeMs === undefined || mtimeMs > newestMtimeMs) newestMtimeMs = mtimeMs;\n\t};\n\tlet nonProgressLanded = false;\n\tfor (const target of targets) {\n\t\tconst abs = path.isAbsolute(target) ? target : path.resolve(process.cwd(), target);\n\t\ttry {\n\t\t\tconst stat = fs.statSync(abs);\n\t\t\tif (!stat.isFile() || stat.size === 0) continue;\n\t\t\t// T-12: clamp a future mtime to `nowMs` (age 0) rather than\n\t\t\t// skipping it — it is a landing, not a stale artifact.\n\t\t\ttouch(stat.mtimeMs > opts.nowMs ? opts.nowMs : stat.mtimeMs);\n\t\t\tif (path.basename(abs) !== \"progress.md\") nonProgressLanded = true;\n\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t// Not on disk — recorded but not a surviving landing.\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tconst keyDir = path.dirname(path.dirname(opts.taskDir));\n\tconst evidenceMtimeMs = newestEvidenceMtimeMs(keyDir, opts.startedAtMs, opts.nowMs);\n\tif (evidenceMtimeMs !== undefined) touch(evidenceMtimeMs);\n\treturn {\n\t\tlanded: targets.length,\n\t\tlastLandingAgeMs: newestMtimeMs === undefined ? undefined : Math.max(0, opts.nowMs - newestMtimeMs),\n\t\tartifactPresent:\n\t\t\tfindNonEmptyReport(opts.taskDir) !== undefined || nonProgressLanded || evidenceMtimeMs !== undefined,\n\t\tprogressDone: PROGRESS_DONE_RE.test(opts.progressText),\n\t};\n}\n\n// ── Task file parsing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\ninterface TaskMeta {\n\ttype: string;\n\t/** task.md `phase:` header (the phase axis of `required = role.require OR\n\t * phase.require`, T-14). Distinct from the `phases` framework array below. */\n\tphase?: string;\n\tphases?: TaskPhase[];\n\ttaskKey: string;\n\tagenticdocRoot: string;\n\t/** Dispatch origin marker (D-104): \"conductor\" on autopilot dispatches,\n\t * undefined on manual/legacy tasks (which keep the fallback path, GC-8). */\n\torigin?: string;\n\t/** task.md `images:` header (T-09/AC-011): `true` only when the dispatch\n\t * declared `images: yes` (the task needs image reads). An undeclared header\n\t * stays `undefined` and changes nothing (zero branches). */\n\timages?: boolean;\n\t/** TRUE .agenticdoc root — task.md four levels up\n\t * (.agenticdoc/{owner}/workers/{taskKey}/task.md → .agenticdoc), where\n\t * goal.md lives (D-116). Distinct from `agenticdocRoot`, which is the\n\t * owner's workers/ dir and stays the outputDir base (contract unchanged). */\n\ttrueAgenticdocRoot: string;\n\t/** Wall budget in minutes from the task.md `timeout:` header. */\n\ttimeoutMin?: number;\n\t/** read_scope entries (D-106), project-root relative. Present → read\n\t * containment enabled; absent → zero interception (AC-012 red line). */\n\treadScope?: string[];\n\t/** deny_globs entries (mw-dual-workspace AC-006), minimatch dual-basis.\n\t * Present → deny firewall active even without read_scope (deny-only). */\n\tdenyGlobs?: string[];\n\t/** write_scope entries (contract C1/T-03), project-root relative. The TRUE .agenticdoc root (goal.md's parent) is four levels\n\t// up from task.md (D-116 semantic split).\n\tconst agenticdocRoot = path.dirname(path.dirname(taskPath));\n\tconst taskKey = path.basename(path.dirname(taskPath));\n\tconst trueAgenticdocRoot = path.dirname(path.dirname(agenticdocRoot));\n\n\t// D-115 carrier convergence: parse the authoritative `write_face:` head with\n\t// the shared operator (D-009/AC-007) so the runtime allow face cannot drift\n\t// from the dispatch-time overlap operator. claimsBlock.claims : undefined,\n\t};\n}\n\n// ── claims settlement (T-04b / design §3.3, AC-008) ───────────────────────\n\n/** Share of `unverified` rows above which the run did not settle its claim\n * contract (AC-008 ②). `>` — the boundary itself passes. */\nexport const CLAIM_UNVERIFIED_MAX_DEFAULT = 0.4;\n\n/** ... except for the review role, which legitimately hits the no-bash wall\n * (RQ-3 §4 B-2: all 46 corpus review units only carry read/find/grep/ls). */\nexport const CLAIM_UNVERIFIED_MAX_REVIEW = 0.6;\n\n/** The `carried-from: <path:line>` audit marker of a re-used verdict (RQ-3 §4\n * B-7: \"code really did not change\" is legal, but only when written down). */\nconst CARRIED_FROM_RE = /carried-from\\s*:\\s*\\S+/i;\n\n/** One `run.json` `claims` subobject (design §3.4). `total` is the card's claim\n * count; the three verdict counters are the rows that settled against it; and\n * `tokens: null` is the contract's \"not attributable\" value (AC-005b: the\n * worker process cannot split LLM usage per claim — the Python side joins the\n * session ledger, and a made-up number would corrupt `tokens_per_closed_claim`).\n * T-05's `readRunClaims` reads exactly these six keys (absent key = no claims). */\nexport interface ClaimCounts {\n\ttotal: number;\n\tclosed: number;\n\tpartial: number;\n\tunverified: number;\n\t/** `[FLOW] tool_call` read-class count (D-008: only allowed calls). */\n\tfetches: number;\n\ttokens: number | null;\n}\n\n/** `裁决` cell folded to its token form (ticks/whitespace/case), mirroring the\n * L3 parser's own comparison so the counters cannot disagree with the verdict. */\nfunction claimVerdictToken(cell: string): string {\n\treturn cell.replace(/`/g, \"\").replace(/\\s+/g, \"\").toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/** Per-run claim counters: the card's claim set against the product's `## 断言裁决`\n * table (first row per id wins, same as `claimCoverage`). A claims-free run has\n * no counters to write at all — the caller guards on `meta.claims === undefined`\n * rather than fabricating zeroes (T-05: an absent key means \"not measured\"). */\nexport function claimCounts(claims: Claim[], table: VerdictTable, fetches: number): ClaimCounts {\n\tconst counts: ClaimCounts = {\n\t\ttotal: claims.length,\n\t\tclosed: 0,\n\t\tpartial: 0,\n\t\tunverified: 0,\n\t\tfetches,\n\t\ttokens: null,\n\t};\n\tconst declared = new Set(claims.map((claim) => claim.id));\n\tconst seen = new Set<string>();\n\tfor (const row of table.rows) {\n\t\tif (!declared.has(row.id) || seen.has(row.id)) continue;\n\t\tseen.add(row.id);\n\t\tconst verdict = claimVerdictToken(row.verdict);\n\t\tif (verdict === \"closed\") counts.closed += 1;\n\t\telse if (verdict === \"partial\") counts.partial += 1;\n\t\telse if (verdict === \"unverified\") counts.unverified += 1;\n\t}\n\treturn counts;\n}\n\n/** The `[CLAIMS]` trace row (design D-004): a line of its own, NEVER folded into\n * `[END]` — both sides of `[END]` are anchored regexes (`shared/heartbeat.ts`,\n * `packages/multi-workers/mw_common.py`). Field order is frozen here and by\n * `usage.py::_CLAIMS_LINE_RE` (T-05). */\nexport function formatClaimsTraceLine(counts: ClaimCounts, now: Date = new Date()): string {\n\treturn (\n\t\t`[CLAIMS] ${now.toISOString()} claims=${counts.total} closed=${counts.closed} ` +\n\t\t`partial=${counts.partial} unverified=${counts.unverified} fetches=${counts.fetches}`\n\t);\n}\n\n/** Append the `[CLAIMS]` row once, lifecycle style (no `[FLOW]` prefix — the line\n * starts with its own anchor). Best-effort like every other trace anchor: a\n * diagnostic append must never change the terminal verdict. */\nexport function appendClaimsTraceLine(taskKey: string, agenticdocRoot: string, counts: ClaimCounts): void {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst dir = path.resolve(agenticdocRoot, taskKey);\n\t\tfs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });\n\t\tfs.appendFileSync(path.join(dir, \"trace.log\"), `${formatClaimsTraceLine(counts)}\\n`, \"utf8\");\n\t} catch {\n\t\t// Diagnostic append — trace.log and run.json carry the rest\n\t}\n}\n\n/** The claim ids named by a gap list (`claim:<id>:<criterion>`), de-duplicated in\n * emission order. This\n * is a deliberately narrow reader (the full grammar lives in `output-sections.ts`,\n * which is frozen for T-04b): only the `path[:line[-line]]` half is needed to ask\n * \"was this citation produced by an EARLIER round?\" — command refs and\n * unparsable refs are ignored, they are owned by the `:evidence` criterion. */\nfunction claimEvidencePaths(cell: string): string[] {\n\tconst paths: string[] = [];\n\tfor (const raw of cell.replace(/`/g, \"\").split(\";\")) {\n\t\tconst ref = raw\n\t\t\t.trim()\n\t\t\t.replace(/「[^」]*」\\s*$/, \"\")\n\t\t\t.trim();\n\t\tif (ref === \"\" || (file === \"\" || file.startsWith(\"/\") || /^[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]/.test(file) || file.startsWith(\"./\")) continue;\n\t\tif (file.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\")) continue;\n\t\tpaths.push(file);\n\t}\n\treturn paths;\n}\n\n/**\n * The three AC-008 settlement criteria that need inputs only the worker layer\n * holds (the role, the run clock, the trace read                         cannot honestly report more\n *                                                fetches than you performed).\n *   ⑥ `claim:<id>:carried-from`                 a closed/partial === 0` (no contract) returns `[]`, and an unknown\n * `taskMtimeMs` skips ⑥ rather than guessing a clock.\n */\nexport function claimSettlementGaps(opts: {\n\tclaims: Claim[];\n\ttable: VerdictTable;\n\t/** Task type whose role sets the ② threshold (`roleForTaskType`). */\n\trole: string;\n\t/** `[FLOW] tool_call` read-class count of this run (D-008). */\n\ttraceReads: number;\n\t/** mtime of this run's task.md — the clock a \"fresh\" citation must beat. */\n\ttaskMtimeMs?: number;\n\t/** Root the evidence paths resolve against (launcher cwd in production). */\n\tprojectDir?: VerdictTable[\"rows\"] = [];\n\tconst seen = new Set<string>();\n\tfor (const row of opts.table.rows) {\n\t\tif (!declared.has(row.id) || seen.has(row.id)) continue;\n\t\tseen.add(row.id);\n\t\trows.push(row);\n\t}\n\n\t// ② unverified share (integer permille so the boundary is exact: `>` not `>=`).\n\tconst limitPermille = Math.round(\n\t\topts.role === CLAIM_UNVERIFIED_MAX_REVIEW * 1000 : CLAIM_UNVERIFIED_MAX_DEFAULT * 1000,\n\t);\n\tconst unverified = rows.filter((row) => claimVerdictToken(row.verdict) === \"unverified\").length;\n\tif (opts.claims.length > 0 && unverified * 1000 > opts.claims.length * limitPermille) {\n\t\tgaps.push(`claims:unverified-ratio:${unverified}/${opts.claims.length}>${limitPermille / 10}%`);\n\t}\n\n\t// ③ Σ取数 against the derived cap and the trace's own read count.\n\tlet fetchSum = 0;\n\tfor (const row of rows) {\n\t\tconst fetches = Number(row.fetches.replace(/`/g, \"\").trim());\n\t\tif (Number.isInteger(fetches) && fetches >= 0) fetchSum += fetches;\n\t}\n\tconst { fileCap } = claimBudgetCaps(opts.claims);\n\tif (fetchSum > fileCap) gaps.push(`claims:fetches:${fetchSum}>${fileCap}`);\n\tif (fetchSum > opts.traceReads) gaps.push(`claims:fetches:${fetchSum}>trace:${opts.traceReads}`);\n\n\t// ⑥ carried-from: a re-used previous-round verdict must say so.\n\tconst projectDir = opts.projectDir ?? command.length : closeAt + close.length;\n\t\t\thasWord = true;\n\t\t\tword += command.slice(i, end);\n\t\t\ti = end;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (ch === \" \" || ch === \"\\t\") {\n\t\t\tflush();\n\t\t\ti++;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (ch === \"\\n\") {\n\t\t\tflush();\n\t\t\ttokens.push(markLineBreak({ text: \";\", operator: true, verbatim: true }));\n\t\t\ti++;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (ch === \">\" || ch === \"<\" || ch === \"|\" || ch === \";\" || ch === \"&\" || ch === \"(\" || ch === \")\") {\n\t\t\tflush();\n\t\t\tlet op = ch;\n\t\t\twhile (i + 1 < command.length && (command[i + 1] === ch || (command[i + 1] === \"-\" && op === \"<<\"))) {\n\t\t\t\top += command[i + 1]; // `ch` repeats, but `<<-` absorbs its `-`\n\t\t\t\ti++;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\ttokens.push({ text: op, operator: true, verbatim: true });\n\t\t\ti++;\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\thasWord = true;\n\t\tappend(ch, true);\n\t\ti++;\n\t}\n\tflush();\n\treturn tokens;\n}\n\n/** Wrapper commands whose following word is still a command position.\n * Byte-frozen: expanded (never replaced) by `COMMAND_WRAPPERS` below. */\nconst SHELL_WRAPPER_COMMANDS = new Set([\"sudo\", \"env\", \"command\", \"nohup\", \"time\", \"nice\", \"stdbuf\", \"xargs\"]);\n\n/** Command-position wrappers: skip their known flags, the next word is the command. */\nconst COMMAND_WRAPPERS = new Set([...SHELL_WRAPPER_COMMANDS, \"doas\", \"timeout\", \"setsid\"]);\n/** Wrappers whose payload is shell source (re-tokenized and scanned again). */\nconst SHELL_SCRIPT_WRAPPERS = new Set([\"bash\", \"sh\", \"zsh\", \"dash\", \"ksh\"]);\nconst CMD_SCRIPT_WRAPPERS = new Set([\"cmd\"]);\nconst PS_SCRIPT_WRAPPERS = new Set([\"powershell\", \"pwsh\"]);\n/** Unwrap recursion budget; a deeper payload is left undecided (fails open). */\nconst MAX_UNWRAP_DEPTH = 3;\n\n/** Wrapper flags that consume one value.
